only account of why the stage failed. A failed stage whose detail is empty takes the setup's final sentence as the error's
"{detail}" ("A step failed, so the workspace is only partly set up."), as `resultOf` already did for a failed setup with no
failed step; that sentence is the run host's (REQ-MCP-112's final outcome). The output's tail is cut where a UTF-8
character begins, so a cut never splits one (`lastUtf8Bytes`), and it is the captured output trimmed of its leading and
trailing blank space.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an empty detail is what REQ-WORKSPACE-092 means for these steps or each has a sentence
of the specification's own; whether a step that could not be started reads in the launch's error, in a fixed sentence, or
empty; and what a failed stage's "{reason}: {detail}" reads when its detail is empty — the build's reading borrows the
run host's final sentence there, REQ-MCP-112's words in this domain's error, the same crossing of categories the repair
removed from every other detail. It also decides whether "the last 400 bytes of its combined standard output and standard
error" are counted on the output as written or, as built, on the output trimmed of its leading and trailing blank space:
the two differ for output that ends in blank lines, and for a tail whose first characters are blank.

**OQ-176 — Does REQ-SHELL-166's 100 ms echo hold on a host whose CPUs other processes oversubscribe?** *(REQ-SHELL-166,
echo latency "within the 100 ms gesture budget of REQ-SHELL-150, measured from the key press to the frame that shows it";
REQ-SHELL-150, whose "sustained load" is a burst of changes in the shell, "a build that misses any of the three under
sustained load fails this requirement". Raised 2026-10-01 while repairing (measured that day; first committed 2026-10-02)
[`terminal-proofs-input-checks-fail-at-random-on-a-heavily-loaded-host.md`](../defects/fixed/terminal-proofs-input-checks-fail-at-random-on-a-heavily-loaded-host.md)
under R-062. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the specification is amended: REQ-SHELL-166's 100 ms echo applies on a machine whose CPUs other programs do not oversubscribe, a load average at or below the CPU count; a red taken above it is run again with the host quiet, and a red on a quiet host is the product's. The bound itself is not relaxed. [`PD-SHELL-007`](../product/directives.md#pd-shell-007) narrows REQ-SHELL-166.

`pnpm terminal-proof`'s `live.echoUnder100ms` was run 120 times on 2026-10-01, with busy loops pinned beside the proof on
one or two of the host's four CPUs and another plan's agents on the host. It went red in 10 runs, at load averages 9.1 to
13.6. Each time one keystroke of three missed the bound (100 to 144 ms), and the other two passed at 18 to 93 ms. The time
went into the run host's frame (key to frame up to 130 ms) or into waiting for the frame to paint. Where it was recorded,
the key had waited in the renderer's queue for at most 11 ms. With no busy loops beside it, the same probe read key to
paint at 20 to 30 ms. The requirement's load is the shell's own (a burst of changes), and REQ-SHELL-166 states no host
condition; neither says whether the bound applies when other processes keep the CPUs busier than the product can be.

**What the build proceeds under.** The bound is kept as stated and is not relaxed for load. The proof records the host's
load average and CPU count beside the reading (`results.live.echoLoad`) and how long the key waited in the renderer's queue
(`queuedMs`). Since 2026-10-02 the reading starts at the key event's own time stamp, so that wait is inside the bound
(`from: 'event'`); until then it started when the page's listener ran and the wait was recorded beside it. A red taken at a load average above the CPU count is run again alone, as the host's own rule says
(`.agents/skills/orchestrated-build/references/environment.md`, "Load"). A red alone is the product's.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the 100 ms applies on any host the product runs on, whatever else that host runs;
or on a host whose CPUs are not oversubscribed, so a red under a load above the CPU count is evidence about the host; or
on a stated reference host and load.

**OQ-177 — Does a user's switch of the entry model onto the model the run was configured with end a move the ladder made?**
*(REQ-MONITOR-142, "A switch of the run's entry model … applies from the next iteration onward"; REQ-ORCH-090, the role's
fallback "tried once per child by rebuilding the agent and transparently re-running"; REQ-ORCH-091 (b), "at most one
same-tier automatic model fallback per child", and (d), a manual model change "persists the override in session state for
the rest of the session"; REQ-MONITOR-194, a pair chosen explicitly is "eligible again". Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`an-entry-model-switch-row-says-it-applies-while-a-ladder-move-keeps-the-root.md`](../defects/fixed/an-entry-model-switch-row-says-it-applies-while-a-ladder-move-keeps-the-root.md),
as OQ-176, and renumbered OQ-177 at its merge because `origin/main` had taken OQ-176 meanwhile. Open until 2026-10-06; ruled that day by the owner, and built.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** every explicit switch wins — a switch of the
entry model from the run header or the inspector ends an automatic fallback, as built, and also takes back any earlier
quota-wait override of the chosen pair, as the quota-wait surface already does, so the entry agent runs on the pair chosen
from the next iteration; an agent that had already followed the override stays where it moved. Minted as
[`PD-ORCH-013`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-013), narrowing REQ-ORCH-091 (d) and REQ-NOTIFY-089, and built the same
day (`Run.setEntryModel` calls `takeBackOverrideOf` on the header path; plan fin21). The reading below is kept as the build
proceeded under it until then.

After the ladder moves the entry agent off its configured model — to the role's fallback when the model is unresponsive
(REQ-ORCH-090), or to a same-tier model on another provider after a rate-limit or quota response (REQ-ORCH-091 b) — the
user can switch the entry model to the configured key from the run header or the inspector. The specification says a
switch applies from the next iteration and says nothing of a switch that names the model the run already asked for, which
only the ladder's move makes a change. Read as a switch, it ends the move: the user chose that model. Read as no change,
the move stands, since nothing the user asked for differs from what the run was asked to use. The same question arises
for a switch onto a pair a change-model resolution moved during an earlier wait (REQ-ORCH-091 d), whose override the
requirement keeps "for the rest of the session", and REQ-MONITOR-194, which lets an explicit choice of an excluded pair
make it eligible again, bears on it without settling it.

**What the build proceeds under** (`packages/engine/src/run/run.ts`, `rootResilience`, `setEntryModel`,
`setEntryReasoning`; `ResilienceMemory.overrideReaching`): a switch is the user's choice and applies. From the next
iteration the root's cell is rebuilt on the chosen model, ending a REQ-ORCH-090 or REQ-ORCH-091 b move, whether or not the
key names the model already requested; the cell's once-per-agent budgets (the one unresponsive fallback, the one same-tier
fallback, the pairs already attempted) carry over, so the ladder does not move the agent automatically more often than the
requirements allow. A reasoning switch is not a model switch: the move stands and the level changes on the model the cell
has. A change-model resolution's override (REQ-ORCH-091 d) is left standing for the rest of the session, as the
requirement says, so a switch onto the pair it moved runs on the override's model, and the row says so in place of "it
applies from the next iteration": "Entry model switched to X, but Y, chosen for P/M during an earlier wait, stands for the
rest of the session: the entry agent runs on Y from the next iteration." The iteration in flight finishes on the setting
it had: the root's ladder is read once per root turn, so a root resumed after its children in the same iteration is not
moved by a switch made meanwhile. The exclusion of an exhausted pair is not touched by a switch (whether an explicit choice
clears it is REQ-MONITOR-194's, recorded in
[`an-explicit-choice-of-an-exhausted-pair-does-not-clear-its-exclusion.md`](../defects/fixed/an-explicit-choice-of-an-exhausted-pair-does-not-clear-its-exclusion.md); *since 2026-10-02 an explicit choice clears it, on a switch and in a quota wait, where the waiting pair itself may be chosen*).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a switch onto the configured key ends a ladder move (as built) or leaves it in force —
and, if it leaves it, what the row says; whether a later switch onto a pair an override moved supersedes that override for
the entry agent, or the override stands (as built) and only the row says so. REQ-MONITOR-194's clearing is in force beside
it since 2026-10-02, which sharpens the second half: a pair a quota wait moved is both excluded and overridden, and a later
switch onto it clears the exclusion while the override, as built, still sends the entry agent elsewhere — so the pair the
user explicitly chose is not what runs, and only the row says so. The wait path is read the other way, and the two
readings stand side by side: a choice made on a wait surface (REQ-MONITOR-303's "change model now … resolves the wait as a
retry on the chosen model") takes back any override an earlier choice set from the pair chosen, so the agent resumes on it
as the wait's row says (`Run.takeBackOverrideOf`, since 2026-10-02, the third round of
[`a-childs-wait-choice-leaves-the-root-calling-the-pair-it-replaced.md`](../defects/fixed/a-childs-wait-choice-leaves-the-root-calling-the-pair-it-replaced.md));
a ruling that a switch also supersedes the override would make the header and inspector path match it.

**OQ-178 — Which notice offers REQ-NOTIFY-045's retry, when a notice carries one action?** *(REQ-NOTIFY-044, whose
vocabulary includes "retry the failed run under REQ-NOTIFY-045"; REQ-NOTIFY-045; REQ-NOTIFY-030; REQ-NOTIFY-066;
REQ-SHELL-114, a notice's "optional action (label plus action identifier)"; REQ-NOTIFY-061, "offers no retry";
REQ-NOTIFY-062, "an action opening the cloud account surface"; REQ-NOTIFY-063, "offering another model or a retry once the
provider resets … and offering an action opening model settings"; REQ-NOTIFY-064, "an action returning to the workspace
view". Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`the-retry-run-notice-action-has-no-target.md`](../defects/fixed/the-retry-run-notice-action-has-no-target.md),
as OQ-177, and renumbered OQ-178 at its merge because `origin/main` had taken OQ-176 meanwhile and this branch's OQ-176
became OQ-177. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** kept as built: no run-failure notice carries a Retry action, each class keeping the action its requirement names and REQ-NOTIFY-063's retry staying in its message, and the composer keeps the draft, so the user resends it with one press of Send. The `retry-run` action keeps its target for a notice that carries it. No requirement names a notice that carries the retry, so this ruling settles it.

REQ-NOTIFY-045 says what a retry does and REQ-NOTIFY-044 lists it among a notice's actions, and REQ-NOTIFY-061 takes the
trouble to say its notice offers none, which reads as though another failure notice does. But every failure class names
its notice's action, and none names the retry: REQ-NOTIFY-062's opens the cloud account, REQ-NOTIFY-063's opens model
settings, REQ-NOTIFY-064's and REQ-NOTIFY-061's return to the workspace view; REQ-SHELL-114 gives a notice one action.
REQ-NOTIFY-063 "offers" a retry in words beside its action, and it is the only failure notice that mentions one. The
specification also says nothing of the composer after the draft has been resubmitted from a notice.

**What the build proceeds under** (`apps/desktop/src/renderer/session-actions.ts`, `retryRun`;
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/main.tsx`, `dispatchNoticeAction`): the action has its target, and no run-failure notice
carries it — each class keeps the action its requirement names, and REQ-NOTIFY-063's retry stays in its message ("Choose
another model, or retry once the provider resets."). Activated, the action resubmits the composer's draft as the window
last published it (REQ-CHAT-014), else as stored (REQ-NOTIFY-066), else — the draft blank — the focused session's newest
`user` row, the prompt the engine's own continue reads as the last one; it goes through the composer's submit path to
the session the window follows (REQ-NOTIFY-030), and is refused, with the reason in a warning notice, when no session
is followed or there is nothing to resubmit. The composer keeps the draft: nothing outside the composer clears it. *Since
2026-10-02 (fin8, the repair of
[`the-retry-action-reads-the-last-prompt-from-the-resident-window.md`](../defects/fixed/the-retry-action-reads-the-last-prompt-from-the-resident-window.md)
and
[`the-retry-action-resubmits-a-prompt-without-its-images.md`](../defects/fixed/the-retry-action-resubmits-a-prompt-without-its-images.md)):*
the blank-draft branch is the engine's (`session.retry`, `Sessions.retry`). It reads the last submitted prompt over every
row, released ones included, where the window had searched its replica's resident window and refused once the prompt was
released; and it resubmits the prompt's images with it, read back from the session's directory and verified by digest,
where the window had re-sent the text alone. A missing or altered image refuses the retry, naming the image. A non-blank
draft is still resubmitted as its text (OQ-183).

**What a ruling decides.** Which notice carries the retry — REQ-NOTIFY-063's in place of, or beside, its model-settings
action (which REQ-SHELL-114's single action would then have to allow), REQ-NOTIFY-064's, or none — and whether a draft a
retry resubmitted is cleared from the composer as a submitted one is.

**OQ-179 — What does the recovery dialog's re-authenticate path offer for a provider whose key the model configuration
carries?** *(REQ-NOTIFY-076, "For key-based providers it offers a masked key field with a save-and-retry control … For
browser and device-code providers it starts that provider's own flow in place"; REQ-NOTIFY-077; REQ-NOTIFY-202;
REQ-CONFIG-083 and REQ-PROVIDER-092, a model's `api_key` / `api_key_env`, read per request, when it names no
`auth_provider`; REQ-PROVIDER-118/140, "Authentication is managed by model configuration." for a provider that resolves to
no sign-in method. Raised 2026-10-02 by the 401 note's part D on `fin6-auth-recovery-2`. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the build is accepted: for a provider whose key the model configuration carries (`api_key` or `api_key_env` with no `auth_provider`), the recovery dialog's second path shows REQ-PROVIDER-118/140's sentence and says to correct the key the model configuration names, then retry, with no key field and no save-and-retry control. Such a provider resolves to no sign-in method and is neither of REQ-NOTIFY-076's two kinds, so this ruling settles it.

REQ-NOTIFY-076 sorts the provider that failed into two kinds: key-based, re-authenticated through a key field, and
browser or device-code, through their own flow. A model can also reach a provider with a key it states itself — `api_key`
or `api_key_env` in `agents.yaml`, with no `auth_provider` — and then no provider record or credential-store entry exists
for it: a key typed into the dialog and stored would never be read by that model, so "save and retry" would retry with the
same credentials, which REQ-NOTIFY-068 forbids. The scripted test provider is one such provider. The specification does not
say what the dialog's second path offers for it.

**What the build proceeds under** (`ProviderService.reauthentication` in `packages/providers/src/signin.ts`;
`AuthRecoveryDialog.tsx`): a provider id that resolves to no sign-in method reads `configuration`, and the dialog's second
path shows REQ-PROVIDER-118/140's sentence and says to correct the key the model configuration names, then retry — no key
field, no save-and-retry control, and nothing directing the user to a shell or a terminal. The first path (another model) is
unaffected. Device-code and browser providers read `unavailable` and say their flow is not provided by this build (the flows
are owed, `packages/providers/src/catalogue.ts`); that is a gap of the build, not of the specification, and is recorded on
[the 401 note](../defects/fixed/a-401-ends-the-run-with-a-bare-failure-notice-and-no-authentication-recovery.md).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether such a provider is offered a key field at all — writing the key into the configuration
the model reads (a write into the user's project files, which REQ-NOTIFY-047 keeps out of notice actions but not out of a
dialog), or into the credential store with the model then pointed at it — or only the sentence this build shows.

**OQ-180 — Where does a board run that stops at its iteration limit rest, and does automatic scheduling start it again?**
*(REQ-TRACE-477, a flow's ending delivered to the surface told it began; REQ-TRACE-482, "the system itself picks up the
next candidate as capacity becomes available"; REQ-TRACE-463; REQ-TRACE-476, "without re-running completed units".
Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`a-rejected-card-back-in-ready-can-never-start-its-next-unit.md`](../defects/fixed/a-rejected-card-back-in-ready-can-never-start-its-next-unit.md),
bundle `fin9-queue-dispatch-and-disclosure`, as OQ-179, and renumbered OQ-180 when the bundle merged `origin/main`,
which had taken OQ-179 meanwhile. Open until 2026-10-06; ruled that day by the owner, and built.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** an iteration-limit stop is a failure — the
card moves to Blocked with a `run-failure` blocker, as a user's stop already does, so a person decides when to resume it
(the blocker's resume provisions the next unit), and automatic scheduling never restarts it on its own. Read, where the
ruling leaves it open, as covering every run that persists `stopped` — REQ-MONITOR-029's `max_iterations`, which a time
limit (REQ-ORCH-069) reaches as well, the coordinator reading the persisted status alone — while an explicit cancel
(`cancelling`) still rests the card in Ready. The requirements were silent on this ending, so the ruling alone settles it.
Built the same day (`outcomeOf`, `apps/desktop/src/main/requirements-runs.ts`; plan fin21). The reading below is kept as
the build proceeded under it until then.

A board run that reaches its iteration limit persists `stopped`; main's coordinator classifies `stopped` and `cancelling`
as `cancelled` (`outcomeOf`, `apps/desktop/src/main/requirements-runs.ts`), and a `cancelled` ending rests the card in
`ready` (`recordRunEnded`, `packages/workspace/src/delivery/transition.ts`). The specification classifies a board run's
ending as completed (review) or not, and says a run-time block returns to the released state; it names no state for a
run that ended neither completed nor failed, and nothing bounds how often automatic scheduling may pick the same card up.

**What the build proceeds under**: as built — the card rests in `ready` on its next unit, and under `automatic` the
dispatch that follows every run's end starts that unit at once on a fresh worktree (the repair above), the finished
unit's tree kept; under `manual` it waits for the queue's release. So a requirement whose runs keep reaching the limit is
re-run, one unit after another, until a person holds it or the queue is stopped.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an iteration-limited run ends `cancelled` into `ready`, or `failed` into `blocked` with
a `run-failure` blocker (whose resume provisions the next unit), as a stop by the user has since R-067; and, if it rests
in `ready`, whether automatic scheduling may pick it up again without bound.

**OQ-181 — Where does REQ-NOTIFY-071's prompt stand "beside the continuing run", and is it drawn while the window shows
another view?** *(REQ-NOTIFY-071, "a successful fallback restart opens a non-modal re-authentication prompt beside the
continuing run"; ADR-0048's non-modal window-level level, "an in-window panel that does not trap focus and leaves the rest
navigable"; REQ-SHELL-022's minimum; REQ-CHAT-010's 180 px transcript floor; REQ-NOTIFY-030. Raised 2026-10-02 by the
401 note's part B, second repair round,
[`a-401-ends-the-run-with-a-bare-failure-notice-and-no-authentication-recovery.md`](../defects/fixed/a-401-ends-the-run-with-a-bare-failure-notice-and-no-authentication-recovery.md),
as OQ-180, and renumbered OQ-181 at the branch's merge beside the note's parts C and D (2026-10-02) because `origin/main` had
taken OQ-179 meanwhile and the branch's own OQ-179 took OQ-180 (since renumbered OQ-182, at the branch's third merge,
because `origin/main` had taken OQ-180). ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the build's placement and visibility are accepted as they are: the prompt is drawn in flow in the Workspace view, between the run header and the transcript, yields to an expanded plan gate as a bar of its title and its answers, and is not drawn while another view is shown, the window holding it by session and drawing it again when the Workspace view returns. "Beside the continuing run" is the Workspace view's run column.

The requirement places the prompt by the run, not by the window, and the level ADR-0048 gives it requires the rest of the
window to stay navigable while it is open — and it stays open until it is answered. Two overlay placements were built
and both covered controls in the built app: `fixed` at the window's top corner (the title bar's Sessions, minimise,
maximise, close and the notice's dismissal), then `absolute` at the top corner of the rail-and-view region (at the
1000x680 minimum the run header's model and reasoning switches and Compress context; with a key field, the composer's
submit; in the other views each one's top-right controls). Any overlay that stays open covers something at some size.
The specification does not say which region "beside the continuing run" is, nor whether the prompt is drawn while the
window shows a view other than the one the run is shown in.

**What the build proceeds under** (`WorkspaceView`'s `reauthPrompt` row, `packages/ui/src/shell.css`):
- the prompt is drawn **in flow in the Workspace view**, the view that shows the run, as its own row of the view's grid
  between the run header and the transcript (the plan gate's kind of place, REQ-SHELL-168). It overlays nothing at any
  window size: the transcript keeps REQ-CHAT-010's floor and the prompt takes what is left, scrolling when that is less
  than it needs with its answers pinned to its floor ~~— at every size~~ (*corrected 2026-10-02, the third repair round*:
  beside an EXPANDED plan gate the transcript is not drawn and the gate's row has no floor, and the prompt, sized first,
  left the gate 42 px with its three answers unreachable at 1000x680. There the prompt **yields to the gate** as the
  transcript does, one action away: it is drawn as a bar — its title and its answers on one row — and its sentence, the
  provider's words and the key's hint are drawn again when the gate is collapsed or answered; the gate, the run's stop
  and the reading area (REQ-ORCH-153, PD-ORCH-002 revision 2), takes the rest. A ruling may also decide whether REQ-NOTIFY-071's
  quote may be withheld from view that way while a plan awaits a decision);
- it is **not drawn while another view is shown**. The window keeps holding it (by session, REQ-NOTIFY-030) and draws it
  again when the Workspace view returns; the run's acknowledgement (REQ-NOTIFY-070) is the window-wide signal, shown in
  any view. A key half-typed into the field is not kept across a view change.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether "beside the continuing run" means the Workspace view's run column (as built), a region
of the window shown in every view (which then has to take space from every view at REQ-SHELL-022's minimum), or a
separate window; and whether a prompt the user has not answered should be reachable from the other views. *Added at the
fourth repair round (2026-10-02, the verifier's optional findings):* in the bar beside an expanded plan gate the only words
drawn are its title, "Re-authenticate <provider>", and its answers — so while a plan awaits a decision the bar names
neither the primary model that failed nor that the run continues on the fallback (REQ-NOTIFY-071's two statements), and
for a provider re-authenticated elsewhere — a device-code or browser provider, whose method this build does not provide,
or one whose key the model configuration carries — it does not say that the method is unavailable here: those sentences,
with the provider's quoted error, are in the document and drawn again when the gate is collapsed or answered. A ruling
may decide whether any of them must stay drawn in the bar (each one taken from the height the plan, the largest part of
the gate under PD-ORCH-002, keeps at REQ-SHELL-022's minimum).

**OQ-182 — What is REQ-NOTIFY-070's restart "with the same prompt", what does "the fallback bookkeeping is cleared" take back,
and how long does "the first authentication failure of a session" last?** *(REQ-NOTIFY-070, "the run restarts with the
same prompt. Where the restart cannot begin, the fallback bookkeeping is cleared and the generic failure notice is
published instead"; REQ-NOTIFY-069, "a recorded last prompt"; REQ-NOTIFY-045, whose retry "resubmits the current composer
draft, or the last submitted prompt"; REQ-NOTIFY-072/075, "a second authentication failure"; REQ-SESSION-026. Raised
2026-10-02 by the 401 note's part A,
[`a-401-ends-the-run-with-a-bare-failure-notice-and-no-authentication-recovery.md`](../defects/fixed/a-401-ends-the-run-with-a-bare-failure-notice-and-no-authentication-recovery.md),
as OQ-177, renumbered OQ-179 at its first merge because `origin/main` had taken OQ-177 and OQ-178 meanwhile, and renumbered
OQ-180 at its second (2026-10-02, beside the note's parts C and D) because `origin/main` had taken OQ-179 meanwhile, part D's
question above, and renumbered OQ-182 at its third (2026-10-02) because `origin/main` had taken OQ-180 meanwhile (bundle
`fin9-queue-dispatch-and-disclosure`'s question above) and the branch's own OQ-181 kept its number; the branch's commit
subjects say OQ-177, and those of its fourth repair round OQ-180. Open until 2026-10-06; ruled that day by the owner, and built.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** every reading below is accepted as built — the
restart appends the last prompt as a new user turn (a run a plan decision launched relaunched as that decision), a restart
that cannot begin takes the pin back, the pin moves every agent on the failed pair, a first failure with no usable fallback
spends the session's first failure, the bookkeeping lasts for the life of the process, and a session not on screen restarts
when it is focused — with one change: **the restart re-sends the prompt's images with its text**, read back from the
session's directory by path and verified by digest through the retry's read-back (`readBackAttachments`). Read the way the
retry reads it, where the ruling leaves the detail open: an image that can no longer be read back, or a model the restart
runs on (the fallback, or the model chosen in the dialog) that declares no image input (REQ-CHAT-171), refuses the restart
by name rather than restarting with less than was sent, so the restart cannot begin, nothing is pinned, and main publishes
the generic notice; a last prompt of images alone is restarted with its images. REQ-NOTIFY-070's "the same prompt" reads so;
no requirement's text is departed from, so the ruling alone settles it. Built the same day (`Sessions.lastPromptOf`, plan
fin21). Corrected the same day at the build's verification: the automatic restart's fallback that declares no image input
does not end at the generic notice — for this prompt it is REQ-NOTIFY-072's "no usable fallback" (`NO_USABLE_FALLBACK`,
`apps/desktop/src/main/auth-fallback.ts`), so main opens the recovery dialog, where a model that takes images can be
chosen; an image that can no longer be read back, and a model chosen in the dialog that takes no image input, still end
at the generic notice. The reading below is kept as the build proceeded under it until then.

Three things the requirements leave to the build:

- **The restart.** REQ-NOTIFY-070 does not say whether restarting "with the same prompt" records the prompt again or
  continues the failed run's request without a new user turn, nor what becomes of the prompt's image attachments.
- **The clearing.** Where the restart cannot begin, "the fallback bookkeeping is cleared". The fallback was pinned before
  the restart was tried (a run resolves its model at start); the requirement does not say whether that pin stands.
- **The session's first failure.** "The first authentication failure of a session" has no stated lifetime: across an
  application restart, the session is the same session, but nothing says the bookkeeping is durable.

**What the build proceeds under** (`Sessions.restartOnFallback`, `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-fallback.ts` — `failure-recovery.ts` until the merge beside parts C and D):
- the restart **re-submits the last user prompt as a new user row** (`Sessions.prompt`), so the transcript shows it sent
  twice, preceded by a system row naming the model that failed and the fallback; the prompt's text is re-sent and its
  attachments are not (the row keeps only their metadata, REQ-CHAT-170);
- *since the fourth repair round (2026-10-02)*, **a run a plan decision launched is relaunched as that decision**
  (`Sessions.relaunchAfterAuthFailure`, the dialog's restarts included): approve carries the plan as the user left it
  again, revise starts the same further cycle with the plan as it stood and the changes stated (REQ-ORCH-154), and no
  prompt is re-submitted — a decision is no prompt. Re-submitting the last user row there had opened a fresh cycle from the
  original prompt and dropped the revise's changes and the plan they revised. A relaunched approval whose run abandoned
  its task appends the request again, as a re-submitted prompt does; a relaunched revise appends none, its work still
  pending. The decision is kept in memory with the run it launched, as the failed model is;
- where the restart cannot begin, **the pin is taken back** as well — a `model_override` entry carrying `cleared: true` —
  so the session stays on the model it had and the generic notice says what happened;
- the "fallback attempted" bookkeeping lives **in main for the life of the process**. The pin itself is durable, so after
  a relaunch the session runs on the fallback, and a failure there is a failure of the fallback, which is not tried again
  (REQ-NOTIFY-075's reading) — the dialog's case.
- Because the restart is a further run of the session, its todo still holds the failed run's task as abandoned
  (REQ-ORCH-074), so a restart that succeeds ends "The run completed with failures: 1 completed, 1 abandoned" — seen in
  `resilience-proof`'s `auth-fallback` run on 2026-10-02. The build leaves it so: the failed run's task did fail.
- The pin is keyed by the **pair** that failed (`provider|model`), as a wait's choice is, so every agent of the session on
  that pair — a child on the primary model included — moves to the fallback; REQ-NOTIFY-070 says "that session's model
  override", which is the one session-wide override REQ-SESSION-026 names.
- *Since the merge beside the note's parts C and D (2026-10-02):* **a first failure with no usable fallback spends the
  session's first failure too.** It opens the recovery dialog (REQ-NOTIFY-072's "a first one with no usable fallback"), and
  the session's next authentication failure — a model chosen by hand in the dialog, or a later prompt after the dialog was
  cancelled — is "a second authentication failure" and the dialog's again, even where a usable fallback has been configured
  meanwhile; only REQ-NOTIFY-078's submission, or a restart that could not begin, makes the next failure the first again
  (`auth-fallback.ts`'s `spent`).
- *Since the same merge:* **a session not on screen is restarted when it is focused.** REQ-NOTIFY-032 holds an unfocused
  session's class publication until a main window follows it, and the automatic restart is the authentication class's
  recovery, so it waits with the rest (`RunFailurePublisher`): the session stays failed under REQ-NOTIFY-032's warning, and
  its restart, its acknowledgement and its prompt arrive with the focus change (REQ-NOTIFY-030). The dialog's restarts
  (`Sessions.restartAfterAuthFailure`, parts C and D) re-submit the prompt as this one does.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the restart appends a user turn or continues the failed request (and so whether the
failed run's task stays abandoned beside the restart's); whether attachments are re-sent; whether a restart that could not begin leaves the pin standing; whether the first-failure bookkeeping outlives
the application; whether the pin covers every agent on the failed pair or the entry agent alone; whether a first failure
with no usable fallback spends the session's automatic fallback; whether a session not on screen is restarted at once,
in the background, or when it is focused; and whether "the same prompt" of a run a plan decision launched is that decision
(as built) or the session's last prompt.

**OQ-183 — Does REQ-NOTIFY-045's "current composer draft" include the images the composer holds?** *(REQ-NOTIFY-045,
"resubmits the current composer draft"; REQ-NOTIFY-066, the draft stored under `composerDraft`; REQ-CHAT-014, the draft
published to application state; REQ-CHAT-011/170/171/172, a submission's attachments and their gates. Raised 2026-10-02 by
the repair of
[`the-retry-action-resubmits-a-prompt-without-its-images.md`](../defects/fixed/the-retry-action-resubmits-a-prompt-without-its-images.md)
(fin8). Open.)*

**Deferred 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)).**

The retry resubmits "the current composer draft" where there is one. The composer holds images beside its text
(REQ-CHAT-170..172), but the draft the specification stores and publishes (REQ-NOTIFY-066, REQ-CHAT-014) is text, and
nothing says whether images held in the composer at the moment a notice's retry is activated belong to "the draft" the
retry resubmits, or stay in the composer for the user's own submission.

**What the build proceeds under** (`retryRun`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/session-actions.ts`): a non-blank draft is
resubmitted as its text alone, as the stored and published draft is text; images held in the composer are not sent by
the retry and stay where they are. A blank draft resubmits the session's last submitted prompt with its images
(`Sessions.retry`, OQ-178's reading since 2026-10-02).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a retry of a non-blank draft carries the images the composer holds (and so whether the
composer publishes them to application state as it does its text), and whether they are then cleared from the composer.

**OQ-184 — Where does REQ-SANDBOX-121's workspace indicator stand, and in what words?** *(Asked until 2026-10-02 as "…and
what does it say after a refused continuation of a confined session?"; that third part was not open and is withdrawn, below.)
(REQ-SANDBOX-121, "A workspace indicator naming the backend appears only for a session whose recorded result is confined"; REQ-MONITOR-257 and REQ-NOTIFY-030, "the sandbox indicator"; REQ-NOTIFY-061, "The sandbox indicator
stops describing the run as sandboxed"; REQ-SHELL-038, the strip's items left to right, a closed list; REQ-SHELL-047, "An
item added to the strip is given its threshold here"; REQ-TOOLS-184. Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`no-workspace-indicator-names-the-confinement-backend.md`](../defects/fixed/no-workspace-indicator-names-the-confinement-backend.md)
(fin8). ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** kept as built, and added to the specification's status-strip item list at that position: the indicator `sandbox: <backend>` (or `sandbox: confined`), named "Confinement backend", stands right after the file-access flag and before the mode flag, and is shown at every width. [`PD-SHELL-008`](../product/directives.md#pd-shell-008) narrows REQ-SHELL-038, REQ-SHELL-047 and REQ-SANDBOX-121.

Two things the requirements leave to the build:

- **Where it stands.** REQ-SANDBOX-121 calls it a *workspace* indicator and places it nowhere; REQ-SHELL-038 lists the
  strip's items and has none for it, and REQ-SHELL-047 says an item added to the strip gets its responsive threshold there,
  which it has not.
- **Its words.** "Naming the backend" fixes the backend's name and nothing else; REQ-TOOLS-184's flags take their
  tooltips' wording from the settings pages, which this indicator is not among.
- ~~**A refused continuation.**~~ *Withdrawn 2026-10-02 (fin8, repair round 1): not open.* It read: "A confined session
  whose next run is refused at the confinement gate (REQ-NOTIFY-061) started no run, and its record still says its last
  run was confined. REQ-NOTIFY-061 has the indicator 'stop describing the run as sandboxed'; whether 'the run' is the
  refused one (which the indicator never described) or the session's latest result is not said." fin8's verifier found the
  reading empty the clause: a refused START leaves no session (REQ-SANDBOX-120), so no indicator is drawn for it either
  way, and the only indicator that can stop is the one a refused continuation would otherwise keep showing. The clause is
  plain, and the build now meets it (below).

**What the build proceeds under** (`statusStripSandboxItem`, `packages/ui/src/composer.ts`; `apps/desktop/src/renderer/main.tsx`):
an inert text item in the status strip, right after the workspace-scope flag, reading `sandbox: <backend>` (or
`sandbox: confined` for a record written before the backend was recorded, whose start event no longer holds it), with the
accessible name "Confinement backend" and a tooltip worded as the settings page's Sandbox mode control words confinement,
joined to the short form as REQ-SHELL-041's flags are. It is shown at every width (no REQ-SHELL-047 threshold). It reads
the focused session's record, so it is absent with no session focused — where a refused start leaves the window, no
session remaining (REQ-SANDBOX-120). After a run of an existing session is refused at the confinement gate (a prompt, a
retry, a continue, a plan decision, an authentication restart) the engine publishes the record no longer sandboxed and with
no backend (`Sessions.refusedAtStart`, `packages/engine/src/sessions.ts`), so the item is gone beside the refusal notice
until a run of the session starts again; the stored row keeps the fact of the run that started (REQ-SANDBOX-094). Until
that repair the reading here was that the item kept describing the last run that started and the refusal changed no
record; the verifier's finding above withdrew it.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the indicator belongs in the status strip (and then its place among REQ-SHELL-038's items
and its REQ-SHELL-047 threshold) or on another workspace surface; its wording beyond the backend's name.

**OQ-185 — Does a mid-run switch of the entry model or reasoning level reach the session's next run?** *(REQ-MONITOR-142,
"A switch of the run's entry model, or of its entry reasoning level, applies from the next iteration onward", its row
saying "it applies from the next iteration"; REQ-MONITOR-143, after the loop has closed "a switch still records the
override"; REQ-SESSION-026, "A mid-session runtime model override (active model key and runtime model configurations) MUST
persist across calls and across reloads of the session"; REQ-MONITOR-146, "Composer-side model, persona, and reasoning
choices apply to the next prompt". Raised 2026-10-02 by
[`an-entry-switch-made-in-a-runs-last-iteration-does-not-reach-a-continuation.md`](../defects/fixed/an-entry-switch-made-in-a-runs-last-iteration-does-not-reach-a-continuation.md)
(fin8, ladder-overrides, task 2), as OQ-183, and renumbered OQ-185 at its merge because `origin/main` had taken OQ-183
and OQ-184 meanwhile. Open until 2026-10-06; ruled that day by the owner, and built.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** keep the switch scoped to its own run, as built,
and reword its row to say it applies for the rest of this run (after the iteration in flight), leaving the composer's model
chip — and, read the same way, its reasoning chip — as the one control for the next run; a reasoning switch is ruled with
the model switch. Minted as [`PD-MONITOR-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-monitor-006), narrowing REQ-MONITOR-142 (the
row's words) and REQ-SESSION-026 (a header switch is not the session-wide override), and built the same day (plan fin21).

A switch of the entry model or reasoning level from the run header or the inspector (`setModel`, `setReasoning`) is held
on its `Run` (`entryOverride`). When the iteration in flight is the run's last, the next iteration is a continuation —
the user's next prompt starts a new `Run`, built from the configuration (`Sessions.launchContinuation`) — so the switch
never applies, though its row said it applies from the next iteration. The requirements pull two ways. REQ-MONITOR-142
speaks of "the run's" entry model and "the next iteration", which a continuation is in the session's numbering;
REQ-MONITOR-143 keeps the override recorded once the loop has closed, which has a purpose only if something later reads
it; and REQ-SESSION-026 makes a mid-session runtime model override persist "across calls and across reloads of the
session". Against them, REQ-MONITOR-146 gives the next run its own selector — the composer's "Model for the next run",
which writes the entry persona's model into the configuration — and a switch that reached the next run would sit beside
that chip, which shows the configured model, with no rule for which wins.

**What the build proceeds under** (`packages/engine/src/run/run.ts`, `entryOverride`, `setEntryModel`,
`setEntryReasoning`; `packages/engine/src/sessions.ts`, `launchContinuation`): a switch **ends with its run**. Its row
still says "it applies from the next iteration", which is true while the run has a next iteration of its own (a queued
prompt, a task added while it runs) and untrue when it has none. A change-model resolution of a wait (REQ-ORCH-091 d) is
not such a switch: its override is session-wide and reaches every later run. The autopsy reader prints the entry key
`undetermined` after a continuation whose snapshot names no entry model when a switch onto another key preceded it
([the repair](../defects/fixed/the-autopsy-reader-keeps-a-switched-key-across-a-continuation-that-records-no-snapshot.md)),
so its reading is right under either answer; a continuation whose snapshot names the entry model says which it ran on.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a switch made from the run header or the inspector reaches the session's next run
(recorded session-wide, as REQ-SESSION-026's override, and taken by the continuation unless the composer's next-run choice
differs), or ends with its run (and its row then says so when no further iteration of the run is queued); the same for a
reasoning switch; and, if it reaches the next run, how it stands beside the composer's next-run chip.

**OQ-186 — Which models does the quota-wait surface's "change model" list: REQ-MONITOR-193's candidates or REQ-NOTIFY-074's
list?** *(REQ-MONITOR-303, "a model picker offering the fallback candidates of REQ-MONITOR-193, listing excluded pairs with
their reason rather than hiding them (REQ-MONITOR-194)"; REQ-MONITOR-193, "exactly the configured models … whose size tier
equals the current model's tier, less any model excluded … in the order their models are declared"; REQ-NOTIFY-263,
"Changing model opens the model list of REQ-NOTIFY-074 and pins the chosen model for the session under REQ-NOTIFY-089";
REQ-NOTIFY-074, "lists models from providers other than the one that failed, ahead of any others … Where no other provider
offers a model, every model except the one that failed is listed"; REQ-MONITOR-194, "from any model selector or from the
quota-wait decision surface … listed there rather than hidden, annotated". Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`the-quota-wait-picker-lists-every-model-without-marking-the-excluded-pairs.md`](../defects/fixed/the-quota-wait-picker-lists-every-model-without-marking-the-excluded-pairs.md)
(fin8, bundle `fin8-noticed-gaps-4`), as OQ-185, and renumbered OQ-186 at its merge of `origin/main` because the
ladder-overrides bundle had taken OQ-185 meanwhile. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the current full list is accepted: the picker offers every configured model key, alphabetically, the waiting model included, with a pair held out of quota annotated and choosable, and both requirements are amended to describe it. [`PD-MONITOR-004`](../product/directives.md#pd-monitor-004) narrows REQ-MONITOR-303 and REQ-NOTIFY-263.

Two requirements describe the one control. REQ-MONITOR-303 lists REQ-MONITOR-193's candidates — the same-tier configured
models from any provider, in declaration order, less the pairs held out of quota — and beside them the excluded pairs,
annotated; a model of another tier is not offered, and a model that resolves through no tier alias "may still be chosen
explicitly" without saying from where. REQ-NOTIFY-263 opens REQ-NOTIFY-074's list — every model, other providers first,
the one that failed left out, each labelled with its model name and its provider — which has no tier and lists no excluded
pair as such, and REQ-NOTIFY-074 written for the authentication recovery dialog leaves the failed model out where
REQ-MONITOR-194 would have the waiting pair, when it is the one held out of quota, listed and annotated. They agree on
one thing: REQ-MONITOR-194 asks every model selector to list an excluded pair annotated with its reason, and an explicit
choice of it to clear its exclusion.

**What the build proceeds under** (`WaitHeader` and `waitModelOptions`, `packages/ui/src/WorkspaceView.tsx`; the record's
`wait.excluded`, `excludedModelKeys` in `packages/engine/src/run/resilience.ts`): what both agree on, over the list as it
was built. The picker lists every configured model key as the configuration snapshot gives them (alphabetical; the
waiting model included), which holds REQ-MONITOR-193's candidates and REQ-NOTIFY-074's models alike, with neither one's
filter nor its order applied; a key whose provider-and-model pair the session recorded out of quota is listed in place,
annotated "provider reported insufficient quota in this session", and stays choosable. Choosing it is the run's explicit
choice (`setEntryModel`), which clears the chosen pair's exclusion (`ResilienceMemory.clearExhausted`, plan fin8's
ladder-overrides bundle) and, in a quota wait on that very pair, resolves the wait as a retry on it with no override
persisted. (Built first on `origin/main` 4ae715a, where that choice cleared nothing and the waiting pair was refused as "the
model that is waiting"; the ladder-overrides merge brought the clearing.) No model is labelled with its provider.

**What a ruling decides.** Which list the picker offers — REQ-MONITOR-193's same-tier candidates beside the excluded pairs,
REQ-NOTIFY-074's (other providers first, each labelled with its provider), or one ahead of the other — and in which order;
whether the waiting pair is listed when it is not held out of quota (a rate-limit wait); and whether a model of no tier is
offered here.

**OQ-187 — Where does the project setup consent dialog stand: over a corner of the view, or in a region of the window that
takes room from every view?** *(REQ-WORKSPACE-106, "a non-modal, window-level dialog (the rest of the app stays
navigable)"; REQ-WORKSPACE-105, opened by itself once per workspace open and open until answered; ADR-0048's non-modal
window-level level, "an in-window panel that does not trap focus and leaves the rest navigable"; REQ-SHELL-022's 1000x680
minimum; REQ-SHELL-024's vertical order. Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`the-project-setup-dialog-is-drawn-over-the-title-bar-window-controls.md`](../defects/fixed/the-project-setup-dialog-is-drawn-over-the-title-bar-window-controls.md)
(fin8, bundle `fin8-noticed-gaps-4`), as OQ-186, and renumbered OQ-187 at its merge of `origin/main` because the
ladder-overrides bundle had taken OQ-185 meanwhile. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the current floating placement is accepted: an overlay of the rail-and-view region at its top corner, inset by `--rt-space-4`, below the title bar and the notice slot, bounded by that region and scrolling with its answers pinned when shorter than it needs. It traps no focus, Escape answers it as a skip, and it lies over the view's top corner while it is open; "the rest of the app stays navigable" is met by controls reachable from the keyboard and, once it is answered, from the pointer.

The dialog is window-level: it belongs to no view and is shown whichever view is on screen, so the decision it waits on is
not lost by navigating. Every placement of such a surface takes something. Fixed at the window's corner it lay over the
title bar's Sessions, Minimize, Maximize and Close window and the notice's answers (the defect above). An overlay of the
rail-and-view region leaves the window's chrome and the notice reachable and lies over the view's top corner instead. A
region of the window laid out in flow — a band below the notice slot, or a column beside the view — overlays nothing but
takes its height or width from every view, which at REQ-SHELL-022's minimum some views do not have to give (the
Workspace view's transcript floor and composer alone are most of it). The re-authentication prompt, ADR-0048's other
surface of this level, was moved in flow because it belongs to one view (OQ-181); this one does not. The specification
does not say which the setup dialog takes, nor whether "the rest of the app stays navigable" is met by controls that are
reachable from the keyboard, and from the pointer once the dialog is answered, but not by the pointer while it is open.

**What the build proceeds under** (`AppShell`'s `windowDialog` slot, `packages/ui/src/AppShell.tsx`; `.project-setup` in
`packages/ui/src/shell.css`): an overlay of the rail-and-view region, `absolute` at its top corner with the language's
`--rt-space-4` inset, bounded by that region (scrolling, its answers pinned to its floor, when shorter than it needs). It
begins below the title bar and the notice slot at any notice height, so no title-bar control and no notice answer is
under it (`init-proof`'s `consent` scenario measures five, none covered). It lies over the view's top corner: measured in
the built app on 2026-10-02, at 1440x900 the Overview's List sessions and New session and the Workspace inspector's
Persona, Steer, Cancel and Pop out; at 1000x680 also the run header's model and reasoning switches and the composer's
right part (its Send is disabled while this prompt is unanswered, REQ-WORKSPACE-112), and the top-right controls of the
other views (Git's New worktree, Library's search, Settings' model rows). It traps no focus (no `aria-modal`, no backdrop),
so they stay reachable from the keyboard (not measured), and Escape answers the dialog as a skip (REQ-WORKSPACE-107).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the dialog may lie over the view while it is open (and then which corner), or stands in
a region of its own that every view yields room to at REQ-SHELL-022's minimum (and then which, with what bound on its
height), or in another form — collapsed to a bar until opened, as the re-authentication prompt yields beside an expanded
plan gate.

**OQ-188 — What does "Keep waiting" on the quota-wait surface do: resolve the wait as a retry now, or leave it as it is?**
*(REQ-MONITOR-303, "keep waiting, which resolves the wait as a retry and returns the status to `running`"; spec resolution 29,
which fixes the three choices and "what each does"; REQ-NOTIFY-263's three choices; REQ-MONITOR-192 and REQ-NOTIFY-087, the
auto-resume variant ending by itself when its interval elapses; REQ-MONITOR-004's closed enumeration of twenty-two operations;
REQ-MONITOR-194. Raised 2026-10-02 by task 1 of plan fin10's `fin10-quota-exclusions-and-choices` bundle, recording
[`keep-waiting-on-the-quota-wait-header-sends-nothing-where-it-should-resolve-the-wait-as-a-retry.md`](../defects/fixed/keep-waiting-on-the-quota-wait-header-sends-nothing-where-it-should-resolve-the-wait-as-a-retry.md).
Open; owner-only, as every question this round raises. Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner, and built.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** keep waiting retries the same model at once in
the out-of-quota wait (the variant that never auto-resumes), clearing its out-of-quota mark through the existing retry path
— read onto the existing switch of the entry model, which the header sends with the waiting pair's key, now carried on the
record's `wait` as `modelKey`, so REQ-MONITOR-004's twenty-two operations are unchanged — and stays a plain acknowledgement in
the timed wait, whose timer already retries. Written as [`PD-MONITOR-004`](../product/directives.md#pd-monitor-004)'s revision 2 (minted on its branch as a
directive of its own and folded in at the landing rebase), narrowing REQ-MONITOR-303, and built the same day (plan fin21). The reading taken where the ruling leaves a detail open, as
corrected in that plan's repair round 1: "retry the same model" moves no other agent — keep waiting resumes only the agents
parked out of quota on the waiting pair and persists no override, an agent parked on another pair keeping its own wait — and
the press is marked as keep waiting and names the wait it answers, so a second press for a wait already retried is refused
rather than read as a switch of the entry model.

ADR-0010's third execution (2026-09-05) read keep waiting as "the absence of a decision": the header acknowledges ("Still
waiting.") and sends nothing, so the wait goes on as it was — the exhausted variant until a person decides, the auto-resume
variant until its timer retries. That reading cites REQ-NOTIFY-263 and REQ-MONITOR-192 and predates REQ-MONITOR-303, which
says keep waiting resolves the wait as a retry, in both variants alike. For the exhausted variant the two readings are not in
tension with any other requirement: retrying is the only thing keep waiting can resolve to, and a retry of a pair the user
chose to keep waiting on is an explicit choice of it (REQ-MONITOR-194), which clears its exclusion — the build already does
this when the waiting pair is chosen in the picker (`setEntryModel`'s quota-retry branch). For the auto-resume variant an
immediate retry ends the provider's own interval early, where REQ-MONITOR-192 says "the wait timing out resolves as a retry"
and REQ-NOTIFY-087 "the wait ends by itself once the computed interval has elapsed"; whether keep waiting retries at once
there, or only acknowledges and lets the timer retry, the specification does not settle. Either retry needs a means on the
control channel: no operation of REQ-MONITOR-004's closed twenty-two names it, so it would be read onto an existing one (the
quota-retry branch of `setModel` with the waiting key serves the exhausted variant only when the waiting pair is a configured
key) or added.

**What the build proceeds under** (as built, unchanged): keep waiting is the absence of a decision in both variants — the
header acknowledges and sends nothing; the exhausted variant ends only by a change of model or a cancel, the auto-resume
variant by its timer as well. No loop with the pre-call exclusion read (`resilientStep`, since the same bundle) is possible,
because nothing is retried.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether keep waiting resolves the exhausted variant as a retry of the waiting pair (and then that
it clears the pair's exclusion as an explicit choice does); whether it retries the auto-resume variant at once or leaves its
timer to retry; and whether either is a new operation or a reading of an existing one.

**OQ-189 — What does a configured model slot call when the session holds its pair out of quota or has replaced it?**
*(REQ-MONITOR-194, "neither retried automatically nor offered as an automatic fallback candidate", and spec resolution 21,
which reads the exclusion as governing automatic behaviour; REQ-ORCH-091 (d), the override "for the rest of the session";
REQ-MONITOR-080, a configured compression model used, else the agent's own; REQ-ORCH-114, the classifier's slot order.
Raised 2026-10-03 by task 2 of plan fin10's `fin10-quota-exclusions-and-choices` bundle, recording
[`a-configured-model-slot-is-called-on-a-pair-the-session-replaced-or-holds-out-of-quota.md`](../defects/fixed/a-configured-model-slot-is-called-on-a-pair-the-session-replaced-or-holds-out-of-quota.md).
Numbered 189, the next free on the branch after its OQ-188; renumbered at the merge if taken meanwhile. Open; owner-only, as
every question this round raises. Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner, and built.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** every helper call — the intent and loop
classifiers, a configured compressor, the summariser and the post-run analyst — follows the session's model override as the
summariser already did; where the pair it reaches is held out of quota with nothing replacing it, a compression runs on the
calling agent's current model, and the classifiers and the analyst make no call. The summariser, which the ruling does not
name, is read as the condensing call it is beside compression: it summarises the child on the model the child ran on, and
writes the fallback report where that is held out of quota too; and a configured `compressor.model` yields to the exclusion
of its pair. Minted as [`PD-MONITOR-007`](../product/directives.md#pd-monitor-007), narrowing REQ-MONITOR-080, REQ-ORCH-009,
REQ-ORCH-114, REQ-ORCH-100, REQ-CONFIG-065 and REQ-LIBRARY-037, and built the same day (plan fin21).

The run's auxiliary calls — the intent classifier and the pre-flight, the loop classifier, a configured compressor, the
post-run analyst, and the summariser — take configured slots. Since fin10 an agent's own calls — its model steps, and a
compression pass on its own model where no `compressor.model` is configured — never reach a pair the session holds out of
quota: the cell is settled before every call and before the turn's compression check (`settleBeforeCall`, which sends the
agent to its same-tier candidate or a wait), and a manual pass in the span before the agent's next call moves it makes no
call and fails with its reason. (Corrected in place at the bundle's first repair round, 2026-10-03. The sentence first read
"Since fin10 an agent's own calls never reach a pair the session holds out of quota (the ladder's pre-call read sends the
agent to its same-tier candidate or a wait)", which was false of the branch as first built: the turn's automatic compression
check ran before the ladder's pre-call move, so a root resumed on a pair its child had just excluded compressed on that pair,
at its threshold, and only then moved — the verifier's reproduction.) Since fin8 these slots follow a session-wide override; the summariser follows the override but not the exclusion, and the others follow
neither. For the override the requirements point one way (REQ-ORCH-091 d keeps it "for the rest of the session", and it
replaces a pair, not an agent's choice); for the exclusion they do not say what replaces the slot: a same-tier candidate
(REQ-ORCH-091 b is an agent's ladder, and these calls have none), the slot order's next entry (REQ-ORCH-114 names one for the
classifier alone), the calling agent's own model (REQ-MONITOR-080's default for the compressor), or skipping the call (which
REQ-ORCH-114 allows for the classifier when no slot resolves) — nor whether a configured `compressor.model` still "wins" over
an exclusion of its pair.

**What the build proceeds under** (as built, unchanged): each configured slot is called as configured. A session that has
recorded its small model out of quota still sends the classifier, the loop classifier, a configured compressor and the
analyst to it; a real provider refuses those calls and each path's own failure handling applies (the classifier skips, the
compression pass fails and is reported, the analyst's run is reported failed).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether these calls follow a session-wide override (and then all of them, as the summariser does);
what each calls when its configured pair is excluded and nothing replaces it; and whether a configured `compressor.model`
yields to the exclusion of its pair.

**OQ-190 — Whose tokens does the status strip's tokens item count: the workspace's runs, or the focused session's?**
*(REQ-SHELL-044, "The tokens item reads the running total of tokens used"; REQ-SHELL-045, the cost item's figure is "the
model provider's reported cost for this workspace's runs so far"; REQ-SHELL-038, the items' accessible names, "Tokens used"
and "Cost so far". Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`the-status-strip-applies-no-responsive-hiding-and-overflows-at-the-minimum-window.md`](../defects/fixed/the-status-strip-applies-no-responsive-hiding-and-overflows-at-the-minimum-window.md)
(fin10, bundle `fin10-strip-notices-and-listing`). Raised as OQ-188; renumbered 190 at the merge, since origin/main took 188 and 189 meanwhile. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** accepted: the tokens item counts the workspace's runs, as the cost item does, the sum of every stored session's `tokens_input + tokens_output` for this workspace, and its tooltip says so ("Tokens used by this workspace's runs so far: {n} tok."). REQ-SHELL-044 names no scope, so this ruling settles it.

REQ-SHELL-045 scopes the cost to this workspace's runs and its tooltip says so. REQ-SHELL-044 says "the running total of
tokens used" and names no scope: not the workspace's runs, not the focused session's, not the current run's. The two items
stand side by side, so a reader compares them, and a session-scoped token count beside a workspace-scoped cost would make
that comparison wrong without saying so.

**What the build proceeds under** (`workspaceUsage`, `packages/engine/src/workspace-usage.ts`; `stripItems`,
`packages/ui/src/composer.ts`): the workspace's runs, as the cost is — the sum of every stored session's
`tokens_input + tokens_output` for this workspace, read from the run host on the `workspace.usage` command when the strip
mounts, when the focused session's own usage moves and every five seconds (a background session's run moves it too). Its
tooltip says so: "Tokens used by this workspace's runs so far: {n} tok."

**What a ruling decides.** The scope of REQ-SHELL-044's running total (the workspace's runs, the focused session, the
current run), and whether the tooltip names it.

**OQ-191 — The workspace domain states five things about the status strip that the shell domain, which owns it, states
otherwise.** *(REQ-SHELL-040, "Neither failure is silent", with the resolution of `docs/spec/resolutions/12-desktop-shell-windows.md`
item 7, "Silent failure is dropped"; REQ-WORKSPACE-019, "a failure to open SHALL be silent"; REQ-SHELL-041, the
`unsaved settings` explanation conveys "that runs keep using the last saved values until they are saved", and the mode
flag's explanation is given word for word; REQ-WORKSPACE-022, the same flag's explanation conveys "that runs use the values
on screen rather than the values on disk", and the mode flag's conveys "exactly the following and no more: which permission
mode is in force and that it decides whether a tool call is allowed outright, put to the user, or refused", the redaction
flag's "that secrets are removed from what is recorded and displayed and that this cannot be turned off", and the
circuit-breaker flag's "that the circuit breaker is armed and will halt a run that trips it"; REQ-SHELL-047,
"This document owns the status strip". Raised 2026-10-02 by the repair of
[`the-status-strip-applies-no-responsive-hiding-and-overflows-at-the-minimum-window.md`](../defects/fixed/the-status-strip-applies-no-responsive-hiding-and-overflows-at-the-minimum-window.md)
(fin10, bundle `fin10-strip-notices-and-listing`). Raised as OQ-189; renumbered 191 at the merge, since origin/main took 188 and 189 meanwhile. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06. *Amended 2026-10-03 (fin10's repair round): raised as "three
things", it missed the redaction and circuit-breaker explanations, which REQ-WORKSPACE-022's "exactly the following and no
more" bounds as well; both are added below.*)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the shell specification's five statements stand, and the workspace specification is amended to match them: the path link's failure is reported, the `unsaved settings` explanation says runs keep using the last saved values, and the mode, redaction and circuit-breaker explanations are REQ-SHELL-041's word for word. [`PD-WORKSPACE-007`](../product/directives.md#pd-workspace-007) narrows REQ-WORKSPACE-019 and REQ-WORKSPACE-022.

Five statements disagree:

- **The workspace-path link's failure.** REQ-SHELL-040 (amended by the shell domain's resolution 7) reports a failure to open
  the folder on the transient error surface with the path attempted; REQ-WORKSPACE-019 still says the failure is silent.
- **What `unsaved settings` explains.** REQ-SHELL-041: runs keep using the last saved values until the edits are saved.
  REQ-WORKSPACE-022: runs use the values on screen rather than the values on disk. They are opposite claims about which
  values a run uses; the product's runs read the saved configuration (ADR-0037's Tier B, applied at the next run start).
- **The mode flag's explanation.** REQ-SHELL-041 gives the sentence ("Permission mode {mode}: how much agents may do
  without asking. Change it under the composer or in Settings → Runtime."); REQ-WORKSPACE-022 bounds it to the mode in
  force and that it decides allow, ask or refuse, "and no more", which the shell's second sentence exceeds.
- **The redaction flag's explanation.** REQ-SHELL-041 gives the sentence ("Secret redaction: anything that looks like a
  credential is masked before it reaches a model or the transcript."); REQ-WORKSPACE-022 bounds it to two facts, that
  secrets are removed from what is recorded and displayed and that this cannot be turned off, "and no more". The shell's
  sentence does not say it cannot be turned off, and adds "before it reaches a model", which the bound excludes.
- **The circuit-breaker flag's explanation.** REQ-SHELL-041 gives the sentence ("Circuit breaker: Rotaris stops a run that
  keeps repeating a failing step."); REQ-WORKSPACE-022 bounds it to that the circuit breaker is armed and will halt a run
  that trips it, "and no more". The shell's sentence says what trips it (a repeated failing step) and does not say it is
  armed.

The file-access flag's two explanations are not among them: REQ-WORKSPACE-022 fixes that pair word for word and
REQ-SHELL-041 asks only that they use the Settings control's words, which REQ-WORKSPACE-022's pair does (REQ-WORKSPACE-148's
control "lets agents read and write outside this workspace folder").

**What the build proceeds under** (`apps/desktop/src/main/commands/workspace.ts`'s `workspace.openFolder`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/strip-facts.ts`, `statusStripSafetyFlags` in `packages/ui/src/composer.ts`): the shell domain's
statements, since REQ-SHELL-047 says that document owns the strip and its resolution 7 is the later decision. A folder that
cannot be opened raises the transient error naming the path (an opener that never answers counts after 5 s,
`apps/desktop/src/main/open-folder.ts`); `unsaved settings` reads "The Settings view is holding edits that have not been
saved; runs keep using the last saved values until they are saved."; the mode, redaction and circuit-breaker flags'
sentences are REQ-SHELL-041's word for word; the file-access pair is REQ-WORKSPACE-022's.

**What a ruling decides.** Which domain's statement stands for each of the five, and an amendment to the other.

**OQ-192 — The sessions card's rows carry a token label, a duration label and a detail caption, which the listing
record's closed field set does not hold.** *(REQ-MONITOR-171, each sessions-card row carries "a detail caption, … the
branch, a token label, and a duration label"; REQ-SESSION-030, the listing record "MUST hold exactly these fields" and
"Every attribute a listing shows about the session itself MUST be one of these — making a new attribute list-visible is a
change to this field set, not a reader-side extension"; REQ-SESSION-042, "Building the list MUST read nothing but those
listing records". Raised 2026-10-03 by
[`the-session-list-counts-each-sessions-checkpoints-from-the-checkpoint-table.md`](../defects/fixed/the-session-list-counts-each-sessions-checkpoints-from-the-checkpoint-table.md)
(fin11, bundle `fin11-strip-labels-and-auxiliary-windows`). ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the three labels stay on the card, and the listing record's field list gains the token total, the run start time and the workspace path. The duration label is the latest run's, as built. [`PD-SESSION-001`](../product/directives.md#pd-session-001) narrows REQ-SESSION-030. [`the-session-list-counts-each-sessions-checkpoints-from-the-checkpoint-table.md`](../defects/fixed/the-session-list-counts-each-sessions-checkpoints-from-the-checkpoint-table.md), whose checkpoint half closed on 2026-10-03, closes with this ruling.

REQ-SESSION-030's twelve fields are `session_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `execution_status`, `schema_version`,
`internal`, `worktree`, `checkpoint_count`, `task_title`, `requirement_id`, `unit_id` and `awaiting_input`. None is a token
total, a duration or a caption, and the requirement forbids showing any attribute of the session that is not one of them.
REQ-MONITOR-171 requires each row of the Overview's sessions card to show all three. The branch is not in the
disagreement: it is the `worktree` binding record's. Neither requirement names the other, and no directive governs either.

**What the build proceeds under** (`Sessions.list`, `packages/engine/src/sessions.ts`; the sessions card,
`packages/ui/src/OverviewView.tsx`): REQ-MONITOR-171's row, drawn from columns of the same session row the listing record
is read from, so building the list still reads one row per session and nothing else of the session's: the token label is
`tokens_input + tokens_output`, the duration label is `durationLabel(run_started_at, …)` and the detail caption is
`workspace_root`. No transcript, state or history is read for them.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the three labels stay on the card (and REQ-SESSION-030's field set gains them, the
"change to this field set" it names), or leave it (and REQ-MONITOR-171 is amended).

*(Added 2026-10-06, a case of the duration label, from finding G8 of the orchestrator's final default live run at `27a5127`
([`fixed/a-continuations-run-timing-starts-after-its-pre-flight-where-a-launchs-counts-it.md`](../defects/fixed/a-continuations-run-timing-starts-after-its-pre-flight-where-a-launchs-counts-it.md)).
The label is the latest run's duration: for a session paused and continued it leaves the first run out (the live run's
`resume` session ran 87.7 s over two runs; its label counts the continuation alone, 64.9 s once that repair counts the
continuation's pre-flight). Neither REQ-SESSION-154 ("a relative-time duration label") nor REQ-MONITOR-171 ("a duration
label") says whether it is the latest run's or the session's. What the build proceeds under is unchanged: the latest run's,
`durationLabel(run_started_at, …)`. What a ruling adds, if the label stays: which of the two it is.)*

**OQ-193 — What does the status strip's branch item show on a detached HEAD, outside a repository and before the first
read: REQ-GIT-161's conveyed states, or REQ-WORKSPACE-020's empty item?** *(REQ-GIT-161, the item "SHALL convey that the
checkout is on no branch when the workspace, or the focused session's worktree, is on a detached HEAD, and SHALL convey that
there is no branch to show when the folder is not a Git repository at all — a state distinct from a repository whose branch
could not be read", each "distinguishable from an ordinary branch name and from the other"; REQ-WORKSPACE-020, "The item
SHALL render as empty text — no icon, no arrow, no tooltip — exactly when the snapshot's branch name is empty, which per
REQ-WORKSPACE-029 covers git being unavailable, the folder not being a repository, a detached HEAD, and an unborn branch";
REQ-SHELL-042, which owns the item and names neither state. Raised 2026-10-03 by the repair of
[`the-status-strips-branch-item-has-no-branch-icon-and-its-tooltip-no-full-stop.md`](../defects/fixed/the-status-strips-branch-item-has-no-branch-icon-and-its-tooltip-no-full-stop.md)
(fin11, bundle `fin11-strip-labels-and-auxiliary-windows`). ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the visible words and tooltips stay as built, and REQ-WORKSPACE-020 is amended to match them: `detached HEAD`, `no git repository`, `no git` and `—` before the first read, each with its tooltip and no icon. The base checkout's tooltip keeps its full stop and its singular or plural commit wording as built, REQ-GIT-122's form read as a template of them. [`PD-WORKSPACE-008`](../product/directives.md#pd-workspace-008) narrows REQ-WORKSPACE-020 and REQ-GIT-122. [`the-status-strips-branch-item-has-no-branch-icon-and-its-tooltip-no-full-stop.md`](../defects/fixed/the-status-strips-branch-item-has-no-branch-icon-and-its-tooltip-no-full-stop.md) closes with this ruling. The ruling does not reach two states this entry never named: an unborn branch, and a repository whose branch could not be read. REQ-WORKSPACE-020's empty item (and, for the unreadable branch, REQ-GIT-161's empty value) still governs them, and the build departed there: it drew the branch icon, `—` and the tooltip "Branch this workspace is on: —.", as if `—` were a branch's name. Found by the verifier of this round and recorded, not repaired, in [`the-status-strips-branch-item-draws-an-unborn-branch-as-a-branch-named-dash.md`](../defects/fixed/the-status-strips-branch-item-draws-an-unborn-branch-as-a-branch-named-dash.md); repaired by fin22 the same day, the item now REQ-WORKSPACE-020's empty item in both states.

REQ-GIT-161 requires a detached checkout and a non-repository to be conveyed, each in words or markers distinct from a branch
name and from each other, and a repository whose branch could not be read to take REQ-GIT-112's empty value. REQ-WORKSPACE-020
requires the item to be empty, with no tooltip, in exactly those cases (and for git being unavailable and an unborn branch).
One item cannot do both. Neither requirement names the other, and no directive governs either.

**What the build proceeds under** (`branchStripItem`, `packages/ui/src/GitView.tsx`; `stripItems`,
`packages/ui/src/composer.ts`): REQ-GIT-161's words, unchanged by this repair. A detached HEAD reads `detached HEAD` with the
tooltip "This workspace is on no branch (detached HEAD)."; a folder that is not a repository reads `no git repository`
("This folder is not a Git repository."), and with git unavailable `no git` ("Git is not installed or not on PATH."); before
the first read the item reads `—` ("Branch this workspace is on: not read yet"). The detached and absent states are set in
italics. None of these draws REQ-SHELL-042's branch icon, which is drawn only before a branch name.

Two readings recorded beside it, which a ruling may revisit: the base checkout's tooltip ends with REQ-WORKSPACE-020's full
stop ("Branch this workspace is on: main.", "…, 1 commit ahead.", "…, {n} commits ahead."), since REQ-SHELL-042 leaves the
wording to the implementation; and REQ-GIT-122's backticked `Branch this workspace is on: <branch>` with `, N commit(s)
ahead` is read as a template rather than a literal, since REQ-SHELL-044 forbids rendering `(s)` as written.

**What a ruling decides.** Which requirement's treatment of the detached, non-repository, git-unavailable and unread states
stands for the strip's branch item, and an amendment to the other.

**OQ-194 — Which root do REQ-MCP-035's filesystem fill-in, REQ-MCP-043's default working directory and REQ-MCP-070's
`lsp_init` call name for a run in an isolated working tree?** *(REQ-MCP-034, "For a run against an isolated working tree,
the appended path SHALL be that tree's root"; REQ-MCP-035, "with no path arguments, the workspace root SHALL be appended";
REQ-MCP-043 and REQ-MCP-050, `cwd` "the entry's configured value, or the workspace root when unset"; REQ-MCP-070, `lsp_init`
"called once with the arguments `{"root": "<workspace_root>"}`". Raised 2026-10-03 by the repair of
[`fixed/an-isolated-runs-code-intelligence-server-is-bound-to-the-anchoring-checkout.md`](../defects/fixed/an-isolated-runs-code-intelligence-server-is-bound-to-the-anchoring-checkout.md)
(fin12, bundle `fin12-worktree-bound-code-intelligence`). Open until 2026-10-06; ruled then, below.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** as recommended, for a run in an isolated tree
REQ-MCP-035's fill-in, the default `cwd` of REQ-MCP-043 and REQ-MCP-050, and REQ-MCP-070's `lsp_init` root all name the
tree's root, by extending the rebinding that already moved REQ-MCP-034's project path; only what the product filled in
moves, and a path or `cwd` the user configured stays. Minted as [`PD-MCP-002`](../product/directives.md#pd-mcp-002), which
narrows REQ-MCP-035, REQ-MCP-043, REQ-MCP-050 and REQ-MCP-070, and built under it (fin21).

REQ-MCP-034 names the isolated tree's root for the one path it appends. The three neighbouring rules say "the workspace root"
and say nothing of an isolated run, while the requirements domain separates the anchoring workspace (where the record stays)
from the root a run executes in (REQ-WORKSPACE-050, REQ-GIT-140). Read literally, a filesystem server carried by a persona of
an isolated run is pointed at the main checkout — the escape REQ-MCP-034's clause closes for code intelligence — and a server
named `lsp` is initialised on it.

**What the build proceeds under** (`mcpConfigurationForExecutionRoot`, `packages/config/src/mcp/index.ts`; the tool port's
`ready()`, `apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`): the literal reading. Only the path REQ-MCP-034's stage appended is
rebound to the tree's root; REQ-MCP-035's fill-in and the default `cwd` stay the workspace root, and the session's
