connections keep the workspace root for `lsp_init`. The shipped configuration carries no filesystem server and no server
named `lsp`, so nothing a default run launches is affected.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether "the workspace root" in REQ-MCP-035, REQ-MCP-043/050 and REQ-MCP-070 reads as the run's
execution root for an isolated run (an amendment naming it, as REQ-MCP-034 does), or stays the anchoring workspace.

**OQ-195 — Whose project memories does a run in an isolated working tree read and write, and what becomes of the project the
runtime creates there?** *(REQ-MCP-034's isolated-run clause; REQ-MCP-102, the block telling the agent "to read the memories
that already exist before it starts exploring the codebase" and "to write durable findings … back through the
memory-writing tools it holds"; REQ-MCP-099, project creation "SHALL be skipped when the runtime's per-project marker file is
already present, and SHALL never overwrite an existing project"; OQ-161's reading, which keeps the marker's directory in the
repository's own exclude file. Raised 2026-10-03 by the repair of
[`fixed/an-isolated-runs-code-intelligence-server-is-bound-to-the-anchoring-checkout.md`](../defects/fixed/an-isolated-runs-code-intelligence-server-is-bound-to-the-anchoring-checkout.md)
(fin12). Open.)*

**Deferred 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)).**

Bound to the tree's root as REQ-MCP-034 requires, the runtime works on a project of its own. Measured on 2026-10-03 against the
pinned runtime (serena-agent 1.7.0, launched as the product launches it, in a scratch repository whose main tree had been set
up by REQ-MCP-099's creation step and whose marker directory was excluded the OQ-161 way): the linked worktree held no marker,
because the directory is ignored and so never checked out; the runtime's first launch against the tree generated the project
there itself (`.serena/project.yml`, named after the tree's directory, its languages detected from the tree's files) and
registered the tree's path as a second project in the runtime's home; `git status` in the tree showed only the run's own
change, the generated directory being excluded too. It answered from the tree — a pattern search found the function written
in the tree and not the main tree's uncommitted one — and never fell back to the main checkout. But `list_memories`
answered empty although the main tree held a memory, and a memory written in the run landed in the tree's own ignored
`.serena/memories/`, which the main tree never sees and which goes when the tree is removed. Every unit worktree also adds an
entry to the runtime home's project list that nothing removes.

**What the build proceeds under**: the tree's own project, as the runtime makes it. Nothing is copied into the tree before the
launch (a copied marker would carry the main tree's project name and its registration), nothing is merged back when the run
ends, and no entry is removed from the runtime's project list. REQ-MCP-102's block is printed unchanged.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an isolated run should read the anchoring project's memories (and how — a copy at the
tree's creation, or the runtime pointed at a shared memory store), whether what it writes there should reach the anchoring
project (at accept, or never), and whether the runtime's project registration of a removed tree is cleaned up.

**OQ-196 — How long may a child at its time limit take to finish the model step in flight, and what is kept when that bound
is reached?** *(REQ-ORCH-088, on expiry "gracefully pause the child", narrowed by `PD-ORCH-004`; REQ-MONITOR-123, a pause
"finishes its current step and then stops", narrowed by `PD-ORCH-005` revision 2; REQ-CONFIG-131's
`graceful_pause_tool_deadline`, which bounds in-flight tool calls only; REQ-CONFIG-113's `child_timeout`, the "hard per-child
wall clock". Raised 2026-10-03 from finding U1 of the orchestrator's duress live run at `1763f7f`
([`a-child-at-its-ceiling-has-the-model-step-in-flight-aborted-30-s-later.md`](../defects/fixed/a-child-at-its-ceiling-has-the-model-step-in-flight-aborted-30-s-later.md)).
~~Open, the owner's.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-06.**)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the current bound stays and is written down — what a child has in
flight when its `child_timeout` expires has at most 30 s to end and is then aborted, so the child's time limit stays hard;
of a model step so cut, its streamed reasoning is kept in the transcript and nothing else of it is kept. As built; by
[`PD-ORCH-004`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-004) revision 5, with back-pointers at REQ-ORCH-088 and REQ-CONFIG-113.

The duress run of 2026-10-03 (pack `2026-10-03T06-15-52-273Z`, endpoint `katalyst`, a model that reasons before it answers)
had two children reach the 1200 s ceiling, each in the middle of a model step. The ceiling asked each to land; the landing
backstop aborted each step at exactly ceiling + 30.0 s — traffic #100 after 115.4 s and traffic #186 after 87.0 s, 202.4 s of
generation in all. Neither step had produced text or a tool call. Their streamed reasoning stayed in the transcript as
`thinking` rows; nothing of either reached the child's conversation, its report or its continuation. #186's reasoning ended
"Now let me write docs/verification.md"; the continuation that then wrote the file took 746 s. At `71ad8e8` all three
landings finished their step. Both children were continued once and both continuations succeeded.

The specification asks for a graceful pause and a hard ceiling, and states one bound between them for tool calls alone.
A model step's landing has none, and single steps of the two cut-off children took up to 131.9 s in this run, four times
the 30 s the build allows.

**What the build proceeds under** (`CHILD_LANDING_GRACE` in `packages/engine/src/children/orchestration.ts`, which is
ADR-0014 rule 1's one 30 s allowance, `STOP_GRACE` in `packages/engine/src/run/grace.ts`): the current behaviour, unchanged
until the owner rules. At the ceiling the turn stops before its next model step, and a step in flight then has 30 s to end;
at that bound it is aborted, and its partial output reaches nothing but the transcript's reasoning rows. The report is
built from the last assistant message that carried text, the child ends `failed` with REQ-ORCH-088's timeout report, and
`PD-ORCH-004`'s cut-off lines and continuation offer follow where it was making progress.

**What a ruling decides.** How long a model step in flight at the ceiling may run to land — the same 30 s, the configured
`graceful_pause_tool_deadline`, a bound of its own, or until the step ends — and what is kept when the bound is reached:
nothing, as now; the step's partial text or reasoning in the child's report; or the partial step handed to the
continuation. A longer landing pushes back the ceiling REQ-CONFIG-113 calls hard, so either answer changes a requirement
or a directive; neither is a repair.

*Recorded 2026-10-06 (fin20, `fin20-continue-and-continuation`).* No code changed. The bound is reported back into
[`adr/0012-the-delegated-child-scheduler.md`](adr/0012-the-delegated-child-scheduler.md) and beside `CHILD_LANDING_GRACE`,
where its reason promised a report, and the note is closed as ruled as built.

**OQ-197 — Does a write of the permission mode that leaves the file's value unchanged displace an unsaved Settings
selection?** *(REQ-CONFIG-423, "for this one field the last write wins over an unsaved selection on this screen" and "a
change to the same field made while Settings is open by any other surface … lands in that pending state"; REQ-CONFIG-420, a
refresh never discards an edit in progress "with the single exception REQ-CONFIG-423 states for the permission-mode field,
where a mode already applied to a live run displaces an unsaved selection"; REQ-CONFIG-288, the composer's control writes
that key alone. Raised 2026-10-03 by the repair of
[`fixed/a-permission-mode-written-elsewhere-loses-to-an-unsaved-settings-selection.md`](../defects/fixed/a-permission-mode-written-elsewhere-loses-to-an-unsaved-settings-selection.md)
(fin13, bundle `fin13-settings-last-write-and-record-pointers`), as OQ-196, and renumbered OQ-197 at its merge of
`origin/main` because the landing-grace question had taken OQ-196 meanwhile. ~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** the current behaviour is kept: only a change of the saved permission mode displaces an unsaved Settings selection, and a write that leaves the file's value unchanged keeps it, as every other field's edit is kept. REQ-CONFIG-423's "last write" is read as a write that changes the field's value, as its own "a change to the same field" and REQ-CONFIG-420's exception have it, so `config:changed` keeps its contract and no directive is minted.

The screen learns of a write made elsewhere only from the reloaded snapshot main announces after it, and a snapshot carries
values, not the writes that produced them. Settings holding an unsaved `plan` over a saved `ask`, the composer writing `ask`
(the value the file already holds) yields a snapshot identical to the one a sign-in's reload yields; the two cannot be told
apart on the screen. REQ-CONFIG-423's "last write" read literally would have the composer's `ask` displace `plan`; its
"change to the same field" and REQ-CONFIG-420's "a mode already applied … displaces" read as a change of the value.

**What the build proceeds under** (`rebasePending`, `packages/ui/src/settings/config-state.ts`): a change of the value. A
reloaded snapshot whose permission mode differs from the one the screen last saved displaces the unsaved selection; one whose
mode is unchanged keeps it, as every other field's edit is kept (REQ-CONFIG-420). The composer shows the file's mode in that
case and Settings the unsaved selection until it is saved or discarded.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a write of the unchanged value must also displace the selection — which would need the
announcement to name the key a `config.setField` wrote (a contract change on `config:changed`) — or whether the change
reading stands.

**OQ-198 — Does `explicit_trivial` reach a request that changes nothing, and may the tie-break choose `moderate_feature`
where no build is plausible?** *(REQ-ORCH-006, which names `explicit_trivial` without a meaning and fixes only
`problem_resolution` ("diagnose AND fix"), `exploration` ("investigate only") and the tie-break ("when several categories
are plausible the tie-break prefers `moderate_feature`"); REQ-ORCH-021, which groups `explicit_trivial` with
`single_file_change` (micro) and apart from `question` and `exploration` (answer); REQ-ORCH-153, whose plan gate exempts the
answer group alone. Raised 2026-10-04 by the repair of
[`fixed/slice-proof-reds-on-live-model-answers-that-vary-run-to-run.md`](../defects/fixed/slice-proof-reds-on-live-model-answers-that-vary-run-to-run.md)
(fin15, bundle `fin15-slice-proof-live-answers`). ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** `explicit_trivial` means a small edit, and the tie-break chooses only among the plausible categories, so a request that changes nothing belongs to the answer group. [`PD-ORCH-011`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-011) narrows REQ-ORCH-006. The classifier's instruction is unchanged, and `slice-proof` now expects the answer group alone for its question (`INTENTS` in `apps/desktop/scripts/lib/live-answers.mjs`, pinned by `live-answers.test.ts`).

Against the registered self-hosted endpoint (`katalyst`, a model that reasons before it answers), the product's classifier
answered "What is the first heading of README.md?" with `question` in eight of the nine runs of 2026-10-03 that reached
it (runs 1, 3 and 5 to 10; run 2 went red before it), and with `explicit_trivial` (0.99, by the strict schema, no fallback)
in one, run 4. Every run of 2026-10-04 whose evidence this session keeps answered `question`. *(Corrected 2026-10-04 at the repair round:
this paragraph first said "five of the six runs … (runs 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7)", counting only the first seven runs' evidence
and missing runs 8, 9 and 10, which the record of
[`fixed/a-first-run-workspace-never-gets-the-starter-agents-yaml.md`](../defects/fixed/a-first-run-workspace-never-gets-the-starter-agents-yaml.md)
keeps.)* The product's own classification instruction calls
`explicit_trivial` and `single_file_change` "the two smallest edits" (`packages/engine/src/intent/classifier.ts`), but no
requirement does. The name says an explicit, trivial request, and a one-line question about one file is that. The group says
an edit. The two readings route the run differently. Under REQ-ORCH-021 the question takes the micro group's playbook
cells instead of the answer group's. In `plan` mode REQ-ORCH-153 holds it at the plan gate, which exempts the answer group
alone.

The tie-break leaves a second question. Read as a tie-break, it chooses among the categories that are plausible, so it never
brings `moderate_feature` into reach of a prompt no build is plausible for. Read literally, any prompt for which several
categories are plausible (the README question is one, on the first question's broader reading) should be classified
`moderate_feature`. The classification instruction passes the sentence on to the model in those words.

**What the build proceeds under.** The product classifies as it does; nothing here is a defect of the code. `slice-proof`
(`INTENTS` in `apps/desktop/scripts/lib/live-answers.mjs`, each prompt with its reason) accepts `explicit_trivial` for the
README question, because no requirement keeps it out. It reads the tie-break as a choice among the plausible categories, so a
`moderate_feature` that is not a fallback is still a red for the question and for the one-line append.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether `explicit_trivial` is meant for edits alone. If it is, a requirement says so, the
proof accepts the answer group alone for the question, and the classifier's instruction stays as it is. If it is not, the
instruction stops calling it an edit. A ruling also decides whether the tie-break may reach outside the plausible set.

**OQ-199 — May a run complete when its entry role ended without writing an answer?** *(REQ-ORCH-069, the run stops with
`tasks_complete` once every non-abandoned task is completed; REQ-ORCH-113, the completion classifier; REQ-ORCH-115, which
skips that classifier for reports attributed to the coordinator role; REQ-ORCH-079, relentless mode (default off), the only
check that compares the outcome with the request; REQ-TOOLS-180, a run terminates when the agent produces a message
addressed to the user and requests no tool call in that turn; REQ-ORCH-095, a child's ending assessed into six categories,
tool calls made counting as `work_performed`. Raised 2026-10-04 by the repair of
[`fixed/slice-proof-reds-on-live-model-answers-that-vary-run-to-run.md`](../defects/fixed/slice-proof-reds-on-live-model-answers-that-vary-run-to-run.md)
(fin15, bundle `fin15-slice-proof-live-answers`). ~~Open, the owner's.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-06.**)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** an execution iteration's entry role that ends its turn with neither
text nor a tool call is asked once more to answer, in its own conversation, as a delegated child is re-prompted; if it
still writes nothing, the run completes as before and the person is told it ended without an answer (a transcript row and
a warning `incomplete_execution` issue). A plan cycle's root is not asked. By
[`PD-ORCH-009`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-009), which extends REQ-ORCH-069.

Run 2 of `slice-proof` on 2026-10-03 (`katalyst`, load 2.5) asked "Read README.md in this workspace and tell me its first
heading, in one sentence." The intent was `question`. The orchestrator read `README.md` and globbed the workspace, both calls
settled, and then ended its turn with reasoning and no text. Its reasoning addressed requests the run never made: a list of
the installed skills, and a test suite under `src/core/parser.ts`. Neither string occurs in the product's prompts. The run
ended `completed` (`tasks_complete`) after 22 s. The transcript holds the person's message, three reasoning groups, two reads
and "The run completed." It holds no answer. The product did what the requirements say: the iteration ended, its task was
done, REQ-ORCH-115 skipped the completion classifier for the coordinator's report, and REQ-ORCH-069 stopped the run. No
requirement says a run that was asked a question must answer it before it completes. REQ-TOOLS-180 names the turn that
terminates a run (a message to the user and no tool call) and is silent on a turn with neither; the build reads it as the
condition that hands a message on, not as the only turn that may end a run. REQ-ORCH-095 assesses a delegated child's
ending, and the root execution record is not one (REQ-ORCH-072); even read across, two settled reads are
`work_performed`, which it accepts without a re-prompt
(`packages/engine/src/children/orchestration.ts`, where a re-prompt follows only an ending with no call and no text).

**What the build proceeds under.** The run completes as it did. `slice-proof` reports such a run as the model's, keeps its
evidence (`run.attempt-1.log`, `.png` and `.json`: the session, the row kinds, the reasoning; copied into
`.proof/slice-proof-answerless/`, where the next run does not remove it) and runs scenario 3 once more.
The second run is held to every check, and a second answerless run is a red that names both
(`answerlessCompletion` in `apps/desktop/scripts/lib/live-answers.mjs`).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an entry-role turn that ends with neither text nor a tool call should be told so and
continued, re-queued as `partial`, or reported to the person as a run that ended without an answer, rather than completing.
Each would add to REQ-ORCH-069, REQ-ORCH-113 or REQ-ORCH-115, so each is a revision or a directive, not a repair.

*Built 2026-10-06 (fin20, `fin20-continue-and-continuation`).* `Run.turn`'s follow-up (the one REQ-ORCH-078's correction
uses, `runWithChildren`'s `followUp`) sends `ANSWER_REPROMPT` once when the root's turn returned `succeeded` with empty text
and the run is not stopping, pausing or coming to rest (`correctionDue`), before any plan correction; a turn that still
returns empty text writes "The run ended without an answer: <role> ended its turn without writing one, even when asked
once more." as a `system` row and an `incomplete_execution` warning issue. Pinned by
`packages/engine/src/run/answerless.test.ts` (two of its three cases red before). `slice-proof`'s answerless rerun
(`answerlessCompletion`) is unchanged: an answerless run is now one whose root stayed silent after the re-prompt too, and
its transcript says so. *Corrected before landing (the verifier's review):* the row is written where what follows the
iteration is known (`Run.tellUnanswered`) — "The run ended without an answer: …" only when the run ends after it, and
"Iteration <n> ended without an answer: …" when the run goes on, parks or only pauses — and only the turn the re-prompt led
to is read, so a later plan correction's silent turn does not count; pinned by two more cases in `answerless.test.ts` and
one in `coordinator-plan.test.ts`, each red on the first form (PD-ORCH-009's first-execution report).

**OQ-200 — Which model call does the run timer count while a run has more than one?** *(REQ-CHAT-158, the run-timing
indicator counts "the time spent inside the model call currently in flight" and restarts "each time the run moves on to
the next model call within the same run"; REQ-ORCH-095 and the delegated children whose calls run beside the root's;
REQ-CHAT-063, the live-refresh rules the tick follows. Raised 2026-10-06 by
[`the-run-timer-counts-from-the-newest-row-not-from-the-model-call-in-flight.md`](../defects/fixed/the-run-timer-counts-from-the-newest-row-not-from-the-model-call-in-flight.md)
(fin18, bundle `fin18-rail-label-and-observations`). ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** confirmed at the reading the build proceeds under: while a run is active the run timer counts from the newest transcript row the run produced, the unsettled one first, so a call that writes no row does not restart it, and no call boundary is published on the record. It was raised on 2026-10-06, after the overview the owner answered, and is confirmed under the same instruction at the reading this entry says the build proceeds under. [`PD-CHAT-008`](../product/directives.md#pd-chat-008) narrows REQ-CHAT-158. Since no call boundary is owed, [`the-run-timer-counts-from-the-newest-row-not-from-the-model-call-in-flight.md`](../defects/fixed/the-run-timer-counts-from-the-newest-row-not-from-the-model-call-in-flight.md) closes with this ruling.

The default live run at `27a5127` captured the run header at a moment when the one call in flight was the transcript
summariser's, 5.5 s in, and the header read 0:09, counted from the newest transcript row. A run can have several calls out
at once: the root's, each running child's, a summariser's, a classifier's. REQ-CHAT-158 speaks of "the model call
currently in flight" as if there were one, and does not say whether a call the product makes for itself (a summary, an
intent or completion classification) is one of "the run's" calls.

**What the build proceeds under.** Unchanged: the value counts from the newest transcript row the run produced, the
unsettled one first (`modelCallStartedAt`, `packages/ui/src/composer.ts`), so a call that writes no row does not restart
it. No call boundary is published on the record (`SessionRecord` carries `runStartedAt` only); the note above records
that as a defect whatever the ruling.

**What a ruling decides.** Which call the value counts when more than one is in flight — the root's alone, the newest to
start, or the oldest still running (the one "taking an unusual length of time") — and whether the product's own calls
count. Each needs the engine to publish a call's start on the record, which is a contracts and engine change before it is
a surface one.

**OQ-201 — Do the repository card's "touched" and "uncommitted" take the Git view's definitions?** *(REQ-MONITOR-168, the
repository card states "how many files were touched and how many changes are uncommitted"; REQ-GIT-105, the Git view's
uncommitted-path count includes untracked paths so that it and the cleanliness gates of REQ-GIT-014 never disagree;
REQ-GIT-107, a worktree row's "files-touched" figure; REQ-GIT-003, the `.rotaris/` exclusion of every working-tree read
the Git domain performs. Raised 2026-10-06 by
[`the-repository-card-and-the-git-view-count-uncommitted-paths-differently.md`](../defects/fixed/the-repository-card-and-the-git-view-count-uncommitted-paths-differently.md)
(fin18, bundle `fin18-rail-label-and-observations`). ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** confirmed at the reading the build proceeds under: the repository card's "touched" counts every path `git status` lists, untracked ones included, and its "uncommitted" the tracked paths with a staged or unstaged change, with no `.rotaris/` exclusion; the Git view keeps REQ-GIT-105's count under REQ-GIT-003's exclusion, so the two may differ for one tree. It was raised on 2026-10-06, after the overview the owner answered, and is confirmed under the same instruction at the reading this entry says the build proceeds under. REQ-MONITOR-168 defines neither word, and REQ-GIT-003's consequences name the Git view's figures, not the card's, so this ruling settles it; [`the-repository-card-and-the-git-view-count-uncommitted-paths-differently.md`](../defects/fixed/the-repository-card-and-the-git-view-count-uncommitted-paths-differently.md) closes with it.

In one launch of the default live run at `27a5127` the Overview's repository card read "4 files touched · 2 uncommitted"
and the Git view counted 4 uncommitted paths in the same tree. The card counts an untracked path as touched and not as
uncommitted, and does not exclude `.rotaris/`; the Git view counts it as uncommitted and excludes `.rotaris/`.
REQ-MONITOR-168 defines neither word. If the card took REQ-GIT-105's count, "touched" and "uncommitted" would be the same
number for the base tree unless "touched" means something else — REQ-GIT-107's files figure is the nearest candidate,
and for the base tree it is the same set again.

**What the build proceeds under.** Unchanged: the card's touched is every path `git status` lists, its uncommitted the
tracked paths with a staged or unstaged change (`countStatus`, `packages/workspace/src/git/repository.ts`); the Git view
keeps REQ-GIT-105's count.

**What a ruling decides.** What each of the card's two figures counts — in particular whether an untracked path is
uncommitted on the card as it is in the Git view, and whether the card's read applies REQ-GIT-003's exclusion — so that
one window never shows two different "uncommitted" counts for one tree.

**OQ-202 — On an `explicit_trivial` or `single_file_change` run, may the coordinator use the direct-work bundle REQ-ORCH-016
grants it, or does REQ-ORCH-029 forbid every file-modifying call and every work item it does not delegate?**
*(REQ-ORCH-016, "Exactly the two simplest intents (`explicit_trivial`, `single_file_change`) grant the entry role the
direct-work bundle", which includes "every tool the public tool-name registry declares as … writing workspace files, or
running commands"; REQ-ORCH-029, which binds the entry role "while it acts as coordinator, which is every run except one taken
under a `single` override": "it makes no file-modifying tool call … every work item it takes on reaches a specialist through a
`delegate` call", constraints that "MUST hold no matter what playbook cell or instruction text is in force" and are
"externally checkable from the run's own records"; REQ-ORCH-025, under which only `single` ends the coordinating status.
Raised 2026-10-06 from finding G2 of the orchestrator's final default live run at `27a5127` (fin18, bundle
`fin18-run-record-truth`; raised there as OQ-200 and renumbered OQ-202 when origin/main, which had taken OQ-200 and OQ-201,
was merged in). ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

Under REQ-ORCH-016 an `explicit_trivial` or `single_file_change` run grants the entry role `write_file`, `terminal` and the
rest of the direct-work bundle; no `single` override is in force, so by REQ-ORCH-025 and REQ-ORCH-029 the entry role is still
the coordinator, and the coordinator makes no file-modifying call and delegates every work item. The two requirements give it
the tools and forbid their use at once. The orchestrator's built-in instructions state REQ-ORCH-029's side ("You coordinate:
you do not modify files or run commands yourself — every work item reaches a specialist through the delegate tool",
`packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`) while its listing carries REQ-ORCH-016's. Neither requirement names the other,
and no directive governs either.

In the default live run's `frictions` scenario (pack `.live-run/runs/2026-10-06T01-30-08-282Z/`, session `dc010fce`, the
self-hosted endpoint) the intent was `explicit_trivial` (0.98) and the orchestrator was offered 29 tools, `write_file`,
`terminal` and `haet_edit` among them (`frictions/model-traffic.jsonl` #1). Its first turn reasoned about the contradiction
("the guardrail says 'You do not modify files or run commands yourself' … Given the tension … do it directly", transcript
row 1): that request took 14,495 ms and 1,034 output tokens of a 32.0 s run, the longest of the run. It then made the
file-modifying call itself (#1 `write_file`) and four `terminal` calls, records REQ-ORCH-029 says must show no such call. The
same shape is in the `frictions` and `terminal` scenarios at `1763f7f` (2026-10-03), both `explicit_trivial`.

**What the build proceeds under** (the code as it stands; nothing changed for this question): REQ-ORCH-016's grant is
applied (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`, the entry port's `directWork`), the orchestrator's instructions keep
REQ-ORCH-029's sentence, and nothing refuses or flags the coordinator's use of a granted tool. A model that uses the bundle
is not stopped, and one that delegates is not either.

**What a ruling decides.** Which requirement gives way on the two simplest intents: whether the bundle's grant ends the
coordinating status for that run as `single` does (REQ-ORCH-029's exemption widened, and the instructions told so where the
bundle is granted), or whether the coordinator keeps it and the bundle is narrowed to what REQ-ORCH-029 allows (REQ-ORCH-016
amended); and, either way, whether the instructions the coordinator is given should name the case so it does not spend a turn
on the contradiction.

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** on the simplest runs the coordinator does the work
itself with the bundle REQ-ORCH-016 grants, and its instructions for that run say so, so the grant and the instructions agree;
the coordinating status stays, and REQ-ORCH-029 gives way only in its three clauses that forbid doing the work. Carried by
[`PD-ORCH-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-006), which narrows REQ-ORCH-029. The reading taken where the ruling leaves a
detail open: "the simplest runs" are every run whose mapping grants the bundle (with the built-in mapping
`explicit_trivial` and `single_file_change`; a `single` override carries the same grant and is told the same); `delegate`
stays in the bundle and may still be used; a prompt the configuration supplies is kept whole with the statement after it; and
a turn the plan gate holds, which REQ-ORCH-153 denies the bundle's writing tools, keeps the coordinating prompt. **Built
2026-10-06 (fin20):** `entryInstructionsFor` (`packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`) read by the root turn in
`packages/engine/src/run/run.ts`; cases in `children/personas.test.ts`, `run/preflight.test.ts` and `run/plan-gate.test.ts`;
`pnpm fetch-proof` reads the instructions its `explicit_trivial` launch received. *Since OQ-162's ruling was built beside
it (`PD-ORCH-005` revision 7 clause 40, fin20, before landing):* the grant the instructions are fitted to is the one the
iteration runs under (`Run.preflightInEffect`), so an iteration a continue by message resumes keeps the instructions of the
grant it started with, and the message's grant fits them from the next iteration; pinned by the fourth "OQ-162 as ruled"
case in `run/preflight.test.ts`.

**OQ-203 — Which items of the coordinator's own plan does REQ-ORCH-075's re-queue hold against a task: every non-terminal
item of the session's plan, or only those the task's own iterations left open?** *(REQ-ORCH-075, "when a report says
succeeded but the agent's own todo list still holds pending/in-progress items … the same top-level task MUST be re-queued
(not abandoned)"; REQ-ORCH-029, the coordinator "does not report the run successful while a todo item is non-terminal or
while a todo item's recorded state disagrees with what happened"; REQ-ORCH-067, each iteration does "work for that one
task only"; REQ-ORCH-077, the task abandoned at the consecutive-retry limit; REQ-TOOLS-144 and REQ-TOOLS-147, the plan is
the agent's own and session-scoped. Raised 2026-10-06 by the builder of fin18's repair of live-run finding G5, from its verifier's finding (bundle
`fin18-run-record-truth`; raised there as OQ-201 and renumbered OQ-203 when origin/main, which had taken OQ-200 and OQ-201,
was merged in). ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-06.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-06 by the owner ([R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071)):** confirmed at the reading the build proceeds under: a task answers for every open item of the plan that was not already open when it was first taken up (its plan cycle, else its first iteration), a record kept with the task, and for no other; a person's own addition to the plan during the task is held against it, and a `PENDING` item re-listed in the id-less shape is the re-listing task's. It was raised on 2026-10-06, after the overview the owner answered, and is confirmed under the same instruction at the reading this entry says the build proceeds under. [`PD-ORCH-012`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-012) narrows REQ-ORCH-075, and [`PD-ORCH-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-006) revision 2 reads REQ-ORCH-029's todo clause the same way.

The repair of `docs/defects/fixed/the-run-records-success-while-the-coordinators-own-plan-holds-a-pending-item.md` returns a
task to the pending queue when its root answers `succeeded` with an item of its plan open (REQ-ORCH-075). The plan is the
session's, not the task's: it outlives the task, the run and every iteration. An item a task was given up on with
(REQ-ORCH-077), or one an earlier run of the session left open, is therefore still `PENDING` or `IN_PROGRESS` when the next
task is taken up. Read literally, REQ-ORCH-075's "the agent's own todo list still holds pending/in-progress items" and
REQ-ORCH-029's "a todo item is non-terminal" hold that item against every later task: each is re-queued and given up on in
turn though its own work was done. That record disagrees with what happened, which REQ-ORCH-029's own other clause forbids,
and a later task's root is told to finish another task's work, which REQ-ORCH-067 forbids. No requirement says which items
belong to which task. The verifier reproduced the literal reading with a queued prompt (REQ-CHAT-040) behind a task given up
on: outcomes `partial, partial, abandoned, partial, partial, abandoned`, the second task's done work recorded as abandoned.

**What the build proceeds under.** A task answers for every open item of the plan that was not already open when the task
was first taken up, and for no other. Its first take-up is the plan cycle that planned it, where one did (REQ-ORCH-153: the
cycle is the coordinator's turn and its grants keep the todo state writable, so the plan it writes there is the planned
task's own); otherwise its first iteration in the session, the one no iteration row names it in yet. That take-up record is
kept with the planner task in the stored todo (`Task.planExcused`, `packages/engine/src/run/todo.ts`; `Run.planCycleTakeUp`,
`Run.takeUp` and `openPlanItems`'s `excused`, `packages/engine/src/run/`), so every later iteration of the task reads the same
record back: the one a continue resumes, and a fresh iteration of the re-queued task in the same run or a later one. A revise
cycle, and the plan cycle after a resumed iteration (PD-ORCH-003 revision 2), keep a record a task already carries. An item
the task's plan cycle wrote, one the task opened, or one its own earlier iteration left open, therefore always holds it; an
item a given-up task, an earlier run or anything else left open before the task was first taken up never does. The continuation that names the open items
(REQ-ORCH-075's marker) is kept with the task too (`Task.planLeftOpen`), goes to the same task's next fresh root only, and is
dropped when the task completes or is given up on. An excused item is not altered: it stays open in the plan the Todo pane
counts, and a run in which a task was given up on reads failed by REQ-ORCH-082 anyway. A task first taken up by a build
before this record existed has none, so every open item is held against it. Pinned by
`packages/engine/src/run/coordinator-plan.test.ts`. (The first form of this reading held the record in the run's memory, so
the run a continue built had none: an iteration it resumed held a given-up task's item against its own task, and a fresh
iteration of a re-queued task in a later run took the task's own leftover item as excused and completed beside it. The
verifier of fin18's second repair round reproduced both; the record has been kept with the task since. The second form took
the first iteration as the first take-up even in plan mode, so the items the plan cycle wrote were recorded as already open
and excused, and every plan-mode run read completed beside its untouched plan; the verifier of the third round reproduced it,
and the plan cycle has counted as the take-up of the tasks it plans since.)

**What a ruling decides.** Whether REQ-ORCH-075 and REQ-ORCH-029 range over the whole session plan (and a stale item then
blocks every later task, or must be closed by someone before the run can succeed) or over the items a task owns, and if the
latter, how ownership is decided and recorded: by what was open at the task's first take-up (as built, kept with the planner task), by a
mark on the item (REQ-TOOLS-144's schema has no field for it), or otherwise; and whether a person's own addition to the agent
plan (REQ-CHAT-090) during a task is held against it, as it is built now. Ownership by id meets one case the build cannot
tell apart: REQ-TOOLS-146's `replace` keeps a `COMPLETED`, `IN_PROGRESS` or `ABANDONED` item by id, but a `PENDING` item
re-listed in the documented id-less shape is given a new id (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/todo.ts`), so a `PENDING` item a
given-up task left, re-listed by the next task's root, stops being excused and counts against that task. A ruling decides
whether such a re-listed item is the new task's (it re-wrote it) or still the earlier task's.

**OQ-204 — When the expanded plan gate cannot hold all its parts, which clause of PD-ORCH-002 revision 2 yields?**
*(PD-ORCH-002 revision 2, over REQ-ORCH-153: expanded, the plan's own text "SHALL be the largest element of the surface and
the only element that grows with it: every other part of the gate is sized by its own content"; REQ-SHELL-022, the
1000x680 minimum; REQ-SHELL-048, every action reachable. Raised 2026-10-06 by
[`the-expanded-plan-gate-gives-the-whole-loss-to-the-plan-when-a-notice-shares-the-window.md`](../defects/fixed/the-expanded-plan-gate-gives-the-whole-loss-to-the-plan-when-a-notice-shares-the-window.md)
(finacc2, bundle `finacc2-accept1-6`). First committed as OQ-202 on the bundle's branch; origin/main had already taken
OQ-202 and OQ-203 (`ef1e6d9`, `6998e3f`), so it takes the next free number, OQ-204. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ **Ruled
2026-10-07.**)*

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** "largest" holds against every
part the product sizes. A later cycle's "You asked for" line is bounded like the implied todo (`max-height:
var(--rt-space-16)`). It scrolls inside itself and wraps long unbroken text, so the plan's floor stands above every part
the product sizes. A revision field the user drags taller keeps the height the user gave it and may then stand taller than
the plan, the one case where "largest" yields. When the area is shorter than the gate's parts with the plan at its floor,
the gate scrolls with its three answers pinned at its foot, as built. Recorded as
[`PD-ORCH-002`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-002) revision 3, one paragraph added and nothing replaced, with REQ-ORCH-153's
back-pointer amended in place.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: decide by who sized the part — cap the "You asked for"
line as the todo is capped, so the plan stands taller than every part the product sizes, and let a field the user drags
keep the user's height. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: the same layout — cap the line below the plan's floor, let the
drag stand, confirm the pinned-answers scroll — reached by refusing to choose between the directive's two clauses where a
layout keeping both exists, as the 2026-10-06 repair's verifier did. **The ruling followed both.** From A it took the
dragged-field reading and the amendment of REQ-ORCH-153's back-pointer in place; from B, that the cycle-2 reading must go
red on the CSS before the change, and that the error line (`composer__error`) is left as it is. The cap is the todo's own
token, so one bound serves both content-sized parts (B's whole-line cap was set aside).

On a short window the gate's row is less than its parts need: at 1000x680 with a 97 px persistent notice it is 261 px, and
199 px with the re-authentication bar as well. If every part but the plan keeps its content height and the plan has no
floor, the plan takes the whole loss (18 px beside the todo's 56 in finacc2's acceptance). The repair keeps both clauses
for every part with a bound: the plan has a floor above the todo's cap (72 px; in edit mode the adopted `textarea.input`
rule's 80 px), every other part keeps its content height, and the gate scrolls below that with its three answers pinned
(at 261 px: the plan 72, the todo 56, the gate scrolling 31 px). The revision field opened by its summary is bounded too:
at its default height (its summary, a step and a `textarea.input` at 80 px, which scrolls rather than grows with what is
typed) it measures 102 px, which beat the plan's 72 (preview) and 80 (edit mode) at 1000x680 with or without a notice, on
the ordinary path to Revise (the bundle's verifier, repair round 2). While that field is open the plan's floor rises to
`calc(var(--rt-space-24) + var(--rt-space-4))`, 112 px, in both modes (at 261 px: the plan 112, the open field 102, the
todo 56, the gate scrolling 151 px). That keeps the plan the largest of the parts that are bounded: the heading, the
intent sentence, the todo, the revision field closed or open at its default height, and the answers. Two parts have no
bound: a later cycle's "You asked for" line (`.plan-gate__prior`, the whole of the changes the user stated) and a revision
field the user drags taller than its default (`resize: vertical`). On a short window either can stand taller than the
plan's floor, and no floor fixed in advance is above a part with no bound. *(Corrected in repair round 2, 2026-10-06. The
entry first read: "Two parts have no bound: a later cycle's 'You asked for' line … and the revision field once opened,
which the user can drag taller". That put the open field at its default height among the unbounded parts; it is bounded,
and a layout keeping both clauses for it exists, so it is repaired rather than asked.)*

**What the build proceeds under.** The plan's floor is `calc(var(--rt-space-16) + var(--rt-space-2))` (edit mode:
`textarea.input`'s 80 px), above the todo's cap, the answers' row and the heading; while the revision field is open it is
`calc(var(--rt-space-24) + var(--rt-space-4))` in both modes, above the open field at its default height. Every other part,
the "You asked for" line and a revision field dragged taller included, keeps its content height, and the gate scrolls with
its three answers pinned to its floor; so on a short window either unbounded part may stand taller than the plan. (Until the bundle's repair round
1 the reading also let the todo yield first, down to its label's line; that chose between the two clauses where a layout
keeping both exists, and was withdrawn.)

**What a ruling decides.** Whether "largest" holds against parts the user wrote or sized (then they need a cap or their
own scroll, like the todo's), or "sized by its own content" holds for them (then "largest" is read over the gate's fixed
parts only). Also whether a gate that scrolls below its minimum, with its answers pinned, is the intended reading when
the window is shorter than the gate's parts.

**OQ-205 — What is a `swarm` run told on an intent the mapping grants the direct-work bundle: to do the work itself, or
to coordinate and delegate as widely as it can?** *(REQ-ORCH-025, a `swarm` override "demands maximum parallel
delegation … it changes instruction text only, and the entry role keeps its coordinating status and its
coordination-only tool set"; REQ-ORCH-016, "Exactly the two simplest intents (`explicit_trivial`, `single_file_change`)
grant the entry role the direct-work bundle … a `swarm` override is not an input to it";
[`PD-ORCH-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-006), which narrows REQ-ORCH-029 alone and tells the entry role a run
granted the bundle does the work itself. Raised 2026-10-06 by the repair of fin22's bundle `fin22-record-tidy`, from its
verifier's finding, beside
[`the-swarm-run-override-changes-no-instruction-text.md`](../defects/fixed/the-swarm-run-override-changes-no-instruction-text.md).
~~Open.~~ Ruled 2026-10-07, confirmed as built.)*

The two requirements meet on one run: a `swarm` override on an `explicit_trivial` or `single_file_change` intent (with
the built-in mapping). REQ-ORCH-016 grants that run the direct-work bundle, since `swarm` is not an input to the
mapping, and the bundle is not the coordination-only tool set REQ-ORCH-025 says a `swarm` entry role keeps. REQ-ORCH-025
demands maximum parallel delegation of the same run, while `PD-ORCH-006` tells a coordinator granted the bundle to do
the work itself; the directive names REQ-ORCH-029 only, so it does not by itself displace REQ-ORCH-025's "keeps its
coordinating status and its coordination-only tool set". Neither requirement names the case. A demand for delegation
beside the direct-work statement would put back the contradiction `PD-ORCH-006` removed (finding G2 of the default live
run at `27a5127`: a first turn of 14.5 s spent reasoning about tools it was told not to use).

**What the build proceeds under** (the code as it stands; nothing changed for this question): the grant follows
REQ-ORCH-016, so the `swarm` run on a granted intent holds the direct-work bundle with `delegate` in it
(`packages/engine/src/intent/gate.ts`, `intentGrant`; `apps/desktop/src/run-host/intent.ts`). Its entry role keeps its
coordinating status in REQ-ORCH-025's sense: it is not a `single` run, so `coordinating` holds
(`packages/engine/src/sessions.ts`) and `delegate` is not withheld (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`). Its
instructions are `PD-ORCH-006`'s, the direct-work statement, and no `swarm` text is rendered beside them, since the
build renders that text on no run (`entryInstructionsFor`, `packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`, reads no run
override; the defect note above). On every other intent a `swarm` run is today the same run as an `orchestrator` one.
*(Corrected 2026-10-06, finacc3, finding F07: the last two sentences no longer describe the build. On every intent the mapping
does not grant the bundle a `swarm` run is now told REQ-ORCH-025's demand, after its playbook (`withRunOverride`,
`SWARM_INSTRUCTION`); on a granted intent the build still renders no `swarm` text beside the direct-work statement, by a
deliberate check in `withRunOverride` rather than because no run reads the override. That is the reading this question
holds open. Corrected again in that bundle's repair round 1: the function is now `runOverrideLayer`, and `runTurn` places
its text after everything else the prompt carries, the MCP section included (`withRunOverrideLayer`); the check that keeps it
off a granted run is unchanged.)*

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a `swarm` override on a granted intent keeps the bundle and is told to do the work
itself (REQ-ORCH-025's coordination-only tool set and delegation demand yield on those intents, as built, carried by a
directive naming REQ-ORCH-025), or keeps the coordination-only tool set and the delegation demand (the grant withheld,
so `swarm` becomes an input to REQ-ORCH-016's mapping as `single` is, and `PD-ORCH-006` does not reach that run), or
keeps the bundle and is told both. The repair of the defect note can render REQ-ORCH-025's `swarm` text on the other
intents whichever way this is ruled; what it renders on the granted ones waits on the ruling.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** on every run where the
intent-to-tools mapping in force (the built-in mapping or a user's mapping file) grants the entry role the direct-work bundle,
a `swarm` override changes nothing the run holds or is told. The entry role keeps the bundle with `delegate` in it and is given
`PD-ORCH-006`'s direct-work statement. It is given no `swarm` text on any turn, including the turn the plan gate holds and any
continuation. [`PD-ORCH-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-006) revision 3 carries this by adding REQ-ORCH-025 to its
Narrows line. On every run the mapping does not grant, REQ-ORCH-025's `swarm` governs as written, and REQ-ORCH-016 and
REQ-ORCH-150 stay unchanged. **The two recommendations weighed:** advocate A (the user's lens) recommended confirming as built
through `PD-ORCH-006` revision 3, since the strategy is a standing workspace setting and the micro cell's one-item task has
nothing to fan out; advocate B (the system's lens) recommended the same confirmation, since withholding the grant would break
REQ-ORCH-016's "not an input", the Specification Gate's resolution 14 and REQ-ORCH-025's own "instruction text only", and both
texts together would restore finding G2. The ruling followed **both**, naming the plan-held turn and continuations, which
neither stated, and taking the owed built-app evidence now. **Confirmed as built 2026-10-07 (fin27):** no behaviour change
(`runOverrideLayer`, `packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`, returns nothing on a granted run); pinned by
`intent/intent.test.ts` (a `swarm` override keeps the grant of the built-in and of a file mapping), `children/personas.test.ts`
(no layer on a granted run, held or not), two `run/preflight.test.ts` cases (a file-mapping grant; a plan-mode granted run's
held turn and its first turn after approval), each red with the granted-run check removed, and
`tools/symbol-artifact/back-pointers.test.ts`; shown in the built app by `pnpm fetch-proof`'s launch 8, `swarm-granted`.

**OQ-206 — Which closes of a main window ask REQ-STARTUP-046's active-run confirmation, now that the instance holds several
main windows and a quit can start outside any window?** *(REQ-STARTUP-046, "When a run is active, a confirmation SHALL be
presented before anything is torn down", its text conveying "that closing the window ends it"; REQ-SHELL-119's third guard,
"with runs active, a user-initiated close asks 'Quit while a run is active?'"; REQ-STARTUP-161, several main windows in one
instance; REQ-STARTUP-047 with REQ-SHELL-018, the switch's close; `PD-ORCH-005` clause 3, a quit leaves unfinished agents
`paused`. Raised 2026-10-06 by the repair of
[`closing-a-window-while-a-run-is-active-asks-no-confirmation.md`](../defects/fixed/closing-a-window-while-a-run-is-active-asks-no-confirmation.md)
(fin22, bundle `fin22-window-strip-config`), which stayed open on it. Raised on that branch as OQ-205 and renumbered
OQ-206 at its landing, OQ-205 being the `swarm` question `fin22-record-tidy` raised first on main. ~~Open.~~ **Ruled
2026-10-07.**)*

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** closing a main window ends the
active runs of the project open in it, and asks REQ-STARTUP-046's confirmation first. The close of the last main window asks,
as built, while the run host counts any run active in the instance ("Quit while a run is active?"). The close of one of
several windows asks while that window's own workspace has a run active ("Close this window while a run is active?",
"…while {n} runs are active?"); its Yes stops those runs as the stop control does before the window closes (PD-ORCH-005
clauses 3, 9, 10 and 21: agents rest `paused` by `stop`, Continue resumes them, and approvals are withdrawn), and the stopped
runs' later notices are held back from the window that stays (REQ-STARTUP-046's last sentence). A window with no active run
of its own closes without asking. REQ-SHELL-021's gate 3 counts only the requesting window's workspace. A quit that starts
outside any window (a signal, the end of the desktop session, the driver's or the capture's quit) asks no active-run
confirmation, as built. Recorded as [`PD-SHELL-009`](../product/directives.md#pd-shell-009), which narrows REQ-STARTUP-046,
REQ-SHELL-119 and REQ-SHELL-122; the ruling also named REQ-SHELL-021, which PD-SHELL-001 already narrows and the symbol
generator admits one narrowing directive per requirement, so gate 3's change is carried through REQ-SHELL-122, whose test
the gate applies (found while building, 2026-10-07). *Reversed 2026-10-13 by [OQ-237](#oq-237) (GV1): `PD-SHELL-009` now narrows
REQ-SHELL-021 itself, as this ruling named it, beside `PD-SHELL-001`'s disjoint case; its REQ-SHELL-122 narrowing stays.
The reason in the sentence before no longer holds.*

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: ask at the close of a window whose own workspace has a
run active, with its own title, and have its Yes stop those runs, so that every active run always has a window and the box
is true wherever it is shown; leave a quit outside any window unasked. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: confirm as built —
ask only at the last window's close, where "closing the window ends it" is true — and record that as a directive narrowing
REQ-STARTUP-046 and REQ-SHELL-119. **The ruling followed A**: B's own risks (a run left executing where no window shows it,
its approvals opening over another project, the other window's switch refused about a run it never showed) are not the
product working under PD-SHELL-002, and PD-ORCH-005 makes the stop resumable. From B it kept: no question at a quit outside
any window, the corrected logout claim (on Windows, Electron emits no `before-quit` at a logout or shutdown —
[`a-windows-logout-skips-the-orderly-shutdown.md`](../defects/fixed/a-windows-logout-skips-the-orderly-shutdown.md), recorded, not
repaired by this ruling; built on a main window's `session-end` by fin29 the same day), a separate defect note for that, and the test of two windows closed in one gesture. macOS Dock Quit is a
person's quit outside any window and is to be reopened when a macOS release is authorized (IC-3, PD-STARTUP-001).
[`closing-a-window-while-a-run-is-active-asks-no-confirmation.md`](../defects/fixed/closing-a-window-while-a-run-is-active-asks-no-confirmation.md)
closes with it.

Both requirements were written when the instance held one main window and its close was the quit. Since REQ-STARTUP-161
the run host keeps executing while any main window stays, and the run host's count of active runs is instance-wide
(sessions are not keyed by workspace; REQ-SHELL-021's gate 3 and OQ-86 read it the same way). Closing one of two windows
ends no run, so REQ-STARTUP-046's sentence "closing the window ends it" would be untrue there; and the switch's outgoing
window closes while its replacement is shown, behind REQ-SHELL-021's gate 3, which already declines a switch while any run
is active. A quit Electron starts on its own account (SIGTERM, the desktop's logout, `app.quit()`, the driver's quit) closes
every window at once and is not a person's close of a window; REQ-SHELL-119 asks its third guard on "a user-initiated close".

**What the build proceeds under** (`confirmActiveRunClose`, `apps/desktop/src/main/close-confirmation.ts`; `guardClose`,
`apps/desktop/src/main/main-windows.ts`). A person's close of a main window — its close control, the title bar's Close
(PD-SHELL-003), the window manager's close — asks the confirmation after the renderer's unsaved-settings guard allows,
when no other main window stays open and the run host counts a run active (a count that cannot be read asks). The box
asks REQ-SHELL-119's question with Cancel and Yes, Cancel first, the default, and Escape's and the close control's answer
(REQ-SHELL-055); its detail conveys REQ-STARTUP-046's three things with REQ-SHELL-119's statement that shutdown is
requested and in-flight work may not finish. Only Yes closes; Cancel changes nothing, and a box that cannot be shown is
Cancel. With another main window staying, the close asks nothing, and the run keeps executing. A quit started outside any
window is not asked; its shutdown leaves the run as `PD-ORCH-005` clause 3 says.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the confirmation is asked on every close of a main window while any run is active
(and then what it says where the close ends nothing), only on a close that ends a run (as built), or on a close of the
window whose own workspace has a run active (which needs the run host's count keyed by workspace); and whether a quit
started outside any window — the desktop's logout above all — asks it.

**OQ-207 — What is a "mostly-elided artifact" in `summary.md`'s Warnings, and what record counts one?** *(REQ-SESSION-140's
Warnings section, which covers "stale-input drops, mostly-elided artifacts, report downgrades, permission denials …, tool
errors, and terminal failures, suspicious successes and timeouts"; REQ-SESSION-139, REQ-SESSION-133. Raised 2026-10-06 by
fin22 (bundle `fin22-summary-and-counts`) while repairing
[`summary-md-carries-none-of-the-sections-its-requirement-lists.md`](../defects/fixed/summary-md-carries-none-of-the-sections-its-requirement-lists.md);
the one gap it leaves stayed open in
[`summary-md-counts-no-mostly-elided-artifacts-until-oq-207-is-ruled.md`](../defects/fixed/summary-md-counts-no-mostly-elided-artifacts-until-oq-207-is-ruled.md)
until this was ruled. Raised on the branch as OQ-205 and renumbered twice as `origin/main` was merged in: OQ-206, since
main's OQ-205 (a `swarm` run on a granted intent) took that number first, then OQ-207, since main's OQ-206 (which closes of a main
window ask the active-run confirmation) took that one. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-07.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a mostly-elided artifact is an
artifact that a delegating agent attached to a delegated agent (`attach_artifacts`) and that the agent's
`PRIOR AGENT CONTEXT (FULL)` block left out because it did not fit the budget. The record that counts one is REQ-LIBRARY-098's
context-selection diagnostic, which the build writes as the timeline's `context_selection` entry, and each agent-and-artifact
pair counts once. `summary.md`'s Warnings line shows that count (`0` when nothing was left out) and says what it counts and
where it is counted from. [`PD-SESSION-002`](../product/directives.md#pd-session-002) extends REQ-SESSION-140 with this
definition and leaves out the sibling index's dropped entries and the continuation handoff's 6,000-character cut. The ruling
weighed two recommendations and **followed A**: advocate A (the user's lens) recommended defining the warning as an
attached artifact left out of the child's full-context block and counting it from `attached_elided`, as a directive;
advocate B (the system's lens) recommended confirming the `n/a` line as built, reading the warning as REQ-SESSION-133's
context-selection record that this store keeps no ring of. The diagnostic itself is kept, whole, on the uncapped timeline,
so B's `n/a` would hide a fact the store holds. A was corrected twice: the count is of distinct agent-and-artifact pairs, since
~~a REQ-ORCH-088 retry rebuilds a child's payload and writes a second entry~~ another execution of the same child (a resumed
child's REQ-ORCH-088 retry in a later run, or a follow-up of a child that never started) assembles its payload again and writes
a second entry, while a retry within one execution reuses the blocks it built (narrowed by fin30); and the conflict A noticed is wider than its wording,
recorded in [`the-attached-artifact-budget-is-48000-characters-where-req-tools-152-sets-100000-and-drops-every-later-one.md`](../defects/fixed/the-attached-artifact-budget-is-48000-characters-where-req-tools-152-sets-100000-and-drops-every-later-one.md).
"Mostly" here means "wholly", a cost the directive states. Built by fin28 (`elidedAttachmentsOf` and `warningLines` in
`packages/engine/src/run/summary.ts`, `StoreDal.elidedAttachmentRowsOf`); the note
[`summary-md-counts-no-mostly-elided-artifacts-until-oq-207-is-ruled.md`](../defects/fixed/summary-md-counts-no-mostly-elided-artifacts-until-oq-207-is-ruled.md)
is repaired.

Every other kind the Warnings section names has a definition and a record: a permission denial is an audit entry
(REQ-SESSION-137), a tool error and the three terminal outcomes are tool-call outcomes and issues (REQ-SESSION-136), and a
stale-input drop and a report downgrade are counts REQ-SESSION-139 takes over the model-input and report-validation records
(which this store does not keep: ADR-0024, the metrics document's `records_kept`). "Mostly-elided artifacts" appears in
REQ-SESSION-140 and nowhere else: no requirement says what eliding an artifact is, what share of it makes it "mostly"
elided, or which record would count one. The nearest thing the build has is a delegated child's payload, whose sibling
index and attached artifacts can be elided to fit its budget (`sibling_index_elided`, `attached_elided` in the
`context_selection` timeline entry, REQ-TOOLS-152 / REQ-LIBRARY-098; corrected 2026-10-07 from "`context_injected` timeline
metadata", a name the build never wrote); that is an artifact left out of a payload, not an
artifact mostly elided, and reading it as the warning would be inventing the definition.

**What the build proceeded under until the ruling** (superseded; kept as the record of it). The line is written and reads `n/a`, never `0` (REQ-SESSION-140's rule for an unavailable
value): `- Mostly-elided artifacts: n/a (no record measures how much of an artifact was elided)`, beside the stale-input
drops and report downgrades, which read `n/a` for the records the store does not keep (`warningLines` in
`packages/engine/src/run/summary.ts`).

**What a ruling decides.** What makes an artifact "mostly elided" (a share of its body cut from a payload or a view, and
which), which record counts it, and whether the warning is then built or withdrawn from REQ-SESSION-140.

**OQ-208 — Does an MCP tool call's record carry an `outcome_kind`, and is `mcp` one?** *(REQ-SESSION-136's record fields,
"`outcome_kind` … only when applicable"; REQ-SESSION-139's tool-outcomes histogram, "`outcome_kind` when the record carries
one, otherwise derived from `status` and `is_error` into rejected, tool-error, success or unknown"; REQ-TOOLS-112's
`outcome_kind` vocabulary, which names terminal observations only. Raised 2026-10-06 by fin23 (bundle
`fin23-summary-and-live-checks`) while repairing
[`summary-md-tool-errors-line-counts-one-outcome-bucket-not-every-tool-error.md`](../defects/fixed/summary-md-tool-errors-line-counts-one-outcome-bucket-not-every-tool-error.md),
at the orchestrator's question whether a bucket named `mcp` belongs among the tool outcomes. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled
2026-10-07.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** an `outcome_kind` names how a
call ended. A record carries one only when the specification gives its tool outcome words: the terminal's REQ-TOOLS-112
set, and the questions tool's REQ-TOOLS-158 outcomes together with PD-ORCH-005's `withdrawn`. `mcp` names a tool family, so
it is no outcome: an MCP tool call's record carries no `outcome_kind` and keeps its `failure_kind` (`tool_error`, `timeout`,
`execution_error`), and REQ-SESSION-139 derives its histogram bucket from `status` and `is_error` as `success` or
`tool_error`. The fetch tool's record falls under the same reading of REQ-SESSION-136's "only when applicable" and drops
`outcome_kind: 'fetch'`. Records already stored keep what they hold, and no directive, migration or reader shim is owed.
The ruling weighed two recommendations and **followed both** where they agree: advocate A (the user's lens) recommended
dropping `mcp` so the histogram stops hiding a failed MCP call (the c2a9444 duress run's `edit_memory` call inside
`mcp 17`), with fetch recorded as a defect; advocate B (the system's lens) recommended the same for MCP, since one tool's
failures landed in two buckets (a schema refusal in `tool_error`, a server failure in `mcp`), and ruling fetch with it.
On fetch it followed B. The terminal-worded timeout issue an MCP or fetch timeout files is recorded separately, in
[`an-mcp-or-fetch-timeout-files-a-terminal-timeout-issue-that-names-a-terminal-command.md`](../defects/fixed/an-mcp-or-fetch-timeout-files-a-terminal-timeout-issue-that-names-a-terminal-command.md)
(repaired by fin30: the message names the call that ran out of time).
Built by fin28 (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/mcp.ts`, `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/fetch.ts`); the fetch half is
[`a-fetch-calls-record-carries-its-tools-name-as-outcome-kind.md`](../defects/fixed/a-fetch-calls-record-carries-its-tools-name-as-outcome-kind.md).
*Beside this ruling since 2026-10-13 ([OQ-238](#oq-238), `PD-TOOLS-013` revision 2):* a fetch, an MCP call or any call its
run cancels carries failure kind `interrupted`, and REQ-SESSION-139 derives such a record, which still carries no
`outcome_kind`, into the bucket `interrupted` rather than `tool_error`. This ruling's reading of `outcome_kind` is unchanged:
no record gains one.

Until the 2026-10-07 ruling, every MCP tool call's record carried `outcome_kind: 'mcp'`, the call succeeding or failing alike
(`apps/desktop/src/run-host/mcp.ts`, the `execute` of each MCP tool executor the run host builds). The histogram followed REQ-SESSION-139's letter and
filed each under the bucket its record named, so `summary.md`'s Tool outcomes line and the metrics document read
`mcp <n>` beside `success`, `tool_error`, `invalid_request`: in the c2a9444 default live run's pack
(`.live-run/runs/2026-10-06T17-41-48-175Z/workspace.db`) the edit, requirements and terminal sessions each have such a
bucket. `mcp` names the tool's family, not how the call ended; a reader of the histogram could not tell an MCP call that
succeeded from one that failed. The specification does not say whether REQ-SESSION-136's "only when applicable" makes an
`outcome_kind` applicable to an MCP call at all, and gives an MCP call no outcome vocabulary of its own: REQ-TOOLS-112's
set (`success`, `shell_failure`, …) is the terminal's.

**What the build proceeded under until the ruling** (superseded; kept as the record of it). The record is left as it is and the histogram keeps REQ-SESSION-139's letter, `mcp`
bucket included. Nothing else depends on the answer since fin23: `summary.md`'s `- Tool errors:` line counts the issues
record's `tool_error` entries, which REQ-SESSION-136 files for a failed MCP call whatever its `outcome_kind`, and the
terminal counts read their own outcomes and issues.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an MCP call's record carries no `outcome_kind` (the histogram then derives `success` or
`tool_error` from `status` and `is_error`), carries one from a vocabulary the specification would name, or keeps `mcp` as a
bucket of its own.

**Recommendation** (added 2026-10-06 by fin25; for the owner, not a ruling): REQ-TOOLS-112's `outcome_kind` vocabulary is
the terminal's, the only vocabulary the specification gives the field, so under REQ-SESSION-136's "only when applicable"
an `outcome_kind` applies to a record whose tool has one, and an MCP call's record would carry none. REQ-SESSION-139 then
derives its bucket from `status` and `is_error`, `success` or `tool_error`, and the histogram tells an MCP call that failed
from one that succeeded. The build was not changed by this recommendation: it proceeded as stated above until the 2026-10-07 ruling.

**First live execution with MCP failures present, 2026-10-07** (the final duress live run at `a68f121`, pack
`2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` of the live worktree, session `e6747bd0`): as ruled. wave3b's two failed code-intelligence
`replace_content` calls, #377 and #378, carry `failure_kind: tool_error` and no `outcome_kind`; `summary.md`'s Tool outcomes
read "success 387, tool_error 16, rejected 0, unknown 0, suspicious_success 1", 404 calls in all with no `mcp` bucket, and its
Tool errors line, 16, equals the issues record's 16 `tool_error` entries — the first live run in which an MCP failure is
counted under the ruling. The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-209 — An error-path tool record's arguments are "truncated to 2000 characters", and paths and identifiers are "never
truncated": which governs, and what do the 2,000 characters measure?** *(REQ-SESSION-136, "On error, recorded args/result
are truncated to 2000 characters"; REQ-SESSION-194, which names "the truncated arguments and results of an error-path tool
record" among the cuts its marker governs and ends "Counts, identifiers, paths and timestamps are never truncated"; the
domain's resolution 21. Raised 2026-10-06 by fin23 (bundle `fin23-terminal-and-records`) on its verifier's finding against
the repair of
[`an-error-path-tool-record-cuts-its-arguments-and-result-without-the-cut-marker.md`](../defects/fixed/an-error-path-tool-record-cuts-its-arguments-and-result-without-the-cut-marker.md).
Raised on the branch as OQ-208 and renumbered OQ-209 when the branch was rebased onto `origin/main`, main's OQ-208 (an MCP
call's `outcome_kind`) having taken that number first. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation
([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)).)*

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** confirmed as built and minted as
[`PD-SESSION-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-session-003), which narrows REQ-SESSION-136 and REQ-SESSION-194. The
error-path 2,000 characters measure the arguments' JSON text. The arguments keep their shape, and only free-text values are
cut, longest first, each ending with `...` inside its own length. A path, identifier, count or timestamp is never cut, and
when those values alone pass 2,000 the record goes over the cap. The key name decides which values are kept whole, and this
product's `delegate` keys `inherited_context` and `attach_artifacts` join the keys kept whole, repaired as a defect
([`a-delegate-calls-sibling-and-artifact-ids-can-be-cut-in-an-error-path-record.md`](../defects/fixed/a-delegate-calls-sibling-and-artifact-ids-can-be-cut-in-an-error-path-record.md)).
The ruling weighed two recommendations and **followed both**, which agree: advocate A (the user's lens) recommended
confirming the reading, a directive, the two keys and a first-executions row — a path or an id cut short gives a false account
to the person reading the record after a failure; advocate B (the system's lens) recommended confirming the reading, a
directive and the two keys with no row — nothing in the product relies on 2,000 as a bound, and the key name is the only
test that reaches an MCP tool. Where they differ it follows B: no first-executions row is owed, the mechanism having run
before the ruling (`PD-SESSION-001`'s precedent). It adds one guard of its own: `cut.test.ts` classifies every argument key
of every built-in tool, and the seams view's tool path names `WHOLE_KEYS`. The ruling names the directive PD-SESSION-002;
it is `PD-SESSION-003` by the number the orchestrator assigned, OQ-207's directive taking PD-SESSION-002. Built by fin28.

A tool call's arguments are a JSON object whose key order the model chooses. REQ-SESSION-136 caps them at 2,000 characters
without saying what is counted (the object's JSON text, or each value), and REQ-SESSION-194 forbids truncating a count, an
identifier, a path or a timestamp. The two meet in two places. A cut of the JSON text from its head drops or cuts through
whatever the model serialised after a long value — a `path` after a 1,990-character `content` — which the first repair did
and the verifier found. And where a value that is a path or an identifier is itself longer than the cap (a deep path, a
long list of ids), no cut can meet both: the cap is exceeded or the path is cut.

**What the build proceeded under until the ruling, and confirmed by it** (`cutArguments`, `packages/engine/src/run/cut.ts`; `SessionWriter.settleToolCall`). The
2,000 characters measure the arguments' JSON text. The arguments keep their shape: an object stays an object with every key,
and only free-text string values are cut, longest first, each ending with REQ-SESSION-194's `...` inside its own length,
until the text fits. A value is a path, an identifier or a timestamp by its key — the key's last word is one of `path`,
`file`, `dir`, `cwd`, `url`, `uri`, `id`, `slug`, `ref`, `hash`, `name`, `at`, `timestamp`, `time`, `date`, `since`,
`until` (or their plurals), or the key is one of this product's own `persona`, `supersedes`, `depends_on`,
`continuation_of`, `write_scope` — and it is never cut, nor anything beneath it; a number, a boolean and null are never cut.
Where what is kept whole cannot fit on its own, every free-text value is cut to the marker alone and the record exceeds
2,000 characters: "never truncated" is read as governing over the cap. A value that only mentions a path (a command
line, a free-text result) is free text and is cut; the result, a single text, is cut from its head as before.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the 2,000 characters measure the JSON text or each value; whether the cap or "never
truncated" yields when a path or an identifier is longer than the cap; and whether a key-name reading of "path, identifier,
timestamp" is the test, or the tool's declared schema should say which arguments are which.

**OQ-210 — Is a published artifact's `body_markdown` the submitted body or the rendered document, and may the submitted body
be stored twice?** *(REQ-LIBRARY-087, which keeps each artifact's Markdown document "on disk as a file the record references
and never holds inside itself"; REQ-LIBRARY-090, that document's rendering; REQ-LIBRARY-093, "whose `body_markdown` is the
submitted body unchanged, whose `key_findings` is that same body"; REQ-LIBRARY-094, REQ-LIBRARY-099 and REQ-LIBRARY-134, which
read and write the one or the other; REQ-SESSION-002, the per-session files. Raised 2026-10-06 by finacc3's acceptance round 1
(finding F16), repairing
[`records-and-code-comments-describe-ruled-questions-as-open-and-cite-questions-never-raised.md`](../defects/fixed/records-and-code-comments-describe-ruled-questions-as-open-and-cite-questions-never-raised.md):
the artifact store's first execution (Part U) said it raised this tension, in `packages/engine/src/artifacts/sidecar.ts` and in
[ADR-0003](adr/0003-files-are-the-system-of-record.md)'s execution note ("Open question, not a settled reading"), and no entry
was ever written, so the owner was never asked. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation.**)*

REQ-LIBRARY-087 fixes the on-disk document as REQ-LIBRARY-090's rendering and forbids the record holding it; REQ-LIBRARY-093 says
a publish's `body_markdown` is the submitted body unchanged. Both cannot be literally true of one stored thing without a second
place to store the submitted body, which neither requirement provides.

**What the build proceeds under** (`packages/engine/src/artifacts/store.ts` `publish`, `sidecar.ts` `renderSidecar`). The
record's `body_markdown` is the document: the file the record names (`body_file`) holds REQ-LIBRARY-090's rendering, and the
submitted body survives unchanged inside it as the Key Findings section and in the record's `key_findings` column, so the
submitted body is stored twice, once in the column and once in the file. REQ-LIBRARY-099's section filter reads the record's
columns and never parses the document; REQ-LIBRARY-094's edit overwrites the document and nothing else, so after an edit the
column keeps the body as published; REQ-LIBRARY-134's fallback for an empty stored body is the same rendering.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether `body_markdown` is the rendered document (as built) or the submitted body, with the
rendering derived; whether the submitted body may be kept both in `key_findings` and in the document; and whether an edit of
the document should also reach `key_findings`.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the body is the document, as
built, and a person's edit of it survives and travels. An artifact's `body_markdown` is its document on disk, created as
REQ-LIBRARY-090's rendering. A publish keeps the submitted body unchanged in two places, `key_findings` and the document's Key
Findings section (which now drops only the blank lines around it, where it was trimmed, so a first line's indentation
survives), and a person's edit changes only the document: `key_findings` and every other column keep their published values
(REQ-LIBRARY-094). A saved edit survives every later re-render, which rewrites only the document's leading frontmatter, and it
is what the product passes on: the follow-up handoff carries an edited artifact's document marked `edited`, and the inspector's
Preview shows every document starting below its frontmatter. Minted as
[`PD-LIBRARY-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-library-003), which narrows REQ-LIBRARY-093 and REQ-LIBRARY-095 and extends
REQ-SESSION-115 and REQ-LIBRARY-132. **The two recommendations weighed:** advocate A (the user's lens) recommended a change of
behaviour, confirming the first two points and making the edit survive a re-render and reach the handoff, without a
directive; advocate B (the system's lens) recommended confirming as built with a directive that narrows REQ-LIBRARY-093's
`body_markdown` clause, and repairing the re-render that overwrites an edit. The ruling **followed both**: B's directive and
re-render repair, A's handoff, read-failure rule and indentation catch, and it added the Preview's start below the
frontmatter; it left out A's optional notice on a section-filtered read. The defect both found,
[`a-re-render-writes-over-a-persons-saved-artifact-edit.md`](../defects/fixed/a-re-render-writes-over-a-persons-saved-artifact-edit.md),
was repaired by bundle `fin28-artifacts` the same day (`ArtifactStore.rerender`, `latestArtifactText`, the inspector's
`previewSource`).

**OQ-211 — Is an artifact's consumer recorded as the reading agent's persona or as its instance?** *(REQ-LIBRARY-099, "every
successful read marks the reading persona as a consumer"; REQ-LIBRARY-096, "marking an artifact consumed appends the actor at
most once and persists"; REQ-LIBRARY-093, whose `created_by` names "the publishing agent instance by its canonical name rather
than by its persona, so two instances sharing a persona stay distinguishable in every artifact listing"; REQ-MONITOR-044,
REQ-MONITOR-052 and REQ-MONITOR-069, whose received-artifact links read the consumers. Raised 2026-10-06 by finacc3's
acceptance round 1 (finding F16), repairing
[`records-and-code-comments-describe-ruled-questions-as-open-and-cite-questions-never-raised.md`](../defects/fixed/records-and-code-comments-describe-ruled-questions-as-open-and-cite-questions-never-raised.md):
`ArtifactStore.markConsumed`'s comment (`packages/engine/src/artifacts/store.ts`) said this was "raised as an open question
rather than settled here", and no entry was ever written. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's
delegation.**)*

REQ-LIBRARY-099 names the reading persona; REQ-LIBRARY-096 names the actor, without saying whether that is a persona or an
agent instance.

**What the build proceeds under** (`markConsumed`, and the artifact port's `artifact_read` in
`packages/engine/src/artifacts/port.ts`). The consumer recorded is the reading agent's canonical instance name, the name
REQ-LIBRARY-093 gives `created_by`: a child's canonical name, and a root's `root_canonical_name` (since the repair of
[`a-roots-publish-names-its-persona-as-its-author.md`](../defects/fixed/a-roots-publish-names-its-persona-as-its-author.md),
