2026-09-29). REQ-LIBRARY-093's reason, that two instances of one persona stay distinguishable, applies as much to who read an
artifact, and the persona can be recovered from the instance where the reverse cannot. The agent surfaces' received links
(REQ-MONITOR-044/052/069) match an agent's consumer entries by that name. Two instances of one persona that read one artifact
are two consumers.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the consumer is the instance (as built) or the persona, and so whether two instances of one
persona reading an artifact record one consumer or two.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** confirmed as built. Every
successful `artifact_read`, filtered or full, records the reading agent instance as a consumer, at most once, by its canonical
name (the name REQ-LIBRARY-093 gives `created_by`: a child's canonical name, a root's `root_canonical_name`); two instances of
one persona that read one artifact are two consumers, and the agent surfaces' received links (REQ-MONITOR-044/052/069) read
these names. Because REQ-LIBRARY-099 and REQ-TOOLS-148 say "the reading persona", the ruling is minted as
[`PD-LIBRARY-004`](../product/directives.md#pd-library-004), which narrows those two requirements' consumer clause; REQ-LIBRARY-096's
"actor" is read as the instance within its text. **The two recommendations weighed:** advocate A (the user's lens) and advocate
B (the system's lens) both recommended confirming as built with a directive — A because the received links show exactly what
the store holds and a persona would make them wrong whichever way they matched, B because the persona can be derived from the
instance and not the reverse, and the persona reading would undo OQ-125's confirmed reading. The ruling **followed both**,
keeping A's test that a child of the entry persona does not credit the run-level agent, and declining B's first-executions
row, since no mechanism ran for the first time. Built by bundle `fin28-artifacts` the same day as records, comments and three
pinning tests (`artifacts/artifacts.test.ts`, `ui/src/inspector-links.test.ts`), each green on the build as it stood.

**OQ-212 — Which built-in personas may publish an artifact?** *(REQ-TOOLS-001 and REQ-TOOLS-002, the names a persona may
declare, `artifact_write` among them; REQ-TOOLS-004, which removes `artifact_write` "declared by a persona that lacks
`can_publish_artifacts: true`"; REQ-CONFIG-106, `can_publish_artifacts` "(bool, default false)", without which the role is not
handed the tool; REQ-TOOLS-007; REQ-ORCH-016, whose direct-work bundle names `artifact_read` and `artifact_list` and not
`artifact_write`; REQ-ORCH-028's role vocabulary, which names the built-in roles and not their tools; REQ-LIBRARY-097 and
REQ-LIBRARY-101. Raised 2026-10-06 by finacc3's acceptance round 1 (finding F16), repairing
[`records-and-code-comments-describe-ruled-questions-as-open-and-cite-questions-never-raised.md`](../defects/fixed/records-and-code-comments-describe-ruled-questions-as-open-and-cite-questions-never-raised.md):
`packages/contracts/src/roles.ts` said "that no built-in persona does is recorded as an open question", and no entry was ever
written. ~~Open, the owner's.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation.**)*

The specification defines the tool, its gate and its prerequisite, but no built-in persona's tool list, so it does not say
whether any built-in role publishes.

**What the build proceeds under** (`BUILT_IN_ROLE_TOOLS`, `packages/contracts/src/roles.ts`). No built-in persona declares
`artifact_write`, and the direct-work bundle does not add it, so with the shipped defaults no agent publishes an artifact
through the tool: the artifacts in a session are the child reports the engine materialises (REQ-LIBRARY-092), and a
workspace's personas publish only where its configuration declares `artifact_write` for them (the artifacts proof declares it
for its orchestrator). `artifact_read` and `artifact_list` join every persona's read group. Whether that configuration also
needs `can_publish_artifacts: true`, as REQ-CONFIG-106 and REQ-TOOLS-004 say, is not this question: the build hands the tool
over whatever the flag says, recorded as a defect (repaired with this question's ruling, below),
[`can-publish-artifacts-is-read-and-never-gates-artifact-write.md`](../defects/fixed/can-publish-artifacts-is-read-and-never-gates-artifact-write.md).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether any built-in role (the orchestrator, the planner, the architect, the codebase analyst, the
librarian or another) declares `artifact_write` and carries `can_publish_artifacts: true` by default, or publishing stays a grant
a workspace's configuration gives.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** confirmed as built. No built-in
persona declares `artifact_write` or carries `can_publish_artifacts: true`, so with the shipped defaults a session's artifacts
are the child reports the engine materialises (REQ-LIBRARY-092). A workspace grants a role publishing through its configuration
with both keys REQ-CONFIG-106 names: `artifact_write` in the role's `tools:` list, restated in full (REQ-CONFIG-101), and
`can_publish_artifacts: true` beside it. Wherever the flag is false the tool is withheld and the removal recorded as
`artifact_publish_not_granted` (REQ-TOOLS-004, REQ-TOOLS-150). The ruling departs from no requirement's text, so **no
directive** was minted (OQ-52's precedent). **The two recommendations weighed:** advocate A (the user's lens) recommended
confirming as built, since the user already receives every specialist's work as a child report and a built-in publisher would
write each body twice and add duplicate Library rows, and repairing the gate alongside; advocate B (the system's lens)
recommended confirming as built, since three requirements treat publishing as a deliberate grant and no requirement names a
built-in publisher, which makes the gate repair a pure subtraction. The ruling **followed both**, taking the concrete steps
from each. **Built by bundle `fin28-artifacts` the same day:** `Persona.canPublishArtifacts` (false for every built-in role),
carried by `personaResolverFor` and read by `createToolPort` in place of the store's presence, repairing
[`can-publish-artifacts-is-read-and-never-gates-artifact-write.md`](../defects/fixed/can-publish-artifacts-is-read-and-never-gates-artifact-write.md);
a pinning test that no built-in role declares the tool or carries the flag (`children/personas.test.ts`); and the artifacts
proof's orchestrator granted with both keys, with a launch (3b) that declares the tool without the flag and finds the
removal in the session log at warning and no artifact stored, which passed.

**OQ-213 — Which todo list does REQ-ORCH-029 hold the coordinator to on multi-step work, what is "more than one step", and
how is the clause held "no matter what … instruction text is in force"?** *(REQ-ORCH-029, "work spanning more than one step is
accompanied by a todo list it keeps current", a constraint that "MUST hold no matter what playbook cell or instruction text
is in force" and is "externally checkable from the run's own records"; REQ-ORCH-004 and REQ-ORCH-068, the planner plan the run
writes and resolves itself; REQ-TOOLS-144 and REQ-TOOLS-147, the `todo` tool's list, the agent's own and "the run's primary
progress display"; REQ-ORCH-059, "Open-todo reminder lines are appended"; REQ-ORCH-025, `single`; REQ-CONFIG-100, a configured
`system_prompt`. Raised 2026-10-07 from live-run finding K2 of the final default live runs (packs at `c2fdd6a` and
`c2a9444`): on 3 of the 6 multi-step runs (edit, resume, frictions) the coordinator delegated more than once and wrote no plan
of its own, the task-plan strip read "Planner plan" with one row, the prompt itself, and the inspector read "todo not used";
on the requirements and terminal runs it planned unasked. Recorded as
[`the-coordinator-keeps-no-todo-list-of-its-own-on-multi-step-work.md`](../defects/fixed/the-coordinator-keeps-no-todo-list-of-its-own-on-multi-step-work.md),
repaired by fin27. Ruled the same day.)*

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the todo list REQ-ORCH-029
requires of the coordinator is its own plan, the one the `todo` tool writes; the run's planner plan does not satisfy the
clause. While the entry role acts as coordinator in an execution iteration and holds `todo`, the run refuses at dispatch the
call that would start the current task's second work item until the entry role has made an accepted `todo` write for that
task, and logs each refusal as a warning citing REQ-ORCH-029. A work item is a `delegate` call, or on a direct-work grant a
call of a tool the registry declares as writing workspace files or running commands. Nothing is seeded from the planner plan,
and REQ-ORCH-059's open-todo reminder lines are built so the coordinator sees its open items as children finish. No directive:
this builds REQ-ORCH-029 as written, and `PD-ORCH-006` already keeps the todo clause on direct-work runs. Two readings are this
entry's ruling: the list is the agent plan, and "more than one step" means the task's second work item. If a later round treats
the work-item reading as a narrowing, it lands as a revision of `PD-ORCH-006`, the one narrowing slot REQ-ORCH-029 admits.

The consortium weighed two recommendations. **Advocate A** (the user's lens) read the clause the same way and proposed a
reminder the run injects into the result of the task's second work item while the coordinator keeps no plan for it, logged as
a warning, rejecting both a refusal (red refused rows and an extra model step on healthy runs) and seeding the list from the
planner plan. **Advocate B** (the system's lens) proposed the refusal at dispatch, held through the entry port's gate beside
REQ-ORCH-153's plan-gate check, with the work-item count and the write kept with the planner task as `planExcused` is. **The
ruling followed B**: A's reminder is still text, which REQ-ORCH-029 says may not decide the question, and the live packs show
the persona text skipped on half the multi-step runs; the specification already holds such limits with refusals at dispatch
(REQ-ORCH-030, REQ-ORCH-153), and a gate refusal settles `blocked`, files no `tool_error` issue, fires at most once per task and
never on a coordinator that already planned. From A it took the logged warning line, the test that a configured
`system_prompt` is still covered, and the reading of "step" as a work item. The engine glossary's "Todo list" names the planner
plan, and the specification uses the phrase for both lists, so the glossary gains a separate "Agent plan" entry.

**As built** (fin27, 2026-10-07). The planner task keeps two facts in the stored todo beside `planExcused`, so a continue and
a later run read them back, both removed when the task completes or is given up on: `workItems`, the task's work items that
reached execution in its execution iterations, and `listWritten`, set by an accepted root `todo` write after the task's take-up
that leaves the agent plan holding at least one task (for the current iteration's task; in the plan cycle that plans the task,
for every task it plans). A person's own edit of the plan never sets it. `Run.todoListOwed` answers the refusal while the run
coordinates (`RunDeps.coordinating !== false`), outside a plan cycle (whose calls neither count nor are refused), when the
task already has a work item and no list; the depth-0 context carries it, and the entry port hands it to the gate only where
the entry role's resolved tool set holds `todo`, the run warning once otherwise and refusing nothing. The gate refuses after
the plan-gate check and before the schema parse: `blocked`, `failure_kind: todo_list_owed`, no `tool_error` issue; a step's
calls dispatch in order, so a `todo` write earlier in the step satisfies the check. Two places where the build reads the
ruling's text, stated so the next round can see them: a work item is **counted when it reaches execution** (past the schema,
the permission and the pre-execution hooks), not when it passes this check, so a call refused for another reason starts no
work item; and a tool the registry carries **no declaration** for (an MCP or plugin tool) is no work item, the ruling counting
what the registry declares. *A third, added 2026-10-07 (fin29, from fin27's review):* the ruling's "test that a configured
`system_prompt` is still covered" is read **at the entry port** (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.test.ts`, "a configured
system_prompt does not lift it"), where the persona's configured text is resolved, and not at the engine, whose scripted runs
carry no persona text; the refusal reads no instruction text at all, so the port is where a replaced text could matter. `completionNotification` appends up to five of the parent's open plan items (REQ-ORCH-059): the
root's are those its task answers for (`openRootPlan`), a child parent's its own todo's. Pinned by
`packages/engine/src/run/coordinator-plan.test.ts`, `packages/agent-tools/src/gate.test.ts`,
`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.test.ts`, `packages/engine/src/children/notify.test.ts` and
`packages/engine/src/children/children.test.ts`, and shown in the built app by `pnpm mission-proof` item 1c; the proofs whose
scripted coordinator delegates more than once open with the scripted client's `plan` step; the live run's harness checks it
over every session it keeps (`apps/desktop/scripts/lib/coordinator-todo.mjs`). The first-executions row waits on the orchestrator's next default live run.
*Amended 2026-10-07 by OQ-220's ruling (`PD-TOOLS-006` revision 6, fin29):* the refusal text (`TODO_LIST_OWED_TEXT`) now ends
"…; its result gives each item's id. Then make this call again, and on a delegate call to a persona that writes workspace files
give todo_item: the id of the item it serves." It read, until then: "…, one item per step with only the step you are on
IN_PROGRESS, then make this call again."
*Amended again by OQ-249's ruling (`PD-TOOLS-008` revision 2, `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 7, fin33):* it now reads "Write one with
the todo tool, one item per piece of work, with only an item you work on yourself IN_PROGRESS and the items you will delegate
PENDING; its result gives each item's id. Then make this call again, and on a delegate call give todo_item: the id of the item it
serves, which the call marks IN_PROGRESS." It read, until then: "Write one with the todo tool, one item per step with only the
step you are on IN_PROGRESS; its result gives each item's id. Then make this call again, and on a delegate call to a persona that
writes workspace files give todo_item: the id of the item it serves."

**First live execution, 2026-10-07 (the final default live run at `a68f121`, pack `2026-10-07T06-48-50-123Z`, the registered
self-hosted endpoint):** the refusal held as built. It fired three times in the ten sessions: edit `#7` (a `delegate`, in the
same step as a `todo` that REQ-TOOLS-145 refused in `PD-TOOLS-008`'s wording), resume `#2` (a `delegate`) and frictions `#2`
(a background `terminal` call on a direct-work grant). Each settled `blocked` with `failure_kind: todo_list_owed`, filed no
`tool_error` issue and logged one warning citing REQ-ORCH-029; each coordinator recovered with exactly one `todo` write and
then the refused call, two model steps, about 19.5 s, 9.5 s and 6 s on the critical path, and none looped or re-planned
twice. The requirements and terminal coordinators planned before their first delegation and were never refused. The five
multi-step sessions stored an agent plan, and the task-plan strip read "Agent plan" (3/3, 4/4 and 3/3 done) with "todo used".
No scenario check failed because of a refusal. **Not reached:** REQ-ORCH-059's open-todo reminder lines, since every
coordinator waited in the foreground with `wait_for_tasks`, whose report block carries none. **Found**, as the pack's
findings, not as defects of this ruling: P3, where REQ-TOOLS-145's single `IN_PROGRESS` refuses the plan of two parallel
delegations and under this ruling that refusal leaves the same step's second `delegate` refused too (the model then
split the write from the call, reading nothing in the refusal that says a same-step write counts); and P7, a harness
finding, where the resume scenario's Pause now lands on one running child instead of two because the second delegation
starts one refusal later. The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-218 — Is REQ-MONITOR-286's per-agent timeout a control, and where does it stand?** *(REQ-MONITOR-286, the three
"interface-level delegation controls", the per-agent timeout "presented in minutes" and initialised from its policy value;
REQ-CONFIG-322, Delegation limits as "two numeric controls"; REQ-CONFIG-256, REQ-CONFIG-263 and REQ-CONFIG-417, the written
keys, the Tier B overlay and destination 1, none naming it; REQ-CONFIG-113 and REQ-ORCH-088, `runtime.child_timeout` in
seconds, 1200 by default; REQ-MONITOR-169, the Overview caps caption. Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live runs' findings —
both duress autopsies (`c2fdd6a`: three of seven children cut off at 1200 s, 66 % of the run behind the ceiling; `c2a9444`:
61.5 %) — as the consortium's question T1, and recorded here as OQ-218, the number the round assigned it.
[`no-surface-presents-the-per-agent-timeout.md`](../defects/fixed/no-surface-presents-the-per-agent-timeout.md) records the
gap. ~~Open.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

No surface shows the per-agent timeout: Settings › Runtime › Delegation limits draws the depth cap and the fan-out limit,
the advanced runtime card shows a key only when a file states it, and the caps line is count against cap. Whether
REQ-MONITOR-286's third item is a control a user moves (then a third Delegation limits control, which departs from
REQ-CONFIG-322's two and from the three enumerations that omit the key), a figure shown read-only, or a figure on the
Overview caps line, the specification does not settle.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** Settings › Runtime › Delegation
limits presents the per-agent timeout as a third numeric control, "Per-agent timeout", in whole minutes clamped 1–240. It is
initialised from the effective `runtime.child_timeout`, so a default install reads 20. It writes minutes × 60 seconds to
`runtime.child_timeout` through Save and the Tier B overlay, the same way as the depth cap and fan-out limit beside it. A
stored value the control cannot express is shown clamped for display with its exact seconds stated beneath, and is never
rewritten until the user changes the field (REQ-CONFIG-446). The Overview caps line keeps REQ-MONITOR-169's caption. Recorded
as [`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003), which narrows REQ-CONFIG-322, REQ-CONFIG-256 and REQ-CONFIG-417
and extends REQ-CONFIG-263 (the ruling named 256 and 417 as extended; PD-WORKSPACE-002 already extends both and the symbol
generator admits one directive per verb, so they are named as narrowed — found while building). *Revised 2026-10-13 by
[OQ-237](#oq-237) (GV1): Narrows is the verb these two take on the exact-enumeration test (acceptance finding F15), not by force of the
generator, and `PD-WORKSPACE-002` now narrows both as well; the reason in parentheses no longer holds.*

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: a third Delegation limits control in whole minutes,
1–240, writing seconds through Save and Tier B, minted as a directive; the caps line unchanged. *Advocate B (the system's
lens)*: a read-only row in minutes under Delegation limits naming the key and the file to edit, recorded as a reading with no
directive, since REQ-CONFIG-322 and the three enumerations list the editable set exactly. **The ruling followed A**:
REQ-MONITOR-286 names controls a user moves and initialises them from policy values, and the 1200 s ceiling the duress runs met
is kept only because a user can raise it. From B it kept the exact seconds on screen where the field cannot show them, a hint
saying the limit bounds delegated agents, and the defect note on the unlisted analysis-timeout control
([`the-improvement-analysis-timeout-control-writes-a-key-no-settings-list-names.md`](../defects/fixed/the-improvement-analysis-timeout-control-writes-a-key-no-settings-list-names.md),
recorded, not repaired). The 240-minute ceiling is a chosen figure, twelve times the default; a file can still state a longer
value.

**First live execution of the default case, 2026-10-07** (the final duress live run at `a68f121`, pack
`2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` of the live worktree, session `e6747bd0`, the self-hosted endpoint): as ruled. The run host logged
`child_timeout=1200 s` (`duress/app.log` lines 13 and 24), and the two working children were cut off at 1,200 s — wave3 landing
at the ceiling +4.25 s, its continuation wave3b at +0.44 s. NOT REACHED: the control, which the live harness never sets and no
launch captured, so the relief this ruling offers — a person raising the limit — is still unmeasured against a real model.
Reported in place in [`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003); the row is in
[`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-220 — Which todo item does a delegation answer for?** *(REQ-ORCH-028 and REQ-ORCH-029, "no two implementation delegations
for the same todo item are outstanding at once"; resolution 15 (b) of `docs/spec/resolutions/01-run-orchestration.md`, ownership
"per todo item and at no other granularity"; REQ-TOOLS-144, the plan's schema; REQ-TOOLS-152, the `delegate` call's
arguments. Raised 2026-10-07 by fin27's build of OQ-213's ruling, at that ruling's instruction. Numbered past the
round's assigned OQ-213 to OQ-219. ~~Open.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

OQ-213's refusal makes a multi-step coordinator keep a todo list of its own, which is the precondition for REQ-ORCH-029's
per-item constraint, not its measurement. A `delegate` call names no todo item (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/delegation.ts`),
and neither the child ledger nor the plan's items record one, so whether two outstanding implementation delegations serve one
item or two cannot be read from the run's records, which REQ-ORCH-029 says each of its constraints must be.

**What the build proceeds under.** The constraint is instructed and not measured: nothing refuses or records a second
implementation delegation for one item, as before OQ-213.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a delegation names the todo item it serves (a `delegate` argument, a field on the plan's
item, or a link the run infers), whether a second implementation delegation for an item already served is refused at dispatch,
and what a delegation that names no item counts as.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a delegation names the todo item it
serves in one optional `delegate` argument, `todo_item`: the id of a task in the caller's own plan. The id is stored on the
child's record, and the call is refused `rejected` when the plan holds no such task. An implementation delegation (REQ-ORCH-028)
is refused `rejected` at admission in three cases: its item is COMPLETED or ABANDONED; another non-terminal implementation child
of the same plan holds the item; or it names no item and comes from the coordinating entry role after that role has written its
todo list for the task (OQ-213's `listWritten`). A delegation that names no item serves no item and holds nothing, so a task's
first work item is the only unnamed implementation delegation the coordinator can make; a continuation inherits the item of the
child it continues, and a `session_id` follow-up keeps its stored item. Recorded as
[`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) **revision 6** (the ruling text names it revision 5; AB1's ruling,
OQ-221, built first in the same bundle, is revision 5, and the round assigned this one revision 6). The dispositions stay as
they are: it narrows REQ-TOOLS-152 and REQ-TOOLS-154 and extends REQ-ORCH-028. The held-item refusal builds REQ-ORCH-028 and
REQ-ORCH-029 as written and needs no directive, following OQ-213's precedent; if a later round reads "a delegation made before
the list serves no item" as a narrowing of REQ-ORCH-029, it lands as `PD-ORCH-006` revision 3, the one narrowing slot
REQ-ORCH-029 admits. The build lacked any way to hold or read the per-item constraint, recorded as
[`no-delegation-names-the-todo-item-it-serves-so-one-item-can-hold-two-implementation-delegations.md`](../defects/fixed/no-delegation-names-the-todo-item-it-serves-so-one-item-can-hold-two-implementation-delegations.md).

**The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed both.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)* recommended that the
coordinator names the item at the call: an optional `todo_item` stored on the child's record; once the coordinating entry role
keeps a list, an implementation delegation names an item from it; one naming an item another outstanding implementation child
holds is refused `rejected`; one made before any list serves the task as a whole, is recorded with no item and blocks none.
*Advocate B (the system's lens)* recommended the same mechanism, with an unnamed implementation delegation serving no item and
admitted only until the coordinator has written its list. Only the coordinator knows which item a delegation serves, so the link
belongs in the call, where the run can still refuse before a child is paid for; inferring the item conflicts with REQ-TOOLS-144
(names need not be unique) and REQ-TOOLS-145 (one item IN_PROGRESS), a field on the plan's item is written too late to refuse,
and recording without refusing leaves the clause on instruction text, which OQ-213's ruling rejected under REQ-ORCH-029. Where
the advocates differed the ruling followed B: a follow-up reads no `todo_item` (OQ-131) and keeps its stored item; the
held-item refusal comes from REQ-ORCH-028 and binds any caller naming an item of its own plan; a terminal item is refused to
implementation work, so the plan never shows COMPLETED work still under way. From A it took the unknown-id refusal for every
delegation (REQ-TOOLS-152's `inherited_context` precedent) and the harness checks. Both advocates missed that `PD-TOOLS-006`
revision 4 had landed for OQ-216, and that a model cannot name an id its own step creates, so `delegate`'s description and
OQ-213's refusal text tell it to write the list first. A refusal that misfires costs one model step (17.7 to 19.6 s measured);
a duplicate costs a whole child, up to 1,200 s.

*Built 2026-10-07 (fin29, `fin29-delegate-admission`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 6.* Store
v34's `children.todo_item`; `admitTodoItem` (`packages/engine/src/children/todo-item.ts`) called by `IterationChildren.delegate`
before the spawn and by `followUp` for the held check; `Run.todoPlanFor` reads the caller's plan and `listWritten`; the run
host injects `implementationRole` (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`); `delegate`'s `todo_item` and its description sentence
(`TODO_ITEM_SENTENCE`); `TODO_LIST_OWED_TEXT` names the ids (OQ-213's entry quotes the text it replaced); the live run's
`todoItemReading` (`apps/desktop/scripts/lib/coordinator-todo.mjs`). Shown in the built app by `pnpm mission-proof` item 1e.
**What a live run then shows:** every implementation child the coordinator spawns after its first accepted root `todo` write
carries a `todo_item` naming an item of its agent plan (only a task's first delegation, made before any list, carries none); no
two implementation children holding one item are outstanding at once; a continuation, such as the duress run's d2, carries the
item of the child it continues; `rejected` delegations for an unnamed, unknown, finished or held item are counted, the target
at most one per run, each followed on the next step by a delegation that names an item; the harness's coordinator-todo check
reports all of these.

**OQ-216 — Is the coordinator told which personas hold a terminal or a file-writing tool?** *(REQ-ORCH-028, a routing table
from need to role, with two capability clauses (`codebase-analyst` "reads the workspace but does not modify it", `librarian`
"likewise does not modify the workspace") and no persona's tools; REQ-TOOLS-001, the three facets every public tool declares;
REQ-TOOLS-006, the controls that narrow a grant; REQ-TOOLS-152, `delegate`'s fields; REQ-CONFIG-100, a configured
`system_prompt` replacing the built-in one; `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 3, which refuses a `write_scope` for a persona that holds
no file-writing tool and names the ones that do. Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live runs' findings L4 (the `c2fdd6a`
duress autopsy) and N3 with N2 (the `c2a9444` duress autopsy), recorded in
[`the-coordinator-is-not-told-which-personas-hold-a-terminal-or-a-file-tool.md`](../defects/fixed/the-coordinator-is-not-told-which-personas-hold-a-terminal-or-a-file-tool.md),
and ruled the same day under the owner's delegation; the consortium's question L4.)*

In both duress runs of 2026-10-06 the orchestrator briefed `docs-writer` children, which hold no `terminal`, to "Run
`node --test` yourself in the terminal". At `c2a9444` the two failed children (2,443.5 s of the critical path) spent 22 of
57 and 23 of 35 rows reasoning about the missing shell, one wrote `.tmp-run-tests.sh` as a workaround, and the answer to the
user said the continuation "ran the suite". At `c2fdd6a` the brief appeared twice, a child called a `run_command` tool that
does not exist, the coordinator wondered whether `verifier` had a shell, and the answer blamed the timeouts on the missing
shell. Each run spent 34 to 37 s on two `write_scope` refusals, `codebase-analyst` given a write task in both. Nothing the
coordinator reads states a persona's tools: the built routing table names roles, and `delegate`'s description was a fixed
list of the built-in names. The specification does not say whether the coordinator is told.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** `delegate`'s description is
built for each calling agent from the persona catalogue. It names every persona that agent can delegate to, with the
REQ-TOOLS-001 facets (reads workspace files, writes workspace files, runs commands) that a child of that agent would be
granted after REQ-TOOLS-006's controls, and it tells the caller to ask a persona only for work its tools allow; revision 3's
write-scope refusal stays as built. By [`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) revision 4, which already
extends REQ-ORCH-028 and narrows REQ-TOOLS-152: the symbol generator admits one directive per requirement for each
relation, so a new directive extending REQ-ORCH-028 could not be built. *(No longer so since 2026-10-13, [OQ-237](#oq-237): Extends
may repeat freely; the revision stays where it landed.)* Separately, the built routing table carries the two
capability clauses REQ-ORCH-028 states for `codebase-analyst` and `librarian`; that repair is covered by REQ-ORCH-028 and
needs no directive
([`the-built-routing-table-drops-req-orch-028s-capability-clauses.md`](../defects/fixed/the-built-routing-table-drops-req-orch-028s-capability-clauses.md)).

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended building `delegate`'s description per caller from the resolved catalogue,
  each persona with the facets its child grant would hold, telling the caller to brief a persona only for work its tools
  allow, recorded as `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 4 with the write-scope refusal kept. The ruling followed A on the vehicle and
  on the record: revision 4, not a new directive.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same per-caller catalogue, generated from the same resolution that
  builds the child's grant, and found what A missed: the built routing table drops REQ-ORCH-028's own clauses for
  `codebase-analyst` and `librarian`, the role given write tasks in both runs. The ruling followed B on restoring the
  clauses as covered work, on the run host computing the facets from the child's own grant resolution (the engine and
  `agent-tools` do not import each other), and on the equality test between the catalogue and the grant a child receives.
  B's proposed new `PD-ORCH` directive was not followed, since the generator refuses it.

Both advocates rejected a refusal for this case: the request to run a command sits in free text, and REQ-TOOLS-001 never
infers a facet from prose. Both rejected the system prompt as the vehicle: REQ-CONFIG-100 replaces it whenever configuration
supplies one, and it cannot apply each caller's `tool_restrictions` (OQ-145). The statement is advice and enforces nothing;
whether it removes the impossible briefs is measured at the next duress live run.

*Built 2026-10-07 (fin27, `fin27-delegate-and-summariser`).* The routing table carries REQ-ORCH-028's two clauses (`ROUTING`,
`packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`). `delegate`'s description is the caller's catalogue: `delegateCatalogue` and
`resolveAgentGrant` in `apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`, rendered by `renderDelegateCatalogue` in
`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/delegation.ts`. The first execution found nothing against the ruling and stated three readings
in `PD-TOOLS-006`'s report: the facets include what REQ-TOOLS-004's prerequisites remove (a run with no terminal backend
tells the caller no persona runs commands); `git_commit`, having no executor, never reads as a writer; the catalogue names
`orchestrator`, which the ledger accepts. Pinned by `delegation.test.ts`, `run-host/tools.test.ts` (each known role's facets
told equal to its child port's grant) and `personas.test.ts`. ~~**Not yet measured:** the duress live run that counts briefs
asking a persona without a terminal to run commands (2 to 3 per run before; target 0) and `write_scope` refusals (2 per run;
target 0).~~ **Measured 2026-10-07 at `a68f121` (the duress live run, session `e6747bd0`, finding D3):** the catalogue was in 35 of
35 coordinator requests; one `write_scope` refusal remained, against 2 per run before (`#115` gave `architect`
`docs/decisions.md`; the refusal answered in 170 ms naming the writers, and request 77 re-briefed a docs-writer in 19.4 s); one
impossible brief remained, against 2 to 3 before (`#114` offered `node --test` to a docs-writer, which called `run_command`,
`#164`, refused at the gate in a 2.5 s step; issues 3 and 4); 16 of 117 docs-writer requests carried a one-sentence missing-shell
aside, against 22 to 23 rows per failed child before; no stray file, no impossible brief on a failed child's path, and the answer
claimed no test run. The default run at `a68f121` chose by facet in 71 of 71 requests. **The target stands at 0, and its first
reading is falsified for revision 4 alone:** revision 4's catalogue did not by itself bring either count to zero, because the
routing table sent the work a route implies to the route's persona (the same task went to `codebase-analyst` at `c2fdd6a`, `#107`,
and to `architect` here). OQ-250 rules the next step, `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 8, measured against the same target.
~~The `write_scope` refusal target: 0 per run.~~ **Falsified 2026-10-13 and replaced by a bound ([OQ-257](#oq-257), ruled under
[R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** at the duress run at `552d346`, with revision 8's routing sentence in 41 of 41 coordinator
requests, one refusal remained (`#92`, `architect` given `docs/decisions.md`, refused in 5 ms before any record and re-routed by the
next `delegate` 30.0 s later); a target of zero for one stochastic sample is replaced by an enforced, recovered bound — at most one
`write_scope` refusal for a non-writer per duress run, each refused before any record exists and re-routed by the coordinator's
next request. The impossible-brief target stays at 0 (0 at `552d346`).

**OQ-217 — What is the report summariser told of how the child ended?** *(REQ-ORCH-088, a timed-out child recorded failed
with a report of the form "Child timed out after <N>s"; REQ-ORCH-108, the report condenses what already happened;
REQ-ORCH-110, the pass's bounds and its fallback, silent on what the pass is given; REQ-ORCH-112, the report status mapped
to the terminal state; OQ-111, which gave the pass the run's deterministic facts; OQ-120, the facts' 12,000-character bound
keeping its head; `PD-ORCH-004`, the cut-off statement. Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live runs' findings L5 (the
`c2fdd6a` duress autopsy) and N5 (the `c2a9444` duress autopsy), recorded in
[`a-timed-out-childs-report-summary-reads-as-success.md`](../defects/fixed/a-timed-out-childs-report-summary-reads-as-success.md),
and ruled the same day under the owner's delegation; the consortium's question L5.)*

Two of the five timed-out children of the two duress runs got summaries that read as success beneath status `failed`:
"The agent completed the requested documentation task" (`c2fdd6a`) and "The agent reconciled documentation …" (`c2a9444`).
The pass is given the task, the most recent part of the transcript and OQ-111's facts, and not the status or the end
reason, which the run decides before the pass runs (`packages/engine/src/children/orchestration.ts`). The artifact copies
neither the errors nor `cut_off`, so the sentence is the only place on its paths a cause could stand. The specification
does not say what the pass is told of the outcome.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the report summariser is told how
a failed child ended. For every child the runner settles other than `succeeded`, the facts it is given open with an Outcome
line: the runner's status, its end reason as the run recorded it and, for a child cut off while making progress,
PD-ORCH-004's statement. The pass is asked to state that outcome in the summary's first sentence, then condense what the
agent did, and never to call the task completed. A succeeded child's request stays as it is, the no-model fallback stays as
REQ-ORCH-110 states it, and no summarising pass can raise a status the runner settled as failed. This fills REQ-ORCH-110's
silence on the pass's inputs, as OQ-111 did, and needs no directive: REQ-ORCH-088, REQ-ORCH-108, REQ-ORCH-110,
REQ-ORCH-112 and PD-ORCH-004 keep their text. The status guard brings the build into line with REQ-ORCH-088 and
REQ-ORCH-112 as written
([`the-summarising-pass-can-raise-a-failed-childs-report-status.md`](../defects/fixed/the-summarising-pass-can-raise-a-failed-childs-report-status.md)).

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended giving the pass the run's status and recorded end reason as one more
  runner-owned fact beside OQ-111's, the summary stating the outcome in its first sentence and then what the child did,
  the status staying the run's. The ruling took A's wording on what remained: the summary says what the transcript shows
  was left, and never claims more was left undone than it shows, since a timed-out child's work may be whole.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same Outcome line at the head of the facts, so OQ-120's head-keeping
  cut never drops it, the plumbing for the cut-off statement, and a guard in `shape` so a pass can never raise a failed
  child's status. The ruling took all three. It departed from B on one point: a succeeded child gets no Outcome line,
  because the runner's `succeeded` means only that the turn ended with an answer, and stating it would invite a completion
  claim over a child whose answer was that it could not do the work.

Both rejected a label beside the summary (it leaves the false sentence stored), a run-written prefix or a separate reason
field (each needs a directive over REQ-ORCH-111 or REQ-LIBRARY-088), and confirming the behaviour as built. OQ-111 is the
precedent: its facts took report denials from 5 of 7 to 0 of 6 with this model.

*Built 2026-10-07 (fin27, `fin27-delegate-and-summariser`); its first execution, reported here as the ruling's record.*
`reportFacts` opens a non-succeeded child's facts with `outcomeLine`'s Outcome line, the ask gains the three sentences when it
is present, `shape` keeps a non-succeeded child's status, and `orchestration.ts` hands PD-ORCH-004's statement on as
`ReportInput.cutOffStatement` (`packages/engine/src/children/report.ts`, `orchestration.ts`). The first execution found
nothing against the ruling and settled two readings it left to the build. "Outcome: failed" is written with the status the
runner settled, since a cancelled child never reaches the pass (it takes the fallback) and `failed` is the only other status
a pass sees; and where the run recorded no end reason the line reads "Outcome: failed" alone, which a child whose turn
failed with no report of its own can produce. Unit cases in `report.test.ts` (the line and the instruction, the reasons'
words, the head kept past the 12,000-character bound, the status guard; each red on the code before) and the two PD-ORCH-004
cut-off cases in `children.test.ts` (the request a scripted run sends carries the line, with the statement and without it).
**Not yet measured:** the duress live run, which should show every failed child's summarising request opening its facts with
"Outcome: failed — Child timed out after 1200s" (and the statement where the child was making progress), each such stored
summary stating the limit in its first sentence and claiming no completion, every such report's status `failed`, and
OQ-111's count of zero denials holding.

*First live execution, 2026-10-07: the duress live run at `a68f121` (pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` of the live worktree,
session `e6747bd0`; its autopsy's L5 verdict and finding D9), reported here with the repair it led to (fin32).* **It held.**
The two failed children, `wave3-verify-all` and its continuation `wave3b-finish-verification`, both cut off at the 1200 s
limit while making progress, were summarised from facts opening "Outcome: failed — Child timed out after 1200s." with the
cut-off statement; both stored summaries opened with the timeout and claimed no completion; both reports and both
`child_end` records read `failed`. **Two things were wrong beside it, neither in the ruling.** (1) wave3b's facts also read
"Edited files: (none)" over 11 `ok` edits through the code-intelligence EDIT tier, so its summary called the edits
"attempted": the Outcome line was right and the fact it sat beside was false — PD-ORCH-004's changed-paths reading (finding
D1), repaired by fin32
([`a-child-that-edits-through-the-code-intelligence-edit-tools-is-reported-as-having-changed-nothing.md`](../defects/fixed/a-child-that-edits-through-the-code-intelligence-edit-tools-is-reported-as-having-changed-nothing.md)).
(2) Both summaries opened "The run failed because the child [agent] timed out after 1200s …", and the timeline relayed them
as "Child wave3-verify-all reported failed: The run failed because …" (entries 74 and 98) while the session completed
`tasks_complete`: the sentence the ruling asked for read as the session failing (finding D9). **The repair, inside the
ruling:** the line now says whose outcome it is — "Outcome of this agent, not of the session: failed — Child timed out after
1200s." (`OUTCOME_HEAD`, `packages/engine/src/children/report.ts`) — and the ask names the agent, asks for the first sentence
as what happened to the agent ("This agent was stopped at its time limit while …"), and forbids opening with "The run failed"
or "The session failed", since the session may continue and succeed. The reading taken in the first execution above,
"'Outcome: failed' is written with the status the runner settled", is kept with its new head. Pinned by `report.test.ts`'s
case "OQ-217's first sentence is the agent's own outcome …" and the updated line cases there and in `children.test.ts`, red
on the wording before ([`a-timed-out-childs-summary-opens-as-if-the-run-failed.md`](../defects/fixed/a-timed-out-childs-summary-opens-as-if-the-run-failed.md)).
**Not measured:** a live run since the repair; it should show each failed child's summary opening with the agent and its own
outcome, and no "The run failed" on the timeline of a session that completed. The row is in
[`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

*2026-10-13 (fin42, the survey's N50): the live measurement written, not run.* No live run had cut a child off since the
repair (the 552d346 duress pack: 0 failed children at a 2,700 s limit). `live-run.mjs`'s opt-in `cutoff` scenario sets the
Per-agent timeout to one minute through Settings and gives one child more work than that, then reads, for every child cut
off: the recorded summarising request carrying "Outcome of this agent, not of the session: failed — Child timed out after
60s." with the agent's name, the stored summary's first sentence stating the limit and not opening "The run failed", and no
`child_result` entry relaying "The run failed" when the session completed (`apps/desktop/scripts/lib/cut-off-reading.mjs`,
pinned by its test against the engine's `OUTCOME_HEAD`). It is the orchestrator's to run (`--only=cutoff`); a child the
limit never reaches is a NOTE there.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** the repair's live measure,
**NOT REACHED**. No child failed or timed out in any of the three packs, so no summarising request opened its facts with an
Outcome line and no timeline entry could read "The run failed". Found nothing, because nothing met the case. Evidence:
[`live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md), [`live-552d346-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-default-autopsy.md), [`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-214 — Does a working child's 1200 s ceiling stay when a model that reasons before it answers fills each life with
generation?** *(REQ-ORCH-088, the child timeout and its expiry path; REQ-CONFIG-113, `runtime.child_timeout`, default 1200;
REQ-NOTIFY-100; REQ-MONITOR-121; REQ-ORCH-062 and REQ-TOOLS-156, which forbid a separate deadline on a wait because every
child is bounded; REQ-ORCH-093, each parent resume bounded by it; REQ-ORCH-144, the per-role stall threshold for slow
models; [`PD-ORCH-004`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-004) revisions 1 to 5, R-048's limit kept and R-071's 30 s landing
(OQ-196). Raised 2026-10-07 from findings L1 of the orchestrator's duress live run at `c2fdd6a` (pack
`2026-10-06T16-02-48-699Z` of the live worktree) and N4 of its duress live run at `c2a9444` (pack
`2026-10-06T17-59-41-271Z`), the self-hosted reasoning model, and ruled the same day.)*

The two duress runs cut five working children off at the ceiling while each was making progress: at `c2fdd6a` d (reconcile),
e (decisions) and d2 (d's continuation), at `c2a9444` d (reconcile) and d-continuation. Each landed 0.39 to 26.7 s after the
ceiling (+7.3, +0.39, +26.7, +1.44, +7.23 s), none aborted; every report carried the cut-off statement and its changed paths;
the three that were not continuations carried revision 5's offer with its sentence, and the two continuations carried none
(read from the packs' `children` rows). Reasoning was 76 to 96 % of the children's output, mean steps 18 to 43 s. Of the eight
continuations made since 2026-09-29, five succeeded; the three that failed all continued the reconcile item. f succeeded at
1,087 s, 91 % of the ceiling. The children's time went largely to work other rulings own: d reasoned about a terminal it does
not hold in 22 of its 66 requests at `c2fdd6a` and its successor in 23 of 35 at `c2a9444` (L4/N3), d2 named `.serena`,
`.rotaris` or `.git` in 37 of its 45 requests (L3/N6, OQ-215), d-continuation met the empty file an undone create left (N2,
repaired, [`undoing-a-create-leaves-an-empty-file.md`](../defects/fixed/undoing-a-create-leaves-an-empty-file.md)), and e had a
complete file by minute five.

**What the build proceeds under.** `runtime.child_timeout`, default 1200 and minimum 1
(`packages/config/src/sections/runtime.ts`), handed to the run (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/configuration.ts`); the timer and
`CHILD_LANDING_GRACE`, the run's one 30 s allowance (`packages/engine/src/children/orchestration.ts`); one continuation, never
chained (PD-ORCH-004).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the default rises, the ceiling extends while the child makes progress, the ceiling scales
with the model, a continuation may be chained or longer, or the ceiling stands as R-048 and R-071 left it.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the working child's ceiling stays
as ruled. `runtime.child_timeout` keeps its 1200 s default and its hard bound with the 30 s landing, a piece of work is
continued once and never chained, and PD-ORCH-004 (revisions 1 to 5), R-048 and R-071 stand unrevised. The five cut-offs of the
2026-10-06 duress runs were each handled as written and are reported back into PD-ORCH-004 as revision 5's live execution.
The question reopens on new evidence: either (a) once the marker-directory (L3/N6, OQ-215) and personas'-tools (L4/N3) rulings
are built, a live run cuts off both a child and its continuation while each spent more than half its requests on its own task,
or (b) any child of a default live run reaches the ceiling. **The measure for (a)** is the autopsy's per-request
classification as L1 and N4 counted it: a request counts as off-task if its reasoning addresses a tool the child does not hold,
the code-intelligence marker directory, or a file outside its brief; on-task otherwise. **The two recommendations weighed:**
advocate A (the user's lens) recommended confirming the ceiling as built, since the long children were circling problems more
time would only multiply, and reporting the two runs back into PD-ORCH-004 with a two-lives reopening test; advocate B (the
system's lens) recommended the same confirmation, since REQ-TOOLS-156, REQ-ORCH-062 and REQ-ORCH-093 rely on the hard bound,
PD-ORCH-004's progress test passes a looping child and the model did not predict the hits, with a reopening criterion measured
per request. The ruling followed **both**: A's report-back, made mandatory by revision 5's "evidence owed", and A's two-lives
test measured by B's per-request count. Two facts stay on record as risk: f succeeded at 91 % of the ceiling, and no surface
presents the setting (REQ-MONITOR-286), which is OQ-218's question. **Recorded 2026-10-07 (fin27):** no code, test, view or
specification text changed; PD-ORCH-004's report-back and its row in `first-executions.md` are written. Findings L1 and N4
close as ruled.

**Reopened and ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** reopened under
condition (a) by finding D2 of the final duress live run at `a68f121` (pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` of the live worktree,
session `e6747bd0`), the first duress run after the marker-directory (OQ-215) and personas'-tools (OQ-216) rulings were built.
The 1200 s ceiling cut off the verifier `wave3-verify-all` and its continuation `wave3b-finish-verification`, both testers
working on their own task: by the measure above, wave3 spent 45 of its 58 requests (78 %) and wave3b 33 of 47 (70 %) on its
own task, even counting every request that so much as mentions the marker directory as off-task. Both were making progress —
their last calls completed 1.5 s and 8.8 s before the ceiling — and both landed inside the 30 s bound, at +4.25 s and +0.44 s,
running an edit; reasoning was 75 % and 90 % of their output. The verification took 2,526.3 s, 60.7 % of the run's 4,162.6 s,
for a deliverable two `failed` children held. The longest child of the same model's default pack lived 204.4 s, and e finished
at 88 % of the ceiling.

**The ruling:** the working child's ceiling stays as the owner ruled it. `runtime.child_timeout` defaults to 1200 s and is a
hard bound with the 30 s landing, and a piece of work is continued once and never chained. PD-ORCH-004 (revisions 1 to 5),
R-048, R-071 and PD-CONFIG-003 stand unrevised, because R-072 delegates open questions and does not reach a clause the owner
has already decided: R-048's "the limit itself is not raised" and R-071's "never longer" are the owner's, so a raised default,
an extension while the child makes progress, a per-model figure or a chained continuation would each reverse one of them, and
each goes to the owner as a recommendation. For long work on a slow reasoning model the relief is
[`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003)'s Per-agent timeout: the duress live harness sets it to 45 minutes for
its own launch, as such a user would, and records that value (`LIVE_RUN_DURESS_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MIN`). The question reopens under
**(a′)** a duress run with the Per-agent timeout at 45 minutes cuts off a child that spent more than half its requests on its
own task, measured as above; or **(b)**, unchanged. Either sends any raise of the default, or any softening of the bound, to the
owner as a recommendation in `docs/product/requests.md`; the consortium rules only inside the owner's rulings.

**The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed both.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: confirm as built; the duress
harness, acting as a user on a slow reasoning model, sets the Per-agent timeout to 40 minutes, the product default when the
variable is unset; R-071's premise written down beside its new count; any change to the default the owner's. *Advocate B (the
system's lens)*: confirm as built; the harness sets it to 45 minutes by default, `=20` re-measuring the default, checking that
the setting took effect; condition (a) replaced by (a′) measured at the raised value. The ruling took B's 45 minutes —
PD-CONFIG-003's first execution drove exactly 2,700 s through Save to the run host, while 40 minutes barely covers the 2,345 s
the two lives generated — and B's harness default; and A's NOTE, the unit-tested rewrite of the stored value, and R-071's
premise kept beside its new count (5 of 9). On the merits both agreed: no signal the product can read separates on-task wave3
from off-task d2 at `c2fdd6a` (both passed PD-ORCH-004's progress test and both wrote late), REQ-ORCH-062 and REQ-TOOLS-156
rely on the hard bound, and no default-pack child came near the ceiling.

**Recorded 2026-10-07 (fin32).** No product code, specification text or view changed. The harness:
`apps/desktop/scripts/lib/runtime-key.mjs` (`withRuntimeKey`, `runtime-key.test.ts`), which faults-args' stall-threshold rewrite
now uses too; the duress launch writes `runtime.child_timeout: <min×60>` into the workspace's `agents.yaml`, copies it to
`duress/agents.yaml` in the pack, restores the original after, checks the run host's `child_timeout=<s> s`, records
`childTimeoutS` in `results.json` and NOTEs any value but 1200; a value outside 1–240 stops the harness before any launch.
`AGENTS.md` carries the recipe (`LIVE_RUN_DURESS_MS=7800000`). PD-ORCH-004 gains the second live execution of revision 5 and its
reaffirmation; PD-CONFIG-003's "not measured" item names the next duress run as its measurement. Finding D2 and this
question's reopening measure (the a68f121 autopsy's first-execution list) close as ruled. **Not yet measured:** the next duress
live run, the harness change's first execution — its `app.log` should read `child_timeout=2700 s`, `results.json` carry
`childTimeoutS: 2700` with the NOTE, and the pack hold `duress/agents.yaml`; a wave-three child may then work past 20 minutes,

lifetime, any compression inside a child, any parent resume, and whether a cut-off child spent more than half its requests on

[`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003) revision 3.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** the harness change's first
