**OQ-215 — Do the built-in search and listing tools skip the code-intelligence runtime's marker directory, and do its
memories leave the workspace?** *(REQ-TOOLS-140, the hard-coded ignore components, a closed list holding `.rotaris` and not
the runtime's directory; REQ-TOOLS-139, the scan filters, which honour "the workspace's `.gitignore`" and nothing else, and
serve a file named by its path; REQ-TOOLS-134, the directory and parent listings, which skip "entries whose name is one of
the ignore components of REQ-TOOLS-140"; REQ-MCP-116, the binding manifest that names the marker file; REQ-MCP-034,
REQ-MCP-099 and REQ-MCP-102, the runtime's project path, its marker and the memories that persist across runs;
REQ-WORKSPACE-100; OQ-161's ruling, which accepted the listing; OQ-195, deferred. Raised 2026-10-07 from findings L3 of the
orchestrator's duress live run at `c2fdd6a` and N6 of its duress live run at `c2a9444` (2026-10-06, the self-hosted
endpoint), and ruled the same day.)*

OQ-161's ruling (R-071) accepted that the file tools list the runtime's directory: the load writes it to the repository's
`info/exclude`, so Git treats it as the product's housekeeping, while the scan reads only the root `.gitignore` and shows it
to the agents as the user's content. That clause was accepted on one run's evidence (`27a5127`, finding H3: 38 calls by 5
agents and 80 rows naming `.serena`). The two duress runs since measured it again. At `c2fdd6a` (L3), 5 agents made 41 calls
and wrote 112 rows naming it, and 37 of the failed child d2's 45 requests, 1,142.5 s of its 1,222.6 s of generation, reasoned
about `.serena`, `.rotaris` or `.git` on the run's critical path; both defects the user was told of concerned product files.
At `c2a9444` (N6), 28 calls and 96 rows named it, a `write_memory` put a file in the tree, and the delivered overview listed
the runtime's files as repository files. The build handled the directory two ways: REQ-TOOLS-140's `cache` hid its `cache/`
and listed `project.yml` and the memories.

**What the build proceeded under, until 2026-10-07.** OQ-161's ruling as built: `IGNORE_COMPONENTS`
(`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/search.ts`) held REQ-TOOLS-140's list alone, so grep, glob and `read_file`'s listings walked
the directory; the version-control half (`keepScopeDirIgnored`, `packages/config/src/load.ts`) held in all four duress runs.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the directory joins the hard-coded components (a directive extending REQ-TOOLS-140's
closed list), the scan honours `info/exclude` (a rewrite of REQ-TOOLS-139 that covers no workspace where no line is
written), or the memories leave the tree (against REQ-MCP-034, REQ-MCP-099 and REQ-MCP-102, on a runtime option no manifest
field records); or the ruling stands.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the code-intelligence runtime's
marker directory joins REQ-TOOLS-140's hard-coded ignore components under
[`PD-TOOLS-012`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-012). Its name is read from the binding manifest of REQ-MCP-116. grep and
glob scans and `read_file`'s directory and parent listings therefore skip it as they skip `.rotaris`, and `read_file` and
`haet_read` still serve a file inside it when it is named by path. The rest of OQ-161's ruling stands as built: `.rotaris/`
alone goes in `.gitignore` and the marker's directory in the repository's `info/exclude`; the marker and its memories stay in
the workspace root and are reached through the memory tools; the agents' instructions are unchanged; and where an isolated
tree's memories live stays with OQ-195, which the owner deferred. **The two recommendations weighed:** advocate A (the
user's lens) recommended revising OQ-161's listing clause so the directory, named from the manifest, joins the hard-coded
components, with the memories, the exclude line and the instructions left as built; advocate B (the system's lens)
recommended the same revision, minted as `PD-TOOLS-012` extending REQ-TOOLS-140, in a new entry with a superseding line in
OQ-161's. The ruling followed **both**, in B's shape for the record; A's later sentence in the agents' instructions waits on
measurement. A scan rooted inside an ignored component, which the ruling found still walked, is a separate question, OQ-219.
**Built 2026-10-07 (fin27):** `IGNORE_COMPONENTS` takes `CODE_INTELLIGENCE_MARKER_SEGMENTS[0]` from `@rotaris/config`; the
one set feeds the walker and `listing` (`files.ts`). The ruling's premise that the parent listing of a missing path already
skipped `.rotaris` was false: it skipped nothing, recorded and repaired in the same bundle
([`a-missing-paths-parent-listing-shows-the-ignore-components.md`](../defects/fixed/a-missing-paths-parent-listing-shows-the-ignore-components.md)),
so it now reads the same set. Pinned by the case "the code-intelligence marker directory is a
hard-coded ignore component, named by the manifest" in `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts`, red on `d12f1f2`.
Findings L3, N6 and H3 close with it; the next duress live run is the measurement.

**Measured 2026-10-07, the first live execution (the duress run at `a68f121`, pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z`, session
`e6747bd0`, finding D4):** the file tools held as ruled — the six whole-tree `glob **/*` calls (#1, #24, #29, #73, #126, #135)
and `**/.*` (#65) listed neither directory, and 0 file-tool calls named one — and the terminal remainder cost: 21 calls and
32 rows named the directories (against 28 / 96 at `c2a9444`), and they reached the delivered report, the answer and a project
memory. So the remainder clause fired, and it is raised as OQ-230. **Instructions clause revised 2026-10-07 by OQ-230 (below)
([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** "the agents' instructions are unchanged" no longer holds: every agent receives a
product statement as its last context unit (`PD-TOOLS-012` revision 2). The text above is kept as it was ruled.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** the duress measure. No
file-tool result listed the marker directory, no memory, answer or delivered file named it, and `.rotaris` reached a deliverable
only as `docs/overview.md`'s faithful quote of the workspace's `.gitignore` line; the calls and rows naming either directory are
read in [`PD-TOOLS-012`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-012)'s report-back, which breaks down why their count is not like for
like with `a68f121`'s. Held as ruled. Evidence: [`live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-219 — Beneath an explicit `grep` path or `glob` base inside an ignored directory, what does a scan return?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-139, the scan filters: "paths containing a hard-coded ignore component are skipped", the workspace's
`.gitignore` honoured with "directories pruned during traversal", and the explicit-naming exemption given to `read_file`
and `haet_read` alone; REQ-TOOLS-140, the components; REQ-TOOLS-141, a `glob` base "outside the workspace or not a
directory is silently ignored"; REQ-TOOLS-138, workspace-relative result paths; REQ-TOOLS-134, whose listing skips "entries
whose name is" a component. Raised 2026-10-07 by the R-072 consortium while ruling OQ-215 (live-run finding L3 at
`c2fdd6a`, where the failed child d2 tried `glob .rotaris/**`, `.git/**` and `**/HEAD` and got unexplained empty answers),
and ruled the same day.)*

The walker tested only the names of entries below a base, never the base or its ancestors, and tested gitignore rules
against each entry's full path, whose rules also match descendants. So the answer for a base inside an excluded directory
depended on how the user spelled one line: under `node_modules/` a scan rooted at `node_modules/pkg` served the package's
top-level files and dropped every subdirectory; under `node_modules` it served nothing; with no line it served everything but
nested `dist`, `build`, `out`, `cache` and `node_modules`. `glob '*.js' base_path='node_modules/x'` returned a file that
`glob 'node_modules/x/*.js'` did not, and `glob '*' base_path='.rotaris'` listed the product's own state. A `grep` entry
naming one file walked its parent's whole subtree and compared lower-cased paths, so on a case-sensitive disk naming
`src/a.ts` also searched `src/A.ts`. Recorded as
[`an-explicit-search-base-inside-an-ignored-directory-is-walked.md`](../defects/fixed/an-explicit-search-base-inside-an-ignored-directory-is-walked.md).

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an explicit base is the caller's decision (the component and gitignore filters stand
aside below it, as `read_file`'s exemption does for a named file, which needs a directive), whether REQ-TOOLS-139 governs as
written (a scan beneath any base returns exactly the whole-workspace scan beneath it), or whether the build's middle reading
(the base honoured, nested components still skipped) is confirmed.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** REQ-TOOLS-139 governs as written.
Beneath any explicit grep `paths` entry or glob `base_path`, a scan returns exactly what the whole-workspace scan returns
beneath that base, so no result path contains a REQ-TOOLS-140 component or lies under a directory the workspace
`.gitignore` prunes, and a grep entry naming one file is searched only when the whole-workspace scan would search that file.
An excluded base stays the base (REQ-TOOLS-141 replaces only a base outside the workspace or one that is not a directory)
and answers `No matches found` or `No files found`. The grep and glob descriptions state this filter and direct the caller to
`read_file`, which serves a named file, searches it with its `grep` argument and lists a named directory. **The two
recommendations weighed:** advocate A (the user's lens) recommended that the caller decides on an explicit base, the
component and gitignore filters standing aside below an excluded base under a directive, so a search inside a named
dependency is not a false `No matches found`; advocate B (the system's lens) recommended the literal reading of REQ-TOOLS-139
as one invariant, a scan rooted at a base equal to the root scan restricted to it, repaired without a directive. The ruling
followed **B**: A's exemption would need a directive and would open `.rotaris` and `.git` to bulk scans, and no autopsy
records a scan rooted in an ignored directory; A's point that an unexplained empty answer is read as fact is kept in the two
descriptions. No directive is minted: the requirement is faithful and the code departed from it. **Built 2026-10-07
(fin27):** `scanExcludes` and the base test in `walkFiles`, and the direct search of a named file in `grepTool`
(`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/search.ts`); pinned by the five cases under "an explicit base or a named file inside an
excluded directory yields nothing" in `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts`, four red on `d12f1f2` (the fifth, a
run rooted under `.rotaris/worktrees/<w>`, guards the repair). Noticed while ruling and recorded open, not repaired here:
[`a-re-included-directory-under-an-ignored-glob-keeps-its-files-ignored.md`](../defects/fixed/a-re-included-directory-under-an-ignored-glob-keeps-its-files-ignored.md). **Repaired 2026-10-07 (fin30):** a rule now matches
the path itself and nothing beneath it, and `ignoredBy` asks every proper directory prefix before the path, in git's
order, so `gen/*` then `!gen/keep/` keeps `gen/keep/f.ts` for the search tools and the contains-code walk alike
(`packages/config/src/init/gitignore.ts`).

**OQ-224 — For REQ-GIT-119's lock, REQ-GIT-120's force and refusal and REQ-MONITOR-251's placement, which runs are "another
run is active"?** *(REQ-GIT-119, the launch dialog's mandatory isolation "while another run is active", its tooltip and hint;
REQ-GIT-120, "whenever any run is active" a launch without an explicit tree is forced into one and a base-workspace session's
resume refused; REQ-MONITOR-251, "the second and any subsequent concurrent launch"; REQ-GIT-124, which counts "a session lock
in this workspace" and calls itself consistent with REQ-GIT-119 and REQ-GIT-120; REQ-MONITOR-256 and REQ-MONITOR-258, the
resume half scoped "there" and "in a workspace where a run is already executing"; `PD-SHELL-002`, "while any run is active in
the workspace, the dialog SHALL lock", and "a window of another project is untouched by all of this". Raised 2026-10-07 by
the R-072 consortium as its question GI1, from
[`the-launch-dialog-locks-isolation-only-for-a-run-in-its-own-workspace.md`](../defects/fixed/the-launch-dialog-locks-isolation-only-for-a-run-in-its-own-workspace.md)
(fin28's repair round 1), and recorded here as OQ-224, the number the round assigned it. ~~Open.~~ **Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

The launch dialog locks isolation on for a busy session of its own workspace (`currentBusy || listBusy` over the window's
session list, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/main.tsx`), while `session.start` forces a launch without an explicit tree into
`rotaris/session/<id>` whenever the run host counts a run anywhere in the instance (`runs.active` with the empty id, since
fin28's repair round 1, `32ac0c0`). So in an idle project's window, while another project's run executes, the dialog offers
isolation unchecked and the launch it shows on the base tree lands in a worktree; and in a non-Git folder, a subfolder of a
repository or a detached HEAD the forced launch fails, about a run in another window. REQ-GIT-120's "any" reads
instance-wide; REQ-GIT-119's hint ("Two runs sharing one working tree would overwrite each other's edits") and the
requirements around it read per workspace. Neither surface agrees with the other, and a workspace folder nested inside
another open workspace shares files with it whichever reading is taken.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** in REQ-GIT-119, REQ-GIT-120 and
REQ-MONITOR-251, a run is active for a launch or a continue in a workspace when it is active and either belongs to that
workspace, whatever tree it runs in, or writes in a tree that is that workspace's folder, lies inside it or contains it. A run
of an unrelated project never counts. Main asks the run host that one count. The launch dialog shows main's answer when it
opens: locked, with REQ-GIT-119's tooltip and hint, when the count is above zero or cannot be read, and unchecked and
enabled, with REQ-GIT-118's hint, otherwise. `session.start` forces the default tree on the same answer, and every time it
forces it raises an informational notice carrying REQ-GIT-119's hint and the branch. REQ-GIT-120's refusal to continue a
base-tree session is built on the same count, with that session excluded. This is recorded as
[`PD-GIT-001`](../product/directives.md#pd-git-001), which narrows REQ-GIT-119, REQ-GIT-120 and REQ-MONITOR-251.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: "another run is active" means a run active in the
launching window's own workspace, a workspace folder nested inside or around it counting as the same workspace; main asks
that one count and the dialog shows main's answer; recorded as `PD-GIT-001`, narrowing the three requirements. *Advocate B
(the system's lens)*: the same per-workspace reading, as equality of the session row's workspace — the dialog as built, main
pointed back at the window's own count, classified as covered with no directive, and the unbuilt resume half recorded and
built. **The ruling followed both**: the per-workspace reading both take, which PD-SHELL-002, REQ-GIT-124 and
REQ-MONITOR-256/258 support; A's directive, whose back-pointer stops a later reader of REQ-GIT-120's "any" re-keying it as
fin28's verifier did, and A's containment rule, without which a base-tree launch in `/repo` would share files with a live run
in a window open on `/repo/app`; and from B the history corrected beside the claim it replaces and the resume refusal placed
at continuing, with the session excluded. Neither settled two things, which the ruling adds: an unreadable count locks the
dialog and forces the worktree, and a forced placement says so.
[`a-base-tree-session-continues-beside-another-run-in-its-workspace.md`](../defects/fixed/a-base-tree-session-continues-beside-another-run-in-its-workspace.md)
records the unbuilt resume half, written before its code.

**OQ-223 — Does Settings › Runtime keep an "Improvement analysis timeout" control, and on what terms?** *(REQ-CONFIG-256's
"Written keys are exactly", REQ-CONFIG-263's Tier B overlay, REQ-CONFIG-323's four runtime policy toggles, REQ-CONFIG-325's
"two numeric policy limits" and REQ-CONFIG-417's destination 1, none naming `runtime.improvement_collector_timeout`;
REQ-LIBRARY-041, the improvement domain's one Settings row, the toggle; REQ-CONFIG-118 and REQ-LIBRARY-039, the key and its
60 s default; REQ-NOTIFY-100 and REQ-LIBRARY-023/124, a timed-out analysis and its notice; OQ-114's F4, the measured analyst
calls. Raised 2026-10-07 by the R-072 consortium as its question IT1, from
[`the-improvement-analysis-timeout-control-writes-a-key-no-settings-list-names.md`](../defects/fixed/the-improvement-analysis-timeout-control-writes-a-key-no-settings-list-names.md)
(noticed while building OQ-218), and recorded here as OQ-223, the number the round assigned it. ~~Open.~~ **Ruled
2026-10-07.**)*

The runtime policy card draws a numeric "Improvement analysis timeout" control after the "Improvement loop" toggle, over
`runtime.improvement_collector_timeout` in seconds, committed by Save. No list the specification keeps names the key — the
desktop save's written keys, the Tier B overlay, the card's toggles, destination 1 — and the build left it out of
`TIER_B_RUNTIME_KEYS` too, so its on-screen value never reached a run unsaved; it got through only because
`DesktopSaveSchema` accepted any runtime key. Its hint names "the collector", it takes any positive number and has no unit
suffix. Whether the control stays (a directive) or goes (covered by the lists), the specification does not say.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** Settings › Runtime keeps the
"Improvement analysis timeout" control directly after the "Improvement loop" toggle. It shows whole seconds with a "seconds"
suffix, is clamped at the widget to 10–600, starts from the effective `runtime.improvement_collector_timeout` (60 by
default), is committed by Save, and is laid on the next run start by Tier B. A stored value outside 10–600 is shown clamped
with its exact seconds stated beneath and is kept until the field changes. When a post-run analysis reaches the limit, the
zero-proposal notice's detail says so. All of this is [`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003) revision 2,
and the desktop save's runtime keys become a closed list that the screen's runtime keys must equal (REQ-CONFIG-256).

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: keep the control and make it complete under a revision 2
of PD-CONFIG-003 — the seconds suffix, a 10–600 clamp, Save, the Tier B overlay, the four lists, a hint a person can act
on — and have a timed-out analysis's notice say so; the bound that decides whether the analyst's chosen model finishes
belongs beside the toggle it qualifies, and OQ-218 settled the same day that a kept ceiling is one the person can move.
*Advocate B (the system's lens)*: remove the control, keep the key file-only as REQ-CONFIG-118 and REQ-LIBRARY-039 state it
— covered work with no directive — and close the desktop save's runtime key set so REQ-CONFIG-256's "exactly" is enforced.
**The ruling followed A**: OQ-114's F4 timed three of six analyst calls past the 60 s that R-071 kept, a timed-out review
read as an ordinary empty one, and removing a working control just before ship would leave that outcome with no on-screen
remedy; B's counter-evidence (analysts cut about 4 s in) measured the live harness's quit. From B it took the closed save
list, the equality tests that would have caught this defect, and the objection to a delegation-titled directive, answered by
widening PD-CONFIG-003's heading. It departs from A on the dispositions: REQ-CONFIG-323's four toggles are untouched
(extended), and REQ-CONFIG-325's "two numeric policy limits" is the count that changes (narrowed). R-071 is not revised: the
60 s default stands.
[`a-timed-out-improvement-analysis-reads-as-one-that-found-nothing.md`](../defects/fixed/a-timed-out-improvement-analysis-reads-as-one-that-found-nothing.md)
records the notice's half, written before its code.

**OQ-225 — What does the run do when REQ-ORCH-029's hold fires on an iteration that has answered?** *(REQ-ORCH-029, the
coordinator "does not report the run successful while a todo item is non-terminal or while a todo item's recorded state
disagrees with what happened"; REQ-ORCH-075, the re-queue's continuation payload, the stripped base payload plus the marker;
REQ-ORCH-078, todo-correction retries reusing the validation-retry setting, "default 0: … re-queues without an
in-conversation retry"; REQ-ORCH-072, a fresh root per iteration; REQ-TOOLS-155, a new root refused the previous root's
children; REQ-ORCH-067, iteration ends visible in the transcript; REQ-ORCH-077, the give-up at the third pending outcome;
PD-ORCH-009, the re-prompt of an answerless root. Raised 2026-10-07 from finding P1 of the final default live run at
`a68f121`, the pack's one FAIL: in session `5df89df3` (terminal) the coordinator answered in full (traffic #24, transcript
row 48) while its plan's "Report one line per command" read `PENDING`; with no correction the task was re-queued, the fresh
root (traffic #25: the task and the marker only; tool call `#25`, `background_output`, refused "not found among your
children") re-delegated the whole probe, and transcript row 54 told the person the report "never delivered". Recorded as
[`a-re-queued-tasks-fresh-root-cannot-see-the-answer-its-iteration-was-held-back-for.md`](../defects/fixed/a-re-queued-tasks-fresh-root-cannot-see-the-answer-its-iteration-was-held-back-for.md),
repaired by fin31.
Ruled the same day.)*

The hold behaves as the specification states, and the G5 repair's note priced its cost ("the fresh root, which has none of
the previous conversation, may redo work to finish it"). What the specification does not settle is what a re-queued root
learns of the iteration it continues, and whether the root that wrote the answer should first be asked to record its plan's
true state while it still holds the evidence: REQ-ORCH-078's default of 0 says it is not.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** if the coordinating root of an
execution iteration answers `succeeded` while items of its own plan are still open, the run sends it at least one plan
correction in its own conversation. The count is the larger of 1 and `runtime.auto_retries_validation`. When the root has
already answered, the correction says the answer has been shown and asks the root to record each item's true state with the
todo tool. A turn that follows the correction is never asked again for an answer the execution has already written. If the
corrections are used up and the task is still re-queued (REQ-ORCH-075) or given up on (REQ-ORCH-077), the run writes one
`system` row in the transcript saying so. The re-queued task's next fresh root receives the held iteration's answer, cut to
6,000 characters, beside the continuation marker. The run never marks a plan item itself. Recorded as
[`PD-ORCH-015`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-015), which narrows REQ-ORCH-078 and extends REQ-ORCH-075, and as
[`PD-ORCH-009`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-009) revision 2. REQ-ORCH-092, REQ-CONFIG-120 and REQ-NOTIFY-100 (the
validation-retry setting's own default of 0) are untouched.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)* recommended an in-conversation correction by default,
with the count the larger of 1 and the validation-retry setting, a correction text saying the answer was shown and a done
item is recorded rather than redone, no re-prompt after an answer, and, where the hold still re-queues, a `system` row and
the held answer with the open item ids carried to the fresh root. *Advocate B (the system's lens)* recommended the same
floor of one correction kept apart from REQ-ORCH-092's default, the correction naming ABANDONED as a true state, a revision
of PD-ORCH-009 so a correction's silent turn after an answer is not re-prompted, and a `system` row on the re-queue, with
the fresh root's payload unchanged. **The ruling followed both**: B in keeping the floor off the shared setting's default,
its ABANDONED wording and its transcript row (extended to the give-up, which REQ-ORCH-067's iteration-end visibility already
asks for), and its numbering of the PD-ORCH-009 revision; A on the fallback, since without the held answer a root that
ignores its correction reproduces P1 one step later. It dropped A's item ids and children's replies. Both advocates rejected
letting the run tick a "report" item from the answer's wording (it would make the run's guess the plan's record), and so
does the ruling. Related and repaired separately, as a defect: finding P4, the follow-up payload's "Recent iterations" reading
timeline entries nothing writes.

**Built 2026-10-07 (fin31).** `Run.turn`'s correction closure counts to `max(1, validationRetries)`, keeps the execution's
answer (the re-prompt fires only while it is empty; the answer stays the report's text when the correction's turn writes
less), and `planCorrectionText(open, answered)` carries the ruling's two sentences; `Run.iterate` stores `Task.heldAnswer`
beside `planLeftOpen`, writes the `system` row (`planHeldRowText`) for a re-queue and a give-up, and `planCarryText(open,
heldAnswer)` hands the answer to the same task's next fresh root. The ruling's step 2 said both "the last non-empty text a turn
wrote" and "a correction turn's text replaces it only when it is longer"; the build keeps the first answer and replaces it only
with a longer one, which is what the ruling's own test ("Recorded." keeps the answer) asks. Pinned by eight cases in
`packages/engine/src/run/coordinator-plan.test.ts` (seven red on `a68f121`) and `run-pure.test.ts`; shown by `pnpm
part-h-proof`'s `plan-correction` launch. First execution reported in [`PD-ORCH-015`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-015)
and in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md); the live terminal scenario waits on the orchestrator's next default run.

**OQ-222 — Do six back-pointers that name a directive whose disposition block omits their requirement mark reaches the
register left out, or are they cross-references written in a back-pointer's shape?** *(`docs/product/README.md`, "The
back-pointer, in place": "Use `Superseded by`, `Narrowed by` or `Extended by` to match the disposition"; `PD-TOOLS-002`'s
Narrows line and `PD-LIBRARY-002`'s Extends and `New:` lines; the notes at REQ-SANDBOX-104 (Narrowed by `PD-TOOLS-002`),
REQ-MONITOR-173, REQ-WORKSPACE-041, REQ-LIBRARY-017 and REQ-NOTIFY-251 (Extended by `PD-LIBRARY-002`), and at domain 14's
introduction, which names no requirement. Raised 2026-10-06 by the F15 repair, which recorded the six as
[`six-back-pointers-name-a-directive-whose-disposition-does-not-name-their-requirement.md`](../defects/fixed/six-back-pointers-name-a-directive-whose-disposition-does-not-name-their-requirement.md)
and left the reading per note to the directive's owner; opened here 2026-10-07 as the R-072 consortium's question BP1,
the number the round assigned it, and ruled the same day.)*

The generated register (`SUPERSEDED_BY`, `NARROWED_BY`, `EXTENDED_BY`) records nothing for five of the six requirements
under the directive their note names (REQ-WORKSPACE-041 only as narrowed by `PD-WORKSPACE-002`), so a reader of code is
told the requirement is untouched while the specification file says a directive reaches it. Either a disposition block
omits a requirement its rule reaches, or a note is a cross-reference in the shape of a back-pointer.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** five of the six notes mark
reaches that their directives' disposition blocks left out, and each block now names its requirement under the verb its
note already carries. `PD-TOOLS-002` Narrows REQ-SANDBOX-104, together with REQ-TOOLS-071 and REQ-TOOLS-072, because its
rule names each of the three by identifier and removes the same downgrade clause from each; `PD-LIBRARY-002` Extends
REQ-MONITOR-173, REQ-WORKSPACE-041, REQ-LIBRARY-017 and REQ-NOTIFY-251, and its `New:` line is retired. REQ-LIBRARY-017
is recorded under Extends because its clauses bind an analysis that a run triggered, and the directive reads it so
("no clause here is relaxed"). The note in domain 14's introduction names no requirement, so it is relabelled as a
cross-reference written in its own words. `back-pointers.test.ts` drops its known list: one case asserts that every note
agrees with the register, a converse case asserts that every register entry has its note, and both lists start empty
once the missing notes at REQ-TOOLS-069 and REQ-SHELL-119 are written. The generator refuses a `New:` line that names a
requirement and `New` beside another verb, the route this defect came in by. No directive is minted or revised: the two
disposition blocks are completed in place, each with a dated italic line beneath it, on the precedent of F15
(`PD-ORCH-014`'s REQ-CONFIG-135 line) and `PD-WORKSPACE-001`'s third execution; no rule text and no requirement text
changes, and no product behaviour changes. R-071's ruling on OQ-65 stands.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: the five reaches enter the disposition blocks under
their notes' verbs, the introduction becomes a cross-reference in the REQ-CONFIG-464 shape, the known list is deleted,
and the notes at REQ-WORKSPACE-041 and REQ-MONITOR-173 gain a sentence each so they stay true after OQ-65 and ADR-0065
decision 7; it named REQ-TOOLS-071, REQ-TOOLS-072 and REQ-LIBRARY-125 as unrecorded reaches. *Advocate B (the system's
lens)*: the same five entries and the introduction relabelled, plus this entry, a converse check that every register
entry has its note (with the notes at REQ-TOOLS-069 and REQ-SHELL-119 written so it starts empty), a generator refusal
of a `New:` line naming an identifier or standing beside another verb, and REQ-TOOLS-071 added to the Narrows line. **The

and
[`the-unattended-advisory-is-empty-for-every-mode-where-pd-tools-002-keeps-it-for-ask-and-restricted.md`](../defects/fixed/the-unattended-advisory-is-empty-for-every-mode-where-pd-tools-002-keeps-it-for-ask-and-restricted.md),

**OQ-226 — How is a foreground terminal call its run cancels recorded?** *(REQ-TOOLS-097, the hard bound whose observation
is returned "on reaching" it; REQ-TOOLS-099, the hard-timeout contract and its detail; REQ-TOOLS-179, 124 reserved for a
hard timeout; REQ-TOOLS-103, a failure before completion; REQ-TOOLS-100 and REQ-TOOLS-112, the closed `failure_kind` and
`outcome_kind` vocabularies, neither of which holds a cancellation kind; REQ-SESSION-136, the outcome-driven issues;
PD-ORCH-005 clause 3, a call a quit cut off "is recorded as interrupted"; OQ-144's handshake sentence. Raised 2026-10-07
from finding P2 of the orchestrator's final default live run at `a68f121` (the self-hosted endpoint), and ruled the same
day.)*

A foreground call the run cancels (the tool context's signal aborted: a pause past REQ-ORCH-134's tool deadline, a stop, a
quit, the explicit cancel, an agent's cancellation or its limit, a cancel during OQ-144's handshake) ends its process tree
and restarts the session, and was then reported as a hard timeout: exit 124, `timeout`, `TimeoutError`, "The command
exceeded its timeout of N seconds", a `terminal_timeout` issue at `error`, and a Timeouts count in `summary.md`. In that
run's terminal session (`5df89df3`), call `#36`, the re-run child's 45 s wedge, ran 3,505 ms before the quit cut it and is
recorded `failed`, `timeout`, exit 124, "The command exceeded its timeout of 100 seconds; … (the call was cancelled)";
issue 10 is `terminal_timeout` at `error`, and `summary.md` reads "Timeouts: 1". The console's NOTE said the hard cap was
not reached. Recorded as
[`a-foreground-terminal-call-the-run-cancels-reads-as-a-timeout.md`](../defects/fixed/a-foreground-terminal-call-the-run-cancels-reads-as-a-timeout.md).

**What the build proceeded under, until 2026-10-07.** Both abort branches of `ForegroundSession.run`
(`packages/agent-tools/src/terminal/foreground.ts`) returned 124 and `timedOut: true` with the error "the call was
cancelled", and `terminal/index.ts` read `timedOut` as the `timeout` kind and wrote REQ-TOOLS-099's detail.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the cancel keeps the hard-timeout reading, is REQ-TOOLS-103's `execution_error` within
the vocabulary as it stands, or gains a kind of its own, the `interrupted` the question and delegation tools already carry,
under a directive that widens REQ-TOOLS-100's and REQ-TOOLS-112's closed sets; and whether such a call files an issue.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a new directive,
[`PD-TOOLS-013`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-013), governs. A foreground terminal call that its run cancels is
recorded with `failure_kind` and `outcome_kind` `interrupted`, severity `warning`, `is_error` true, no exit code and
`timeout` false; this covers a pause past the tool deadline, a stop, a quit, the explicit cancel, an agent's cancellation or
limit, and a cancel during OQ-144's handshake. Its detail says the run cancelled the call, what became of the session and
what was restored, and the call files no outcome-driven issue. The hard-timeout reading (124, `timeout`,
`terminal_timeout`) stays reserved for a call that reached its hard bound, as REQ-TOOLS-097, -099 and -179 state, so the
timeout encoding a cancel carried is repaired as a defect against them. **The two recommendations weighed:** advocate A
(the user's lens) recommended repairing within the vocabulary, the cancel read as REQ-TOOLS-103's `execution_error` with no
exit code and a marker that suppresses the issue, and no directive; advocate B (the system's lens) recommended the
directive, `interrupted` as a fifth failure kind and an eleventh outcome kind at severity `warning`, the kind PD-ORCH-005
already gives every other call a run cuts short, with no issue filed and the gate unchanged. The ruling followed **B**: A's
`execution_error` reads a deliberate cancel at severity `error`, in the bucket of real backend faults, still departs from
REQ-SESSION-136's letter, and gives the gate a second way to mark an interrupted call, where B reuses the product's own
word and the gate's existing branch. It takes A's test plan (a mid-command cancel, the real timeouts pinned, Timeouts
reading 0). OQ-144's handshake parenthetical is revised in place beside the struck reading; R-071's ruled behaviour for
replaced and ended shells stands. The ruling's directive number was written as `PD-TOOLS-011` by advocate B, taken; it is
`PD-TOOLS-013`. Noticed while ruling and recorded, not repaired: the gate's catch and fetch still file a `tool_error` for
a call the run cancels
([`a-call-the-run-cancels-in-the-gate-or-in-fetch-files-a-tool-error-issue.md`](../defects/fixed/a-call-the-run-cancels-in-the-gate-or-in-fetch-files-a-tool-error-issue.md)).
**Built 2026-10-07 (fin31):** `ForegroundResult.cancelled` and both abort branches of `ForegroundSession.run` (no exit code,
`timedOut: false`), the `interrupted` kind, `InterruptedError` and the cancel's detail in `terminal/index.ts`, and the kind in
both vocabularies of `classify.ts`; `gate.ts` and `export.ts` unchanged. The ruling's dispositions could not stand as
written: the symbol generator admits one directive per verb on a requirement, and `PD-TOOLS-009` already narrows
REQ-TOOLS-112 and `PD-SESSION-003` REQ-SESSION-136, so PD-TOOLS-013 narrows REQ-TOOLS-100 and extends those two.
*Reversed 2026-10-13 by [OQ-237](#oq-237) (GV1): PD-TOOLS-013 narrows all three, as this ruling named them; the substitution and its
reason no longer stand.* Pinned by
the cases named in the repaired note and `pnpm driver-proof`'s launch 13d, a quit during `sleep 60`, red before and green
after.

**OQ-227 — What does `single_file_change` mean to the intent classifier?** *(REQ-ORCH-006, the taxonomy and the three meanings
it fixes, none for `single_file_change`; PD-ORCH-011, "`explicit_trivial` and `single_file_change` are the two smallest
edits"; PD-ORCH-006, the direct-work bundle a `single_file_change` grants; REQ-ORCH-021, the micro group. Raised 2026-10-07
by fin30's repair of finacc3 A2-03,
[`slice-proof-reds-on-one-intent-answer-outside-the-accepted-set.md`](../defects/fixed/slice-proof-reds-on-one-intent-answer-outside-the-accepted-set.md).
Numbered past the round's assigned OQ-221 to OQ-224; raised as OQ-225, renumbered OQ-227 at landing because origin/main took
OQ-225 (the REQ-ORCH-029 hold, PD-ORCH-015) and OQ-226 (fin31, PD-TOOLS-013). Open.)*

The classifier's instructions (`CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `packages/engine/src/intent/classifier.ts`) say what the
specification says and no more: `single_file_change` is one of "the two smallest edits". A live model classified "Add a
--json flag to the CLI that prints the effective configuration as JSON, with a unit test for it." as `single_file_change`
(0.82) once in two runs. Under PD-ORCH-006 that category grants the coordinator the direct-work bundle, so a feature and its
test would be worked by the coordinator alone, with no delegation. Nothing in the specification says that is wrong, and
nothing says the category means one file.

**What the build proceeds under.** The instructions are unchanged. `slice-proof` reads `single_file_change` as out of reach of
that prompt (its name, `lib/live-answers.mjs`) and asks once more on one such answer, going red on a second; the product is
held to nothing about it.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether `single_file_change` means an edit confined to one file (and the classifier is told so,
beside REQ-ORCH-006's three fixed meanings), whether a request that names a test beside its change is out of its reach,
and whether PD-ORCH-006's direct-work grant should follow the category or the size of the change.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** `single_file_change` SHALL mean a
small edit confined to one file, as the request states or implies. A request for a change together with a test of it, or
one that names several files to change, is outside the category unless the request puts all of it in one file. The
classifier's system prompt states this meaning on every rung. This is [`PD-ORCH-011`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-011)
revision 2, which narrows REQ-ORCH-006. `PD-ORCH-006`'s direct-work grant keeps following the category, as REQ-ORCH-016
states, and `slice-proof` keeps its accepted sets and its single retry. The entry's status above ("Open.") is history.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended the one-file meaning as PD-ORCH-011 revision 2, one sentence in the system
  prompt, the grant left keyed to the category, and a first execution against the registered self-hosted endpoint: the
  identifier is on screen under REQ-ORCH-014, and the same prompt ran directly in one launch and delegated in the next.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same, worded "a small edit confined to one file, as the request
  states or implies", with the micro group's glossary entry naming it: the system prompt goes out on every rung while only
  rung 2's example carried a meaning, and `slice-proof` already judged the product by a one-file meaning nothing in the
  record stated; B held that the live first execution needed the owner's fresh consent.

The ruling confirmed what both rest on: `CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` goes out on every rung, only rung 2 carries the "one
file, one edit" example, and the 0.82 miss came through rung 1, so the category's meaning depended on which rung the
provider accepted. Letting the grant follow measured size would conflict with REQ-ORCH-008 and REQ-ORCH-016. It adopted B's
wording — "small" agrees with revision 1's "the two smallest edits" and keeps a large one-file rewrite out of micro — and
B's glossary step. On the first execution it followed A: R-068's standing authorization covers the unmetered self-hosted
default. The cost both name stays: a small change requested with its test now runs delegated and slower, and same-file test
languages depend on the request saying so.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin34, `fin34-library-and-intent`); its first execution is reported in PD-ORCH-011's entry.* One sentence
in `CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, pinned on all three rungs by `intent.test.ts` (red before); `live-answers.mjs`'s `why` and
`intentOutcome` comment cite the revision; `packages/engine/CONTEXT.md`'s micro group names the meaning. Note moved:
[`the-intent-classifiers-rungs-give-single-file-change-different-meanings.md`](../defects/fixed/the-intent-classifiers-rungs-give-single-file-change-different-meanings.md).
**Not yet measured:** the live first execution (`pnpm slice-proof` against the registered self-hosted default), which the
orchestrator runs under R-068; it should show the flag prompt (3b) in the build groups and the README append in the micro group.

<a id="oq-232"></a>

**OQ-232 — When the loop classifier is cut on a raw-count trigger, are four consecutive calls of one tool evidence of a loop
whatever their arguments?** *(REQ-ORCH-104, the raw-count fallback's "≥ 4 consecutive same-tool calls — never from counts
alone"; REQ-NOTIFY-109, "back-to-back invocations of the same tool"; REQ-ORCH-101, the product's one comparison of two
actions, the tool name and the whole arguments; REQ-NOTIFY-102, no corrective message where no loop occurs; REQ-ORCH-100,
the raw count of 60; REQ-CONFIG-467 and OQ-114, the 2.0 s classification bound kept; OQ-126, the message limb. Raised
2026-10-07 from finding D6 of the final duress live run at `a68f121`, recorded in
[`the-raw-count-fallback-declares-a-loop-on-four-reads-of-different-files.md`](../defects/fixed/the-raw-count-fallback-declares-a-loop-on-four-reads-of-different-files.md),
and ruled the same day under the owner's delegation; the consortium's question D6.)*

The duress pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` (session `e6747bd0`) holds the limb's first live firing. At
`wave2e-decisions`'s 60th call the classification (request 149) was cut at 1,915 ms, and the fallback found calls #229 to
#232: four `read_file` calls in two steps over `test/extra.test.js` and `docs/decisions.md`, a child checking its own
document. Timeline entry 43 (07:33:11.581, `trigger: raw-count`) told it "Pause and reassess read_file around
docs/decisions.md …", and the child spent request 150 (24.5 s, about 5 kB of reasoning) answering "nothing foreign — only my
own writes". The build compares the last four calls by tool name alone (ADR-0059 decision 5), as the text reads; the
specification does not say whether a read-only tool counts, or whether "same-tool" means the same action as REQ-ORCH-101's
repetition trigger does.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** when the loop classifier fails or
is cut on a raw-count trigger, REQ-ORCH-104's fallback counts four or more consecutive tool calls as evidence of a loop only
when they are the same action under REQ-ORCH-101 — the same tool name and identical whole arguments. Calls of one tool with
differing arguments count as counts alone, whatever the tool's facet, and no tool family is exempted. The message limb as
OQ-126 ruled it, the repetition, cycle and stuck rules, the deterministic message and the 2.0 s classification bound kept
under OQ-114 are unchanged. This is [`PD-ORCH-016`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-016), which narrows REQ-ORCH-104 and
REQ-NOTIFY-109 (numbered 016: fin31's PD-ORCH-015 was assigned before it).

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **A**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended comparing whole actions by REQ-ORCH-101's rule, with no tool family exempted
  and the 2.0 s bound kept, as a directive narrowing both requirements: with this model every classification is cut, so the
  fallback's accuracy is what the user lives with, the limb's one live firing was false, and comparing whole actions covers
  reads and edits alike with a rule the product already has.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended confirming the build: the text takes the tool as the unit, requiring
  identical arguments leaves the limb nearly redundant beside the repetition trigger, reading one file in shifting windows is
  the circling only this limb can see, and the cost — one step per three or four duress runs — is bounded.

The ruling agreed with B that the build is faithful, so a change needs a directive, and with both that no tool family is
exempted and the bound stays. On the limb it followed A: 9 of 9 classifications cut falsify ADR-0059's "activations are rare"
for this model, the one live firing was false, and the classifier's one late answer had judged a child's edits and
verification reads to be no loop. B's strongest point is the directive's stated cost: after the change the limb adds
evidence only where identical calls follow a pending raw-count trigger, and a single-tool loop with varied arguments is left
to the third activation's escalation, the stall watch or the ceiling.

*Built 2026-10-07 (fin32, `fin32-child-reports-and-limits`); its first execution is reported in PD-ORCH-016's entry.*
`rawFallbackHasEvidence` compares the last four tool events by `fingerprint`; `supervisor.test.ts` and `pnpm part-h-proof`'s
`raw-count-varied` and `raw-count-same` launches pin it. Beside the ruling, recorded and not repaired: the classification timer
is armed from `runtime.loop_classification_timeout` uncapped by REQ-NOTIFY-106's remaining budget
([`the-loop-classification-timer-is-not-capped-at-the-activation-budget.md`](../defects/fixed/the-loop-classification-timer-is-not-capped-at-the-activation-budget.md));
repaired 2026-10-13 (fin35): the bound is the smaller of the key and what remains of the 2 s budget, counted from the
activity that satisfied the trigger.
**Not yet measured:** a live run; the next should show no `loop_supervisor_activation` with `trigger: raw-count` unless the
agent's last three messages with text were normalised-equal or its last four tool calls were identical in name and whole
arguments.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** reached once, not

**OQ-231 — Does a `haet_edit` miss that matches at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 2 or 3 say so?** *(REQ-TOOLS-189, `haet_edit`
matches at level 1 only "because the anchoring hash exists precisely to make the edit exact", and "a failure to match reports
the path and directs the caller to read the file again"; its stale-hash clause, whose message "SHALL NOT quote the file's
current content"; REQ-TOOLS-136, the four match levels — level 2 trailing whitespace, level 3 a uniform indentation shift;
REQ-TOOLS-134, the read's line format and its 30,000-character output cap; REQ-SESSION-136, the `tool_error` issue a failed
call files. Raised 2026-10-07 from finding D5 of the final duress live run at `a68f121` (pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` of
the live worktree, session `e6747bd0`, the self-hosted endpoint), and ruled the same day.)*

wave3 (`wave3-verify-all`) failed 6 of its 14 `haet_edit` calls with "old_string was not found exactly" (#290, #292, #297,
#304, #315, #321), and after each near miss ran `sed -n … | cat -A` to see the file's whitespace (#293, #298, #305, #322);
its continuation wave3b did the same after #382 (#380, #385, #386, `awk … indent=`). The autopsy priced it at 7 failed edits,
about 14 extra steps and about 63 s, all inside the two children the 1200 s ceiling cut off, and seven `tool_error` issues
(7 to 12 and 18). The build already knew: `matchEdit` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`) runs every level, and the
miss branch discards a level-2 or level-3 match (`if (!m || m.level !== 1)`). Recorded as
[`haet-edit-answers-a-whitespace-only-miss-with-not-found-exactly.md`](../defects/fixed/haet-edit-answers-a-whitespace-only-miss-with-not-found-exactly.md).

**Replayed before the build (fin32, 2026-10-07).** `docs/verification.md` was rebuilt from the pack's store — wave3's
`write_file` #289, then every successful `haet_edit` and code-intelligence `replace_content` in ordinal order, each
`haet_edit`'s `content_hash` checked equal to the rebuilt bytes' SHA-256 — and each miss's `old_string` run through the
build's own `matchEdit`. #292, #297, #304, #315, #321 and #382 each match **one window at level 3** (the file's lines one
space deeper or shallower than `old_string`'s; #304's first line one space shallower); #290 matches at level 4 only
(similarity 0.908: its first line named citations the file did not hold). None matched at level 2. So 6 of the 7 "not found
exactly" misses of the two children were a single level-3 window.

**What the build proceeds under.** REQ-TOOLS-189 as written: any miss at level 1 answers "old_string was not found exactly in
<path>. Read it again with haet_read.", whatever a lower level found.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the edit applies at level 2 or 3 (as `write_file`'s does), whether the miss names the near
match and quotes it while the edit stays exact, or whether the reply stands as built.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** when `haet_edit` (or `haet`)
holds a current hash, `replace_all` is false, and `old_string` misses at level 1 but matches exactly one window at REQ-TOOLS-136
level 2 or 3, the edit is refused and nothing is written. The reply names the path, the match level and the window's lines,
and says in words what differs: trailing whitespace or carriage returns on the named lines, or the leading prefix the file
carries in addition to or instead of `old_string`'s, quoted as JSON. It then states that the held content_hash is still
current, asks that `new_string` carry the file's whitespace, and quotes the window's text as one JSON string, up to 30,000
characters. When several windows match at level 2 or 3, the reply names the level and their lines and quotes nothing. Level 4,
no match, `replace_all` and the stale-hash refusal keep today's replies, and `haet_edit` still applies a level-1 match only.
Recorded as [`PD-TOOLS-014`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-014), which narrows REQ-TOOLS-189's failure-to-match clause.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: keep the edit refused; name the matched lines and the
level, say what differs in words, quote the lines in REQ-TOOLS-134's `N: line` format and state that the hash is current, as a
directive narrowing REQ-TOOLS-189's miss clause. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: the same refusal and facts, the quote as one
JSON string, `replace_all` left unchanged, as a directive extending REQ-TOOLS-189 — and, inferred rather than measured, a CRLF
file on Windows (the only platform shipped, PD-STARTUP-001) where a multi-line `old_string` written with LF matches only at
level 2 and a re-read cannot show the `\r`. **The ruling followed both**: the position they share; from B the JSON quote (an
`N: line` quote shows neither a trailing space nor a `\r`), the CRLF case and `replace_all` unchanged; from A the 30,000-character
cap and the disposition Narrows, since in this case the reply no longer sends the caller to read again.

**The readings rejected, with their reasons.** *Applying the edit at level 2 or 3*: `applyMatch` writes `new_string` over a
level-3 window unshifted, and a caller whose `old_string` had the wrong indentation almost always wrote `new_string` from the
same belief, so the block would land at the wrong depth (a Markdown paragraph turned code block, a Python or YAML meaning
changed) beside a success; at level 2 it would drop trailing spaces (a Markdown hard break) and `\r` (mixed line endings);
and it undoes the exactness REQ-TOOLS-189 gives as the hash's whole reason. *Confirming the miss as built*: the build computes
the fact, discards it, and points the caller at a re-read that shows nothing new; the measured cost stays inside ceiling-bound
children. **Costs kept on record:** each near miss is still one failed call and one `tool_error` issue; a second
implementation built from the specification alone returns the plain miss; replies grow by up to the window's size.
**Built 2026-10-07 (fin32):** `nearMissMessage` and the level-3 `shifts` of `matchEdit`'s `EditMatch`
(`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`); pinned by five cases under "PD-TOOLS-014" in
`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts`, red on the code before, and one guarding the unchanged replies; the pack's six
level-3 misses replayed through the built tool each name their lines and apply when their quote is sent back on the same hash.
Every one of the six carried the same extra space in its `new_string` too, so `write_file`'s unshifted level-3 apply is raised
as OQ-233. The next default and duress live runs are the measurement (`live-run.mjs`'s near-miss NOTE). Finding D5 closes
with it.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** **NOT REACHED**: no
`haet_edit` missed at level 2 or 3 in any pack (the harness NOTE each time). Evidence: [`live-552d346-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-default-autopsy.md), [`live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md), [`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in
[`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-230 — Are the agents told what the product's own directories in the workspace are?** *(PD-TOOLS-012, the marker
directory among REQ-TOOLS-140's hard-coded ignore components; OQ-161's ruling (R-071), "the agents are not told that the
product wrote the exclude line"; OQ-215's ruling, "the agents' instructions are unchanged", and its remainder clause, "if that
remainder still has a measurable cost, it is raised as its own question"; REQ-TOOLS-140; REQ-MCP-099 and REQ-MCP-102, memories
that persist across runs; REQ-WORKSPACE-060, the always-active context units and their order; REQ-CONFIG-100, a configured
persona's prompt; REQ-CONFIG-013, the `.rotaris/` line in `.gitignore`. Raised 2026-10-07 from finding D4 of the final duress
live run at `a68f121` (pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z` of the live worktree, session `e6747bd0`, the self-hosted endpoint), and
ruled the same day.)*

The file tools are clean since PD-TOOLS-012: the six whole-tree `glob **/*` calls (#1, #24, #29, #73, #126, #135) and `**/.*`
(#65) list neither directory, and 0 file-tool calls name one. The remainder OQ-215 foresaw came through the terminal: b's
`ls -a` (#47), wave3's `ls -la`, `find . -type f` and four `git check-ignore` probes (#249, #250, #281, #283, #285, #286),
wave3b's `ls -a` of both (#354) — 21 calls and 32 rows, against 28 / 96 at `c2a9444` and 41 / 112 at `c2fdd6a`. It reached all
three things the user keeps: line 224 of the delivered `docs/verification.md` discusses the marker directory's files; the
answer's "Remains" (row 766) relays that `docs/overview.md` claims everything gitignored is absent while both are present; and
wave3's `edit_memory` #311 wrote into the project memory `todo-app/docs-pair` that both are present and "absence must be
checked with `ls`". The false absence claim was written by docs-writer c, which holds no terminal: the file tools hid the
directories, so it inferred absence. Recorded as
[`the-product-directories-reach-the-users-report-answer-and-memory-through-the-terminal.md`](../defects/fixed/the-product-directories-reach-the-users-report-answer-and-memory-through-the-terminal.md).

**What the build proceeds under.** OQ-161's and OQ-215's rulings as built: the directories hidden from the file tools, shown
by a terminal, and no agent told what they are.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether every agent is told (a context unit), only the agents that can see them (the terminal's
description), whether the runtime's data moves out of the tree or its memories are filtered, or whether the remainder is
accepted.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** every agent built for a session
receives one fixed product statement as its last always-active context unit, after REQ-WORKSPACE-060's four, whatever prompt
its persona carries. The statement names the workspace scope directory and the code-intelligence marker directory from their
single sources. It says four things: where present, they hold the application's own state; the application keeps them out of
version control with lines it writes itself (the marker's line only at a repository's top level); the file tools hide them and
a terminal shows them; and unless the task concerns them, they stay out of documents, reports, answers and project memories
and are not counted as changes. This is recorded as [`PD-TOOLS-012`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-012) revision 2, which
extends REQ-WORKSPACE-060 and revises the instructions clauses of OQ-161 (R-071) and OQ-215. The directory, the exclude line,
the tool descriptions and existing memories stay as built.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: tell every agent — one fixed product statement as the
last injected context unit, so a configured persona keeps it too, carrying the four points, named from the constants;
PD-TOOLS-012 revision 2. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: tell the agents that can see them — one fixed sentence in the
terminal tool's description, "where present", built from the same two constants; PD-TOOLS-012 revision 2 extending
REQ-TOOLS-095; and revision 1's first execution owes this pack's result. **The ruling followed A**: the false absence claim
came from a docs-writer, which holds no terminal, so B's sentence would reach only the checker, whose task concerned the
directories; A's unit reaches the writer and the checker alike. B's objection that REQ-CONFIG-100 drops a prompt line does not
hold for context units, which `run.ts` and `orchestration.ts` append after whatever prompt the persona carries. From B it took
the "where present" wording and the report-back of revision 1's first execution. **Rejected:** moving the runtime's data out
of the tree or filtering memories (each reaches one sink and contradicts REQ-MCP-034, REQ-MCP-099 and REQ-MCP-102); accepting
the remainder (a memory that compounds from run to run). **Costs kept on record:** about 80 tokens per request; a fifth unit
for black-box conformance; possible priming; an agent possibly holding back a relevant fact; a poorer fit for a user who tracks
the marker directory; no change to memories already written. **Reopening:** if a delivered document, the answer or a memory
still carries either directory when the task does not concern them, the question reopens for a write-side measure.
**Built 2026-10-07 (fin32):** `PRODUCT_DIRECTORIES_UNIT` (`packages/config/src/product-directories.ts`), pushed last by
`SkillHost.contextUnits` (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/skills.ts`) on every call; pinned by
`packages/config/src/product-directories.test.ts`, seven cases in `apps/desktop/src/run-host/skills.test.ts` red on the code
before, an engine guard in `packages/engine/src/run/record.test.ts`, and `pnpm mcp-proof`'s launch 1 reading the built app's
prompt. The statement is 599 characters, nearer 150 tokens than the ruling's estimate of about 80 (*corrected by the bundle's
review, 2026-10-07:* it left out point (b)'s last words, that elsewhere version control may list the marker's directory as
untracked; with them it is 662 characters, nearer 165 tokens). Finding D4 closes with it;
the next default and duress live runs are the measurement.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** the statement reached 144 of
144 agent requests at `552d346`'s default pack, 188 of 188 in its duress pack and 188 of 188 at `0bc3eee`; no delivered file
named either directory in any pack. At `0bc3eee` two coordinator briefs named both as tooling not to write about, the one
sign of priming. Read in [`PD-TOOLS-012`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-012)'s report-back. Evidence: [`live-552d346-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-default-autopsy.md), [`live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md),
[`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

<a id="oq-233"></a>

**OQ-233 — When `write_file`'s edit matches at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 3, is `new_string` shifted by the same prefix?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-136, the four match levels and "a window match replaces whole lines", silent on whether the replacement takes
the shift that let `old_string` match; REQ-TOOLS-135, the edit's report, which names the level. Raised 2026-10-07 by the
R-072 consortium while ruling OQ-231 (finding D5 of the final duress live run at `a68f121`), which does not decide it, and
recorded by fin32. The number lies in the range the round assigned fin33 (OQ-233 onward); whichever of the two lands second
takes the next free number. Ruled 2026-10-13 under R-072.)*

`applyMatch` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`) writes `new_string` over a level-3 window exactly as given, unshifted,
and reports "Match level: 3." beside the success; the case "level 3" in `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts` pins it
with a `new_string` that happens to sit at the file's depth. A caller whose `old_string` had the wrong indentation usually
wrote `new_string` from the same belief: in OQ-231's replay of the `a68f121` duress pack, all six level-3 misses of `haet_edit`
carried one space more than the file in both strings. Through `write_file` such an edit would have succeeded with the block one
space off — in Markdown a list item or code block changed, in Python or YAML a meaning changed — beside a success. Shifting
`new_string` by the same prefix breaks the opposite case, the one the test pins, where the caller wrote `new_string` at the
file's depth. The specification fixes neither reading.

**What the build proceeds under.** The unshifted write, as built.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a level-3 `write_file` edit shifts `new_string` by the window's prefix, writes it as given
(the build), or is refused with OQ-231's near-miss facts, as `haet_edit`'s now is.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** when `write_file`'s edit matches one
window only at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 3, the indentation of `new_string`'s first visible line decides the outcome. If it equals
`old_string`'s, `new_string` takes the window's shift. If it equals the file's, `new_string` is written as given. If `new_string`
holds no visible character, it is written as given (a deletion). Every other case is refused and nothing is written, with the
near-miss facts of `PD-TOOLS-014`. The success reply says which of the two applies. Recorded as
[`PD-TOOLS-015`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-015), which narrows REQ-TOOLS-136 and extends REQ-TOOLS-135 for `write_file`
only; `haet_edit` and `PD-TOOLS-014` are unchanged, and no earlier ruling is revised (`PD-TOOLS-014` left `write_file` to this
question).

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: shift `new_string` when its first non-blank line carries
`old_string`'s first-line indentation, say so after "Match level: 3.", and refuse every other level-3 case with OQ-231's
near-miss facts — `PD-TOOLS-015` narrowing REQ-TOOLS-136. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: shift `new_string` under the same
test, and otherwise write it as given with a reply saying "written as given; verify its indentation" — `PD-TOOLS-015` extending
REQ-TOOLS-136, which is silent on `new_string`. **The ruling followed both**: the shift both proposed, which repairs the measured
case (6 of 6 level-3 misses in the `a68f121` pack carried the same extra space in both strings); from B the as-given write for a
`new_string` at the file's depth or with no visible character, which reads unambiguously and as built writes correctly (A would
have refused the case the "level 3" test pins); from A the refusal, but only where the tool cannot tell what the caller meant (a
`new_string` at a depth equal to neither string's, a shallower shift a visible line cannot take), where B's "written as given"
would be the same silent wrong result this question exists to remove. The three conditions are disjoint because level 3 requires
the two first-line indentations to differ. **Rejected:** confirming the build (a known silent mis-indentation beside a success);
shifting unconditionally (breaks the as-given case); refusing every level-3 match as `haet_edit` does (wastes a call in the
common case, and PD-TOOLS-014's first execution found the retry with the quote and the model's own deeper `new_string` would
still land one space deep). **Costs kept on record:** one failed call and one REQ-SESSION-136 `tool_error` per ambiguous level-3
edit; `write_file` and `haet_edit` differ at level 3; an implementation built from the specification alone writes unshifted; a
rare double shift when a caller deliberately indents by exactly the prefix. **Set aside, raised as its own question:** both
advocates read from the code that a CRLF file meets `write_file`'s level-2 apply with mixed line endings; this ruling does not
decide it ([OQ-246](#oq-246)).
**Built 2026-10-13 (fin35):** `shiftNewString` and `writeFileTool`'s level-3 branch (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`),
the refusal through `nearMissMessage` in `write_file`'s wording; pinned by nine cases under "PD-TOOLS-015" in
`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts`, seven red on the code before; the `a68f121` pack's six level-3 misses replayed
through the built `write_file` over the rebuilt `docs/verification.md` each shifted to the file's depth (6 of 6). The first
execution is in place under the directive.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** **NOT REACHED**: no
`write_file` edit matched at level 3 or said "shifted". Evidence: [`live-552d346-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-default-autopsy.md), [`live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md), [`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

**OQ-234 — Does a child cut off at its per-agent timeout name, where the person sees the failure, the Settings control that
sets the limit?** *(REQ-ORCH-088, the expiry path and its fixed error "Child timed out after <N>s"; REQ-CONFIG-113,
`runtime.child_timeout`; [`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003), the Per-agent timeout control, and its
revision 2's notice detail for the other timeout a user can set; [`PD-ORCH-004`](../product/directives.md#pd-orch-004)
revisions 1 to 5, the cut-off statement and offer; REQ-MONITOR-040, -044, -052 and -069, what a tree row, a presented agent, the
inspector and an instance tab carry; REQ-MONITOR-041, -285 and -286; REQ-NOTIFY-092, -100 and -261; OQ-217's Outcome line;
OQ-218 and OQ-214, the rulings that kept the 1200 s default because a user can raise it. Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live
runs, by the ruling of finding D2 of the duress live run at `a68f121` (session `e6747bd0`), and recorded as the R-072
consortium's question CN1; ruled the same day.)*

In that run the testers `wave3-verify-all` (`bg_dcecf655`) and its continuation `wave3b-finish-verification` (`bg_98fa54d7`)
were each cut off at 1200 s while making progress (issues 14 and 19; the parent's calls `#248` and `#336` carry their
reports). Each row read `failed` and nothing else. "Child timed out after 1200s" reaches the parent model, the issue record and
the timeline, and no screen shows any of them; `AgentRecord` carries no end cause; the report artifact copies only the status
and the summary, so the one cause a person could read was the summariser's text (finding D9). The control that moves the limit
lives in Settings › Runtime, in minutes. Recorded as
[`a-child-cut-off-at-its-per-agent-timeout-reads-only-failed.md`](../defects/fixed/a-child-cut-off-at-its-per-agent-timeout-reads-only-failed.md).
What the specification does not settle is whether a surface that shows the agent ends with the limit and a pointer to its
control, and which surfaces those are.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a delegated agent whose stored
report carries REQ-ORCH-088's timeout error shows that error wherever its failure appears. Its delegation-tree row and its
Mission-table row carry a "timed out" tag after the state. The inspector (directly under its meta line) and the agent's
persona-window instance tab (directly under its state) carry one line, worded once: "Cut off at its per-agent timeout of
<limit>[ while making progress]. Settings › Runtime › Per-agent timeout sets this limit for runs started from now." The limit,
its default, the 30 s landing, the single continuation, REQ-ORCH-088's error, PD-ORCH-004's statement and offer, OQ-217's
Outcome line, the issues, the timeline, the Library document and the notices all stay as built. This is
[`PD-CONFIG-003`](../product/directives.md#pd-config-003) revision 3, which extends REQ-MONITOR-040, REQ-MONITOR-044,
REQ-MONITOR-052 and REQ-MONITOR-069.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)* recommended that every surface showing the agent — the
Mission table row, the tree row, the inspector and the persona window — carry one sentence giving the limit in minutes, whether
the agent was still working, and the path Settings › Runtime › Delegation limits › Per-agent timeout, with an inspector button
that opens Settings › Runtime, recorded as PD-CONFIG-003's next revision. *Advocate B (the system's lens)* recommended one
code-written line in two places only — under the inspector's meta line and in the persona window's instance tab — naming the
control and its current value, with the rows, the engine's records, the timeline and the notices left as built. Both kept the
runner's texts unchanged, since REQ-ORCH-088 fixes the error's form, PD-ORCH-004 is the owner's ruling and models cannot open
Settings. **The ruling followed both**: from A the row tag, where `failed` is first seen (a terminal agent never shows the
stalled tag, so the timeout tag takes its slot), and the making-progress distinction read from the cut-off statement, so a
looping child's line does not suggest a longer limit would have helped; from B the line's two placements and no new action, so
REQ-MONITOR-052's actions stay as listed. It departs from both in writing the path in the shape revision 2 built
("Settings › Runtime › <control>"), so the two timeouts follow one rule, and in stating no current value, which Settings shows
one step away.

**Built 2026-10-07 (fin33).** The settle writes REQ-ORCH-088's error through `childTimedOutMessage` and `timedOutOf` reads it
back with the cut-off statement (`packages/engine/src/children/cut-off.ts`); `toAgentRecord` fills `AgentRecord.timedOut` for an
agent presented `failed`; `timeoutLine` (`packages/ui/src/agents.ts`) words the line once, its path built from the labels
Settings renders. Found while drawing it: the tag beside the state squeezed the sidebar row's persona onto two lines and
scrolled the Mission card sideways, so it takes a line of its own under the state; recorded in PD-CONFIG-003's first execution
of revision 3. Pinned by `cut-off.test.ts`, `activity.test.ts`, `children.test.ts` and `agent-timeout.test.ts` (red on
`b90d27f`); shown by `pnpm mission-proof` item 1d. Repaired note:
[`a-child-cut-off-at-its-per-agent-timeout-reads-only-failed.md`](../defects/fixed/a-child-cut-off-at-its-per-agent-timeout-reads-only-failed.md).
**For the live run:** at D2's 45-minute duress launch, a child cut off reads "Cut off at its per-agent timeout of 45 minutes
while making progress. …" in the inspector and its persona window, and its rows carry the tag; the record carries
`timedOut: { limitSeconds: 2700, makingProgress: true }`. Not reached until a live run cuts a child off.

<a id="oq-235"></a>

**OQ-235 — Does the retrospective read user-global and machine-wide instruction files, or only the workspace's own?**
*(`PD-LIBRARY-002`, "Reach, and the boundary it holds": "SHALL NOT read outside the workspace: no other workspace's
record, no user-global location", and its rule's "the workspace's own `AGENTS.md` or `AGENTS.override.md` as
REQ-WORKSPACE-041 fixes discovery"; OQ-65's ruling under [R-071](../product/requests.md#r-071), "reads exactly the set
injection reads"; `PD-WORKSPACE-002`'s discovery bases; REQ-WORKSPACE-048. Raised 2026-10-13 from
[`pd-library-002-says-no-user-global-location-where-the-retrospective-reads-user-global-instruction-files.md`](../defects/fixed/pd-library-002-says-no-user-global-location-where-the-retrospective-reads-user-global-instruction-files.md),
the R-072 consortium's question LG1, and ruled the same day.)*

The run host served both readers of the instruction files from one computation (`SkillHost.instructionFiles`), and
since `PD-WORKSPACE-002` that computation discovers under the workspace root, the Rotaris global configuration directory,
`~/.agents`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.openhands` and `/etc/codex`. So the built retrospective read user-global and
machine-wide files the directive's reach clause rules out, while OQ-65's ruling said it reads exactly the set injection
reads. Two owner decisions (R-033's directive and R-071's ruling) disagreed on the record.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the two owner decisions are
reconciled by holding each to the question it answered. `PD-LIBRARY-002`'s reach clause (R-033) governs reach and
OQ-65's ruling (R-071) governs the switches. The retrospective reads the enabled instruction-file set injection computes,
restricted to the files discovered at the workspace root (the four root names, the per-file switches and
REQ-WORKSPACE-048's master switch all applied), and reads no file under the global, home-relative or machine-wide bases.
[`PD-LIBRARY-002`](../product/directives.md#pd-library-002) takes revision 2, which states that set in the rule paragraph
and keeps the reach clause word for word. Injection is unchanged: agents are still given every enabled base.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **B**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended keeping the wide read — the retrospective reads exactly the enabled set
  injection reads, user-global and machine-wide files included — with a revision 2 rewriting the reach clause to say so,
  and each instruction-file evidence entry labelled with its inventory source and absolute path so a global `AGENTS.md`
  cannot be mistaken for the workspace's own: the analysis would otherwise not know what agents were already told and
  would propose rules the user already keeps globally.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended restricting the read to the workspace root with the reach clause left
  whole: OQ-65 said "The discovery half is not the question. The switch half is the question", so R-071 never weighed
  reach, and the wide read produces evidence attributed only by file name, an `agents_md_update` carried out in the
  workspace against a file elsewhere, and one workspace's history proposing edits that govern every other workspace.

The ruling took B's substance. The executor takes its rollback point from the workspace's Git tree, so an approved
proposal to change `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` would have no undo under REQ-LIBRARY-116 and would change every other workspace
on the strength of this one's history; A's labelling fixes how such a proposal is cited and does nothing for either. A's
cost to the user is real but small: the analysis may miss a rule kept globally and propose a duplicate, which the human
gate catches, and global files still reach every agent through injection, whose effects the analysis sees in the session
history. From A it kept the form: a directive revision rather than an italic note, so the directive itself names the set.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin34, `fin34-library-and-intent`); its first execution is reported in `PD-LIBRARY-002`'s entry.*
`SkillHost.retrospectiveInstructionFiles` keeps the `workspace:` entries of the enabled set and logs "retrospective: N of
M enabled instruction file(s) at the workspace root (ids)"; `dispatch`'s `retrospective.capture` passes it. Pinned by
four cases in `apps/desktop/src/run-host/skills.test.ts`, red before the change.

**OQ-236 — Which further requirements does `PD-LIBRARY-002` reach, under which verb, and what does its start gesture do
while an analysis runs?** *(`PD-LIBRARY-002`'s disposition block; REQ-LIBRARY-011, REQ-LIBRARY-020, REQ-LIBRARY-109,

the note OQ-222's ruling left for these reaches, as the R-072 consortium's question LR1, and ruled the same day.)*

OQ-222 entered the four reaches the back-pointers already marked into `PD-LIBRARY-002`'s Extends line and left the rest:
the artifact container's non-null `source_session_id`, the parser's backfill of the current session, the indicators' fixed

the Overview hint the build had already rewritten, the Library's two fixed texts, and the post-run notices' fixed titles.
Each carried neither a note nor a disposition. Both advocates also found the retrospective's two buttons disabled while
any analysis runs, against REQ-LIBRARY-125's "no control … may be disabled while analysis runs", while the palette entry
queued the same command.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):**
[`PD-LIBRARY-002`](../product/directives.md#pd-library-002) gains a revision 2. It Narrows REQ-LIBRARY-011,
REQ-LIBRARY-020, REQ-LIBRARY-109, REQ-LIBRARY-124, REQ-LIBRARY-125, REQ-LIBRARY-130 and REQ-NOTIFY-250, and adds
REQ-LIBRARY-126 and REQ-LIBRARY-128 to its Extends line. The palette entry, REQ-LIBRARY-127 and REQ-LIBRARY-174 take no
disposition. The build changes in two places. The Library's two REQ-LIBRARY-109 texts name the retrospective as a second
source. The retrospective's start gesture stays available while a post-run analysis is queued or running, queues behind
it, and is refused on all three surfaces only while a retrospective is already queued or running in that workspace, with

exhaustively.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**, each on the points below:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended Narrows for REQ-LIBRARY-011, -020, -109, -124, -125 and -130 and Extends for
  REQ-LIBRARY-126, -128 and REQ-NOTIFY-250, the built hint ratified, the Library's two texts naming both sources, and the
  gesture disabled only while a retrospective is queued or running in the workspace, refused there with one info notice so
