- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended one test for every verb — Narrows where a fixed text departs, Extends where
  the retrospective sits beside a requirement — giving Narrows for REQ-LIBRARY-020, -125 and REQ-NOTIFY-250 and Extends for
  REQ-LIBRARY-011, -109, -126 and -128, REQ-LIBRARY-130's hint restored word for word, and the two buttons never disabled.

The ruling applied B's test to every requirement. On REQ-LIBRARY-011 it followed A: that requirement marks
`collector_model` and `notes` nullable and leaves `source_session_id` non-null, and the same container stores
retrospective artifacts, so a null there departs. On REQ-NOTIFY-250 it followed B: its "only while that analysis is in

and ratified the built hint, which has the same shape as the two REQ-LIBRARY-109 texts A rightly found false of the
retrospective rows beneath them. On the gesture it followed A's narrower refusal: a second retrospective over an unchanged
workspace reads the same evidence and duplicate suppression discards its proposals, so B's "always enabled" spends the
owner's tokens for nothing. Revision 2 rests on the R-072 precedents B cited.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin34, `fin34-library-and-intent`); its first execution is reported in `PD-LIBRARY-002`'s entry and in

<a id="oq-237"></a>

**OQ-237 — May two directives narrow, or extend, one requirement?** *(`docs/product/README.md`, "Identifiers", "The shape
of an entry" and "The back-pointer, in place": the meaning of Narrows and Extends, and the generator's refusal of a second
directive under one verb on one requirement, "precedence must be unambiguous"; `tools/symbol-artifact/generate.mjs`, the
per-verb maps that hold one directive per requirement; acceptance finding F15, the shape repaired for `PD-ORCH-014`.
Raised 2026-10-13 from
[`a-requirement-two-directives-narrow-can-name-only-one-so-the-second-is-recorded-under-another-verb.md`](../defects/fixed/a-requirement-two-directives-narrow-can-name-only-one-so-the-second-is-recorded-under-another-verb.md),
noticed 2026-10-07 by fin31's reviewer, and ruled the same day under the owner's delegation; the consortium's question GV1.)*

The generator keeps `SUPERSEDED_BY`, `NARROWED_BY` and `EXTENDED_BY` as one directive per requirement each and refuses a
second under any verb. Three builds met it and wrote a disposition under a verb its ruling did not name, or left it out:
`PD-TOOLS-013` lists REQ-TOOLS-112 and REQ-SESSION-136 under **Extends** though it adds a member to a closed set and removes
an issue (OQ-226); `PD-CONFIG-003` names REQ-CONFIG-256 and REQ-CONFIG-417 as narrowed where its ruling named them extended
(OQ-218); `PD-SHELL-009` carries its ruling's REQ-SHELL-021 through REQ-SHELL-122 (OQ-206). `PD-WORKSPACE-002` left
REQ-CONFIG-464 out altogether, its own text saying "no single revision could honestly hold" the two halves; revisions of
`PD-TOOLS-006` and `PD-ORCH-006` hold narrowings that "land here whatever [they are] about", and `PD-MONITOR-004` holds a
revision minted as a directive of its own and folded into it at a landing because "the symbol generator refuses two
directives narrowing one requirement". The generated
artifact answers "Extended by PD-TOOLS-013 … This still governs in full" for a requirement that no longer does.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the register may hold several directives under Narrows or Extends on one requirement,
on what terms, and which dispositions the one-per-verb rule bent.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the symbol generator admits several
directives under **Narrows** and under **Extends** on one requirement, each verb's reach held as a list. **Supersedes** stays
one per requirement, and a superseded requirement may be neither narrowed nor extended. Two directives that narrow one
requirement state disjoint cases; at least one of the two names the other in its own entry, and the generator refuses the
pair otherwise; a case that overlaps an earlier narrowing is written as a revision of that directive. Extends carries no
citation rule, since nothing is displaced. Every disposition the one-per-verb rule bent is corrected to the verb its ruling
and the README's definitions give (`PD-TOOLS-013`, `PD-SHELL-009`, `PD-WORKSPACE-002`), and `docs/product/README.md` is
amended in place. No requirement's behaviour departs, so no directive is minted.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended lists for Narrows and Extends, a later directive naming every earlier one under
  the same verb, Supersedes single, and every bent disposition corrected so each requirement's label says what governs:
  REQ-SHELL-021's only note says the replacement route is governed "in full", and a builder trusting REQ-TOOLS-112's label
  could remove `interrupted` again. A bounded re-read of the requirements two directives already reach.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same lists, with Supersedes beside Extends refused as Supersedes beside
  Narrows already is, the lists emitted sorted, the citation required of a second narrowing only, and the "lands here
  whatever it is about" sentences marked as no longer binding; REQ-CONFIG-256 and REQ-CONFIG-417 move to Narrows under
  `PD-WORKSPACE-002` by the F15 test.

The ruling agreed with both that "precedence must be unambiguous" holds for Supersedes alone: two replacements leave no
governing text, while two narrowings stating disjoint cases leave the requirement governing outside both, and two
extensions displace nothing. It took B on the four points they differed (no citation for Extends; Supersedes beside Extends
refused; sorted lists; the catch-all sentences marked) and A's bounded re-read, limited to the requirements two directives
reach, since only there could the rule have bent a verb. Its own change: the citation check is order-independent ("at
least one of the pair names the other"), because order in `directives.md` follows the domain, not the date.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin34, `fin34-record-and-cancels`); the first execution is reported in `docs/product/README.md`.*
**The bounded re-read, what it found.** Of the fifteen requirements two directives reached, read under the README's
definitions and the exact-enumeration test: corrected to Narrows, the six the ruling named (REQ-TOOLS-112 and
REQ-SESSION-136 under `PD-TOOLS-013`; REQ-SHELL-021 under `PD-SHELL-009`; REQ-CONFIG-464, REQ-CONFIG-256 and REQ-CONFIG-417
under `PD-WORKSPACE-002`), and three it did not: **REQ-TOOLS-152 under `PD-ORCH-004`**, whose field list calls itself "the
whole of the `delegate` contract" and gains `continuation_of` (R-058 had recorded Extends because "the symbol artifact holds
one narrowing directive per requirement", the rule bending a verb the note did not list), and **REQ-LIBRARY-099 and
REQ-TOOLS-148 under `PD-LIBRARY-001`**, whose closed section sets gain `commands`. **Found nothing** at REQ-CHAT-057 and
REQ-CHAT-069 (`PD-CHAT-005`'s colour and indent leave every stated figure whole), REQ-ORCH-075 (`PD-ORCH-015` adds the held
answer to a payload the requirement does not close), REQ-SESSION-115 (`PD-LIBRARY-003` keeps the exact budgets and changes
only how an edited artifact is read), REQ-SHELL-119 (`PD-SHELL-003`'s title-bar control enters the same guards),
REQ-STARTUP-161 (`PD-SHELL-001`'s window is a window of the one instance, and the closed set there is the launch outcomes,
untouched) and REQ-WORKSPACE-041 (`PD-LIBRARY-002`'s retrospective reads what discovery finds). Every pair of narrowings the
register now holds names each other. The generator's one-per-verb reason is marked as no longer binding wherever the
register still gave it in the present tense: beside the "lands here" sentences of `PD-TOOLS-006` and `PD-ORCH-006`, at
`PD-MONITOR-004`'s folded revision, and at `PD-ORCH-003`'s "it would also be refused" (whose supersession half still holds).
**Checked again at the landing rebase** (2026-10-13), against every disposition `origin/main` then carried, those landed while
this was built included (`PD-CONFIG-003` revision 3, `PD-LIBRARY-002` revision 2's seven narrowings and two extensions,
`PD-ORCH-011` revision 2): none was bent by the one-per-verb rule, since each requirement they name under a verb carries no
other directive under it, so nothing more is corrected. Outside the bound and recorded, not corrected:
[`pd-library-001-extends-two-requirements-whose-closed-sets-it-changes.md`](../defects/fixed/pd-library-001-extends-two-requirements-whose-closed-sets-it-changes.md).
**Corrected the same day** (fin36, `fin36-last-notes-and-optionals`): on the same test `PD-LIBRARY-001` now narrows REQ-LIBRARY-088
(a closed field inventory gaining `commands[]`) and REQ-LIBRARY-090 (a fixed section order gaining **Commands**), the disposition
it replaces quoted beside it and the two back-pointers relabelled; no other directive reaches either, and no behaviour moves.
Whether another directive that alone reaches a requirement carries the same shape is still not swept.

<a id="oq-238"></a>

**OQ-238 — Does every call its run cancels read `interrupted`, or only the terminal's?** *(PD-ORCH-005 clause 3, a call the
rest cut off "is recorded as interrupted"; `PD-TOOLS-013`, the terminal's cancel; REQ-SESSION-136, the outcome-driven
issues; REQ-TOOLS-092 and REQ-SANDBOX-025, fetch's closed vocabulary; REQ-SESSION-139, the histogram's four derived
buckets; ADR-0023's reading of the run's abort mid-fetch as `network_error`; OQ-208, no `outcome_kind` on an MCP or fetch
record. Raised 2026-10-13 from
[`a-call-the-run-cancels-in-the-gate-or-in-fetch-files-a-tool-error-issue.md`](../defects/fixed/a-call-the-run-cancels-in-the-gate-or-in-fetch-files-a-tool-error-issue.md),
noticed by the consortium while ruling OQ-226 and recorded by fin31, and ruled the same day under the owner's delegation;
the consortium's question GC1.)*

`PD-TOOLS-013` made the terminal's cancelled call read `interrupted` and file no issue. Three sibling paths still read a cancel
as a failure. The gate's catch writes `cancelled` for an executor that throws once the signal is aborted
(`packages/agent-tools/src/gate.ts`), a kind no vocabulary holds; fetch writes `network_error`, the kind of a real transport
fault (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/fetch.ts`, `transportFailure`); and the MCP executor's catch writes `execution_error`
(`apps/desktop/src/run-host/mcp.ts`), though its SDK call receives the run's signal (`packages/mcp/src/client.ts`). All three
fall through to the gate's `tool_error` warning, which `summary.md`'s Tool errors line counts, while the turn already answers
each call as interrupted (`callSignal.aborted`). A record with failure kind `interrupted` and no `outcome_kind` (those three,
and a released delegation wait) derives into the histogram's `tool_error` bucket.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether every call its run cancels reads `interrupted` and files no issue, which requirements that
departs from, and where such a call is counted in REQ-SESSION-139's histogram.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** [`PD-TOOLS-013`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-013)
revision 2, retitled "a call its run cancels reads `interrupted`", governs every tool call cut off by its run's signal: the
gate's catch, fetch and the MCP executor as well as the terminal. Each such call is recorded with failure kind
`interrupted` and a detail saying the run cancelled it before it completed, and files no outcome-driven issue. When it
carries no `outcome_kind`, the tool-outcomes histogram counts it under `interrupted`. A deadline that expired first still
reads `timeout`, and a fetch keeps its eight other kinds unchanged. The revision narrows REQ-TOOLS-092 and REQ-SANDBOX-025
(fetch's vocabulary gains `interrupted`, `InterruptedError`) and REQ-SESSION-139 (a fifth derived bucket); OQ-208's
reading stands, since no record gains an `outcome_kind`.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended that a call the run cancels read `interrupted` and file no issue whatever its
  tool, the MCP executor included, with fetch's vocabulary widened by a revision of `PD-TOOLS-013` narrowing REQ-TOOLS-092,
  and the histogram counting such a call under `interrupted`, since under any other reading `summary.md` would still count
  a quit as a tool error.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same three repairs as revision 2 of `PD-TOOLS-013`, retitled, narrowing
  REQ-SANDBOX-025 beside REQ-TOOLS-092 (it "mints no further kind" on its own), and the MCP catch testing the allowance
  timeout before the abort, as fetch tests its deadline first.

The ruling took B's record shape (REQ-SANDBOX-025 narrowed; the timeout tested first in MCP) and A's histogram (a
one-line derivation of REQ-SESSION-139). Leaving MCP out would reopen the same defect under a new name. The ruling named
REQ-SESSION-139 as extended and kept REQ-TOOLS-112 and REQ-SESSION-136 as extended; [OQ-237](#oq-237), ruled and built the
same day, reads a change to an exact enumeration as a narrowing, so the revision narrows all three (recorded in the
directive's disposition).

<a id="oq-239"></a>

**OQ-239 — Does the launch dialog owe the unattended advisory for `ask` and `restricted`?** *(REQ-TOOLS-072, "before the
application starts an unattended run"; REQ-TOOLS-192, "a run whose session will have no approval presenter"; REQ-SANDBOX-107,
"whenever the session being started would be unattended"; `PD-TOOLS-002`, which empties the advisory for `autonomous` and
says that for `ask` and `restricted` it "behaves as today"; REQ-TOOLS-053, REQ-TOOLS-069, REQ-SANDBOX-101 and ADR-0019, what
makes a run attended; REQ-SANDBOX-130, the disclosure shown "when that advisory is empty". Raised 2026-10-13 from
[`the-unattended-advisory-is-empty-for-every-mode-where-pd-tools-002-keeps-it-for-ask-and-restricted.md`](../defects/fixed/the-unattended-advisory-is-empty-for-every-mode-where-pd-tools-002-keeps-it-for-ask-and-restricted.md),
recorded 2026-10-07 at OQ-222's request, and ruled the same day under the owner's delegation; the consortium's question UA1.)*

`unattendedAdvisory` (`packages/ui/src/StartSessionDialog.tsx`) took the permission mode, whether confinement was active and
the permissive opt-in, discarded all three and returned `''`, so the "Start session" dialog never showed the advisory, and its
comment said the `ask`/`restricted` behaviour was kept. `apps/desktop/src/renderer/main.tsx` read the mode for it and passed
`allowUnsandboxedAutonomous: false`, "the side that produces the advisory". Whether `''` is right for `ask` and `restricted`
was not settled.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a run the dialog starts can be unattended at launch, and so whether the three advisory
requirements owe it any text.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the Start session dialog's
unattended advisory is empty for every permission mode, **confirmed as built**. Every run that dialog starts is attended at
launch (REQ-TOOLS-053, REQ-TOOLS-069, REQ-SANDBOX-101, ADR-0019), so the unattended-launch condition that REQ-TOOLS-072,
REQ-TOOLS-192 and REQ-SANDBOX-107 (as `PD-TOOLS-002` narrows them) attach the advisory to never holds on that surface, and
those requirements are met as written. The misleading comment and the dead inputs are corrected and the reason is pinned by a
test. **Forward guard:** a future surface that can start a run with no registered presenter must have the advisory's text
re-ruled before it shows one, because under `PD-TOOLS-002` the settings the old text named
(`runtime.allow_unsandboxed_autonomous`, the downgrade to `ask`) are inert or insufficient. No directive, no specification
text and no back-pointer change.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended confirming the empty advisory as built for all three modes, since every
  dialog start is attended and a non-empty advisory would show a false sentence on every default launch; correct the code
  and the record to say why, pin it with a test that renders the dialog, and close the note.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same reading as a record-only amendment: an OQ entry, the comment
  corrected, the behaviour pinned, the note moved; and a guard that a windowless launch surface re-rules the text first.

The ruling labelled it confirm-as-built, as A did: the code comment, the inputs and the test are more than a record-only
amendment. It took B's forward guard and A's render-level test, so REQ-SANDBOX-130's disclosure is shown to survive the empty
advisory. The evidence it checked: `PresenterRegistry.attended` is true while a window is registered and liveness has not
lapsed (`packages/agent-tools/src/approvals.ts`); each main window registers on creation (`main-windows.ts`,
`registerPresenter`; `index.ts`); the last window closing quits (`window-all-closed`); and `ed1c167` shows the function
already returned `''` for `ask` and `restricted` before `PD-TOOLS-002`, so "as today" never meant visible text. The
liveness-lapse edge is narrow: a start reaches the run host through main, the process whose reply clears the lapse, and the
run reports any refusal as REQ-SANDBOX-107 allows.

**As built (2026-10-13, fin34):** `unattendedAdvisory()` takes no input and returns `''`, its comment stating this ruling;
the renderer's launch state no longer carries `permissionMode` or `allowUnsandboxedAutonomous`, and the dialog is given
`unattendedAdvisory()`. The `advisory` prop and the `start-session-advisory` paragraph stay as REQ-TOOLS-192's presentation
seam. Pinned by `packages/ui/src/start-session-advisory.test.ts` (its first case red on the old form: the function took one
input). Nothing a user sees changes.

**OQ-221 — Which budget and which dropping rule govern a delegated child's attached artifacts, and what is the caller told?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-152, the attached-artifact section budgeted at 100,000 characters, "the first whose full body would carry the
section past the budget is dropped, and so is every attachment after it", "the observation warns how many were dropped for
size"; REQ-TOOLS-153, "any attachment warning"; REQ-TOOLS-154 item (4); REQ-LIBRARY-098, the `PRIOR AGENT CONTEXT (FULL)`
block "within a 48,000-character budget"; REQ-ORCH-032; domain 05's resolution 26 and limits inventory; `PD-SESSION-002`,
which counts the block's elisions. Raised 2026-10-07 from
[`the-attached-artifact-budget-is-48000-characters-where-req-tools-152-sets-100000-and-drops-every-later-one.md`](../defects/fixed/the-attached-artifact-budget-is-48000-characters-where-req-tools-152-sets-100000-and-drops-every-later-one.md),
recorded by fin28 while building `PD-SESSION-002`; the consortium's question AB1, numbered OQ-221 as the round assigned. Ruled
the same day.)*

Two requirements budget one block differently, and the build followed neither whole: it used REQ-LIBRARY-098's 48,000
(`FULL_CONTEXT_BUDGET`, `packages/engine/src/artifacts/context.ts`), skipped an overflowing body and kept trying the later ones,
where REQ-TOOLS-152 drops every attachment after the first that overflows, and its observation said "N artifacts were attached
to its context", counting the references that resolved at delegation before any budget applied
(`resolveAttachments`, `packages/engine/src/children/orchestration.ts`). A caller could be told of an artifact its child never
received, and no observation warned how many were dropped for size.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the `PRIOR AGENT CONTEXT (FULL)`
block, the attached-artifact section of a delegated child's payload, is budgeted at REQ-TOOLS-152's 100,000 characters.
Attachments are taken in the caller's order and each body is carried whole or not at all. A body that would carry the section
past the budget is left out, and every later attachment is still tried. The delegate observation is computed at acceptance by
the same selection that assembles the block: it states how many attachments the child will be given, and names the ids left
out for size (citing the budget), the references that could not be resolved and the attachments whose document could not be
read. `PD-SESSION-002`'s count then reads the distinct agent-and-artifact pairs whose body did not fit the 100,000-character
section after the attachments carried before it; for every child whose payload was assembled, those are exactly the ids its
observation named as left out for size. Recorded as [`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) **revision 5**
(the ruling text names it revision 4; revision 4 is OQ-216's, landed in `e02a308`, and the round assigned this one revision 5),
which narrows REQ-TOOLS-152 and REQ-LIBRARY-098 to this rule: that directive holds REQ-TOOLS-152's one narrowing slot, and
revision 3 states that a narrowing of `delegate`'s fields lands there. REQ-TOOLS-153 keeps governing, since its "any attachment
warning" defers the warning's content to REQ-TOOLS-152, and REQ-TOOLS-154's order is unchanged. `PD-SESSION-002` gains a dated
cross-reference note and no revision.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)* recommended the 100,000 budget with the build's
skip-and-continue, carried by `PD-TOOLS-006` as a narrowing of REQ-TOOLS-152 and REQ-LIBRARY-098, and an observation counting
only what the child receives, naming each id left out for size, unresolved or unreadable. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*
recommended REQ-TOOLS-152 whole: 100,000 with the prefix rule (the first overflowing attachment and every one after it dropped),
an observation stating how many the child carries and how many were dropped for size, and a new `PD-LIBRARY-005` narrowing
REQ-LIBRARY-098's 48,000. The advocates agreed that the budget is 100,000, that the observation is a defect against faithful
requirements, and that the observation and the block must share one selection. **The ruling followed A** on the dropping rule:
resolution 26 gave its reasons as determinism, preserved order and never-partial bodies, and skip-and-continue keeps all three
while never displacing an earlier attachment, so the child always receives a superset of what the prefix rule gives; under the
prefix rule a short attachment withheld for its position costs the same characters plus a turn through `artifact_read`. B's
strongest point, that a bare count does not identify what is missing, is answered by naming the ids. B's point about the
narrowing slot was settled earlier: the generator admits one narrowing directive per requirement, and revision 3 places a
narrowing of `delegate`'s fields in `PD-TOOLS-006`. A's fallback of a `PD-LIBRARY-005` narrowing only REQ-LIBRARY-098 was
rejected, since it would leave REQ-TOOLS-152's prefix rule governing. From B the ruling adopted that the dropped-for-size count
is required content, and B's boundary and unreadable-in-the-middle tests.

*Built 2026-10-07 (fin29, `fin29-delegate-admission`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 5.*
`FULL_CONTEXT_BUDGET` is 100,000 and `fullContextBlock` counts the separator between sections (`packages/engine/src/artifacts/context.ts`);
`selectAttachments` is the one selection the observation at acceptance and the block at assembly read, and `AttachmentOutcome`
carries `given`, `elidedForSize`, `unresolved`, `unreadable` and `budget` (`packages/engine/src/children/orchestration.ts`,
`delegation.ts`); `attachmentWarnings` renders it (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/delegation.ts`). Pinned by
`artifacts/artifacts.test.ts`, `children/children.test.ts` and `tools/delegation.test.ts`, red on the code before, and shown in the
built app by `pnpm artifacts-proof` launch 7. **What a live run then shows:** only when a `delegate` call uses `attach_artifacts`
(none of the four autopsied runs did): within 100,000 characters every attachment reaches the child whole and the observation says
how many; over it, the observation names the id left out for size with the budget, a later attachment that fits is still carried,
the child's block names the same id, the `context_selection` entry's `attached_elided` lists it and `summary.md`'s Mostly-elided
line counts it.

<a id="oq-245"></a>

**OQ-245 — Does a child's report list every file a cross-file code-intelligence EDIT call changed, or the path its arguments
name?** *(`PD-ORCH-004` revision 1's changed-paths clause, "the workspace paths the child's own file-writing calls changed", and
its report-back "The changed-paths reading falsified" (fin32), which took the argument path as a literal reading open for the
owner; REQ-ORCH-109, a report "cannot conceal files it failed to account for", and OQ-111's ruling; REQ-ORCH-108's edited files;
REQ-LIBRARY-088 and REQ-LIBRARY-090, the artifact's Edited Files; REQ-MCP-015, the EDIT tier of coding-agent, tester and
refactorer. Raised 2026-10-13 from PD-ORCH-004's report-back and ruled the same day; the number is the round's assigned one.)*

fin32 made the EDIT tier's calls file-writing calls and reads the path each changed from its arguments
(`codeIntelligenceEditPaths`). For the two cross-file tools the arguments name less than the call changes: a symbol rename is
listed by the declaring file alone, a whole-project cross-file replacement by nothing, and a directory-scoped one by the
directory. A child whose only writes are such calls is told to its parent as having changed no workspace paths, and the pass's
facts read "Edited files: (none)" — D1's falsehood for the two tools a refactorer exists to use. Recorded as
[`a-cross-file-code-intelligence-edit-is-reported-by-its-argument-path-alone.md`](../defects/fixed/a-cross-file-code-intelligence-edit-is-reported-by-its-argument-path-alone.md).

**What the build proceeds under.** fin32's literal reading: the argument path, none for a whole-project replacement.

**What a ruling decides.** Where the list of a cross-file call's files comes from — the arguments, the server's result text, or
the workspace observed around the call — and what the report says when that source cannot name them.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a delegated child's report lists every
workspace file that a cross-file code-intelligence EDIT call (a symbol rename, a cross-file replacement) changed. The run host
learns these files by observing the files the call can reach, before and after the call, whatever the call returned. This
replaces fin32's literal reading (the argument path alone), which is falsified and kept beside its replacement in
`PD-ORCH-004`'s report-back. When the observation could not be completed, the report names what it does know, says that the call
may have changed files the record cannot name, and never says the child changed no workspace paths. No directive is minted:
`PD-ORCH-004` already asks for the paths the calls "changed", so this repairs a defect against that wording and REQ-ORCH-109.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: overturn the literal reading; observe the workspace the call
can reach (the project for a rename; the directory, or the project, for a cross-file replacement) before and after it, whether
it succeeds or errs, subtract other agents' recorded writes in the window, and carry the result as a product-owned field the
model never sees — a repair of PD-ORCH-004 and REQ-ORCH-109 with no new directive. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: `PD-ORCH-004`
revision 6; read a cross-file replacement's files from its applied summary, list a rename by its declaring file with a counted
statement, and say plainly when the result names fewer files than the call may have changed; no worktree observation, since
siblings share the workspace and a terminal writes outside every count. **The ruling followed both**: from A the observation,
the only source that tells the truth in every case (the pinned runtime's rename returns a count and no file, and a cross-file
replacement writes file by file, so a failure part-way leaves files written under an error result, which parsing the result
would hide); from B the plain "may have changed files the record cannot name" statement when the observation was not completed,
and a proof that needs no language server. B's attribution concern is real and taken with A's mitigation; the bound that remains
is stated: a sibling's terminal write in the window can still be listed under this child, and REQ-ORCH-109 and `report.ts`'s own
policy prefer overstating to concealing. *(Written down 2026-10-13 by fin36, from fin35's review: the same bound covers a
sibling's own code-intelligence EDIT call landing in the window, since only the native tools are journaled.)* **Rejected:** confirming the literal reading (a known false "changed no workspace
paths" and a directory listed as a file); parsing the server's text (cannot name a rename's files, hides a partial failure,
couples the product to unpinned prose); deferral (a refactorer's rename is ordinary first-release use).
**Built 2026-10-13 (fin35):** the manifest's `scope`, `codeIntelligenceEdit`, `observeReach` and `WriteJournal`
(`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/observe.ts`) around the MCP executor, and `writeReadingOf` in the report and the cut-off;
pinned by cases in five test files, red on the code before, and `pnpm code-intel-proof`'s ninth launch (`child-across`, red on
the unrepaired build with `[]`, green with both files). The report-back is in `PD-ORCH-004`; the note is
[fixed](../defects/fixed/a-cross-file-code-intelligence-edit-is-reported-by-its-argument-path-alone.md).
*Measured for the rename 2026-10-13 (fin42, N59):* `pnpm code-intel-proof`'s tenth launch (`child-rename`) renames a TypeScript
function across two files through the language server after a reference search, and the child's report and artifact list exactly
both; its eleventh (`child-rename-cold`), the rename alone, lists exactly the one file it changed — the observation holds — and
finds the runtime's rename reaching the declaring file alone, recorded as
[`a-symbol-rename-that-is-the-servers-first-cross-file-request-renames-the-declaring-file-alone`](../defects/a-symbol-rename-that-is-the-servers-first-cross-file-request-renames-the-declaring-file-alone.md)
and raised as [OQ-272](#oq-272). Not measured: a live run (the opt-in `rename` scenario, written). The report-back is in
`PD-ORCH-004`, in place.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** **NOT REACHED**: 0
code-intelligence EDIT-tier calls in any pack; the duress tester held the tier and wrote through `write_file` and `haet_edit`.
Evidence: [`live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-duress-autopsy.md), [`live-552d346-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-552d346-default-autopsy.md), [`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

<a id="oq-246"></a>

**OQ-246 — When `write_file`'s edit matches at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 2, does the replacement keep the window's line endings
and trailing whitespace?** *(REQ-TOOLS-136, level 2 "exact after trailing whitespace is stripped from every line on both sides"
and "a window match replaces whole lines"; REQ-TOOLS-135, the success that reports the lines changed; `PD-STARTUP-001`, Windows
the only platform shipped; `PD-TOOLS-014`, `haet_edit`'s near miss, which quotes the `\r`. Raised 2026-10-13 by fin35 from the
case both advocates of OQ-233's ruling read from the code, which that ruling set aside. The number is the next after the round's
assigned OQ-245, taken by this plan; if another plan lands it first, this one takes the next free number. Ruled 2026-10-13
under R-072.)*

On a CRLF file a multi-line `old_string` written with `\n` alone matches only at level 2, and `applyMatch`
(`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`) writes `new_string`'s `\n`-only lines over the window's `\r\n` lines: the file is
left with mixed line endings, and the success counts an unchanged line as changed because it lost its `\r`. The same apply drops
a replaced line's trailing spaces that `new_string` does not repeat (a Markdown hard break). Probed and recorded as
[`a-write-file-edit-at-match-level-2-on-a-crlf-file-writes-lf-lines-among-crlf-ones.md`](../defects/fixed/a-write-file-edit-at-match-level-2-on-a-crlf-file-writes-lf-lines-among-crlf-ones.md).
The specification fixes neither keeping the window's endings nor writing `new_string`'s.

**What the build proceeds under.** The apply as built: `new_string`'s lines written as given.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a level-2 `write_file` edit carries each window line's line ending (and trailing whitespace)
into the replacement, writes `new_string` as given, or is refused with `PD-TOOLS-014`'s level-2 near-miss facts, as `haet_edit`'s
is.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** when a `write_file` edit
(`replace_all` false) matches one window at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 2, every line of `new_string` that pairs with an identical line of
`old_string` is written as the window's own line, byte for byte, its trailing whitespace and `\r` included. At levels 2, 3 and 4,
a window whose terminated lines all end in `\r` gives a `\r` to each other replacement line that a line break follows (a window
with no terminated line takes the reading from the file's other lines), and when such a `\r` is added the success says so in
one sentence, `new_string was written with the file's CRLF line endings.` Recorded as
[`PD-TOOLS-016`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-016), which extends REQ-TOOLS-136 (its silence on what a window match's
replacement lines carry) and REQ-TOOLS-135 (the sentence); level 1, `replace_all`, several windows, `haet_edit` and `haet`
(`PD-TOOLS-014`) and `PD-TOOLS-015`'s level-3 decision and refusal are unchanged.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: `PD-TOOLS-016`; pair `new_string`'s lines with
`old_string`'s by an exact-text line LCS and write every paired line as the window's own; give a CRLF window's other lines `\r`
at levels 2 to 4; add the CRLF sentence to the success. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: `PD-TOOLS-016`; the same line-ending
rule at levels 2 to 4, but pair only the leading and trailing runs of equal lines, because a second implementation could not
reproduce an LCS; leave the success unchanged. **The ruling followed both**: from both the line-ending rule at levels 2, 3 and 4
(they share `applyMatch`, so an LF `old_string` with a typo on a CRLF file writes the same mixed endings at level 4), and the
rejection of a level-2 refusal (the retry matches at level 1 and writes `new_string`'s LF lines anyway); from A the LCS pairing,
since B's runs leave an unchanged interior line (the Markdown hard break the defect note names) losing its trailing spaces and
counted as changed, and B's objection holds only while the tie-break goes unstated — `lcsChanges` in `diff.ts` already settles
it, and the directive writes the walk out; from A the success sentence, after `PD-TOOLS-015`'s precedent. Added by the ruling: a
window with no terminated line takes its reading from the file. **Rejected:** confirming as built (silent mixed line endings
and a success that counts an untouched line as changed, on the only platform shipped, `PD-STARTUP-001`); refusing level 2 as
`haet_edit` does; amending the record only; deferring. **Costs kept on record:** a window edit can no longer convert CRLF lines
to LF nor strip an unchanged line's trailing whitespace (`overwrite` or an exact level-1 `old_string` still can); where
`old_string` repeats a line, the walk fixes which copy's bytes a paired line takes; `write_file` and `haet_edit` still differ at
level 2; an implementation built from the specification alone writes `new_string` as given. Closes
[`a-write-file-edit-at-match-level-2-on-a-crlf-file-writes-lf-lines-among-crlf-ones`](../defects/fixed/a-write-file-edit-at-match-level-2-on-a-crlf-file-writes-lf-lines-among-crlf-ones.md)
once built.
**Built 2026-10-13 (fin36):** `carryWindow` in `writeFileTool`'s edit branch and `linePairs` in `diff.ts`; pinned by twelve
cases under "PD-TOOLS-016" in `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts` (ten red on the code before) and `diff.test.ts`. The
level-1 sibling the ruling asked to probe writes `new_string`'s LF lines into a CRLF file through both tools; recorded as
[`a-level-1-edit-writes-new-strings-lf-lines-into-a-crlf-file`](../defects/fixed/a-level-1-edit-writes-new-strings-lf-lines-into-a-crlf-file.md),
not decided here (raised as [OQ-254](#oq-254)). The first execution is in place under the directive.

<a id="oq-247"></a>

**OQ-247 — Does REQ-STARTUP-147's list of the variables the domain reads name the platform-convention ones?** *(REQ-STARTUP-147,
"Environment variables read by this domain"; REQ-STARTUP-145, the platform-conventional per-user directories; REQ-STARTUP-161
and -164, the instance claim and its hand-over endpoint; `packages/platform/src/dirs.ts`, `packages/platform/src/instance.ts`.
Raised 2026-10-13 by fin34 from fin30's review of the platform paths, which left it as an optional finding. Numbered after
OQ-235 to OQ-239, which this plan's other bundles hold; raised as OQ-240 and renumbered OQ-247 at the landing, since
origin/main had skipped to OQ-245 and OQ-246 past a block another plan may still hold.)*

REQ-STARTUP-147 lists the environment variables this domain reads: `APPIMAGE`, `ROTARIS_BUNDLED`, `COMSPEC`, and the variable by
which an artifact form names the file a launch started from. The domain also reads `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` (Linux)
and `LOCALAPPDATA` (Windows) to find the per-user directories REQ-STARTUP-145 calls platform-conventional, and the instance claim
reads `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` for where its hand-over socket goes (since 2026-09-19; `socketDirectoryCandidates`). None of the four is
in the list. fin30's builder justified them as platform convention under REQ-STARTUP-145; the list's own wording, "Environment
variables read by this domain", reads as exhaustive, and its next sentence bounds what any variable it covers may decide.

**What the build proceeds under.** The four are read, as REQ-STARTUP-145's platform convention: each only locates a directory,
none selects a workspace, enables diagnostics, touches the update check or permits a second instance, so REQ-STARTUP-147's
second sentence holds for them either way. **What a ruling decides.** Whether REQ-STARTUP-147's list is exhaustive — and then
whether it should name the platform-convention variables, or REQ-STARTUP-145 should say the convention's variables are read —
or whether it lists only the variables this product defines or depends on beyond the platform's own conventions.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the four reads stay exactly as
built, and REQ-STARTUP-147 is amended in place, with no directive, so that its list names a class of **platform-convention
directory variables**: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on Linux, and `LOCALAPPDATA` on Windows. Each
locates a directory and does nothing else; a value is used only when it names an absolute directory (fully qualified on
Windows), and otherwise the convention's default is taken; the list's second sentence binds every member. The home and
temporary directories the operating system reports are read through the platform's own interfaces, and the variables those
interfaces consult are outside the list. The amendment and its reason are recorded in
`docs/spec/resolutions/11-startup-distribution-updates.md`. Nothing a user meets changes.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: keep the reads and amend REQ-STARTUP-147 in place so its
list names the four as a class that locates a directory and decides nothing, which makes the list truly exhaustive for
REQ-STARTUP-111's acceptance. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: keep the reads and record them in a new directive,
`PD-STARTUP-006`, extending REQ-STARTUP-145 and -147, which also accounts for the home and temporary-directory variables the
platform's own lookups consult. **The ruling followed both**: A's form, an amendment in place, because the corpus already depends
on these reads — REQ-CONFIG-001 spells the Windows path as `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rotaris\rotaris\` and REQ-UIBENCH-039 requires
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to be honoured — so an exhaustive REQ-STARTUP-147 disagreed with two live requirements, and a disagreement
within the corpus is an amendment (OQ-21's and OQ-227's precedent), not a directive, which records the owner wanting something
other than what the corpus states; and B's content, the stated class with the home and temporary lookups assigned explicitly,
since naming only the four would leave `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` and `TMPDIR`/`TEMP` unaccounted for (A's own first risk).
**Rejected:** B's directive (it would record behaviour nobody is changing as a departure); confirming without amending (a list
REQ-STARTUP-111's acceptance reads as closed that is not). Checked against the code: `dirs.ts`'s `xdgBaseDirectory` and
`localAppDataDirectory`, `preferences.ts`'s `resolvePreferenceRoot` and `instance.ts`'s `socketDirectoryFor` each take a value
only when it is absolute and otherwise the default, and none selects a workspace, touches the update check or permits a second
instance.

<a id="oq-248"></a>

**OQ-248 — Is the hand-over endpoint a launch opens before it loses the claim a write REQ-STARTUP-164 forbids?** *(REQ-STARTUP-164,
"a launch SHALL write nothing but the record itself while resolving it"; REQ-STARTUP-161, REQ-STARTUP-162; ADR-0055, "The
endpoint is listening before the record is written, not after" and "A launch that is handed over writes nothing";
`packages/platform/src/instance.ts`, `claimInstance`'s `attempt`, `openEndpoint`, `closeEndpoint`, `socketDirectoryFor`. Raised
2026-10-13 by fin34's review of the repair of `docs/defects/fixed/the-instance-record-is-written-before-its-endpoint-listens.md`,
with fin30's optional finding #13 folded in. Raised as OQ-241 and renumbered OQ-248 at the landing, after OQ-247.)*

ADR-0055 decides two things that the code, once it keeps both, shows cannot both hold on a platform whose endpoint is a file.
The endpoint listens before the record naming it is written, so a second launch never reads a record naming an address that
is not yet accepting; and a launch that is handed over writes nothing, "structural rather than a discipline", because "an
exclusive create that fails writes nothing". Since fin34 every claim attempt opens its endpoint first, so on Linux and macOS a
launch that then loses the exclusive create has created a unix socket in the socket directory (and, on the fallback path,
the private `rotaris-<uid>` directory below the temporary directory, as it already did before fin34) and removes the socket
again before it hands over. On Windows the endpoint is a named pipe and nothing is written to disk. REQ-STARTUP-164 says a
launch SHALL write nothing but the record itself while resolving it; REQ-STARTUP-162 that a handed-over launch writes nothing
to any per-user or per-workspace state.

**What the build proceeds under.** ADR-0055's order: the endpoint first, the socket of a launch that loses the claim closed
and unlinked before it hands over (`closeEndpoint`), so nothing it created outlives it and nothing it wrote is per-user or
per-workspace state the product reads. **What a ruling decides.** Whether a transient endpoint, created and removed within the
resolution, is "a write" in REQ-STARTUP-164's sense — and if it is, which of ADR-0055's two decisions gives way: the endpoint
opened only after the record is won (the order fin30 had, with the double-instance window the repaired note describes), or a
form of endpoint that is no file (Linux's abstract socket namespace; nothing equivalent on macOS), or the record's own write
taken to include the endpoint it names.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the record is the file and the
endpoint it names, together with anything a claim attempt creates to hold that endpoint; all of these are "the record itself" in
REQ-STARTUP-164, because REQ-STARTUP-161 makes "how a launch reaches it" part of what the record is and leaves its form to the
implementation. ADR-0055's order stands: the endpoint listens first, then the record is written. A launch that is handed over
**leaves nothing behind**: whatever its attempt created for the endpoint — on the temporary-directory fallback a per-attempt
private directory, which replaces the shared `rotaris-<uid>` one — is removed before it ends. A reclaim removes the stale
endpoint of a dead recorded process along with the record file. No directive: no requirement is contradicted, so the
specification keeps its text; the ruling is recorded here and in ADR-0055. On Windows (the released platform, `PD-STARTUP-001`)
the endpoint is a named pipe and nothing touches disk.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: confirm as built, reading the endpoint as the record's own
write; record it in ADR-0055 and the sequence view; repair the open denial note with a per-attempt `mkdtemp` directory removed
with the socket, which this reading covers. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: confirm and amend the record only, restating
ADR-0055's second decision as "a launch that is handed over leaves nothing behind"; treat `rotaris-<uid>` as a standing runtime
location; flag that crash-orphaned sockets build up. **The ruling followed both**: from both the reading anchored in
REQ-STARTUP-161 and ADR-0055's order (reversing it reopens the double-instance window fin34 repaired; Linux's abstract namespace
gives every local user an unguarded hand-over channel and has no macOS equivalent); B's "leaves nothing behind"; from A the
per-attempt directory, since `socketDirectoryFor` creates `rotaris-<uid>` before the claim, so a handed-over launch could leave
it behind — B's "standing runtime location" is the weaker reading, and the per-attempt directory makes the rule literally true
and closes the denial note; and B's risk 2 followed to its end: if the endpoint belongs to the record, reclaiming the record
removes the endpoint too. **Rejected:** the endpoint opened after the record is won; the abstract socket namespace; deferring.
**Costs kept on record:** the reading takes "the record itself" broadly, anchored in REQ-STARTUP-161's own words; an instance
that crashes leaves its endpoint until the next reclaim removes it; a launch killed between its `mkdtemp` (or its `listen`)
and its `closeEndpoint` while it is losing the claim leaves its private directory (and socket), which no record names, so no
reclaim removes it; a reclaim leaves the endpoint of a recorded process that is running but unresponsive, whose own closer
removes it. Settles
[`another-local-user-can-deny-the-instance-sockets-temporary-fallback`](../defects/fixed/another-local-user-can-deny-the-instance-sockets-temporary-fallback.md),
[`a-handed-over-launch-can-leave-the-private-socket-directory-behind`](../defects/fixed/a-handed-over-launch-can-leave-the-private-socket-directory-behind.md)
and [`a-reclaim-leaves-the-dead-instances-socket-behind`](../defects/fixed/a-reclaim-leaves-the-dead-instances-socket-behind.md)
once built.
**Built 2026-10-13 (fin36):** `placeSocket`, `removeOwnDirectory` and `removeDeadEndpoint` in
`packages/platform/src/instance.ts`, `closeEndpoint` shared by the closers; pinned by cases in `instance.test.ts` and
`instance-order.test.ts`, red on the code before, and `pnpm workspace-proof`'s scenario 13b (63 passed; the unrepaired build
failed its new checks). The report-back is in place in ADR-0055.

<a id="oq-249"></a>

**OQ-249 — Does REQ-TOOLS-145's single active task bound a coordinator's parallel delegations?** *(REQ-TOOLS-145, "at most one
task may be `IN_PROGRESS` at a time"; REQ-TOOLS-146, `replace`'s protection of the active task; `PD-TOOLS-008` revision 1,
"Everything else REQ-TOOLS-145 fixes still governs: at most one task is IN_PROGRESS"; REQ-TOOLS-147, the Agent plan as the
run's primary progress display; REQ-ORCH-029, a list the coordinator "keeps current"; REQ-ORCH-028 with `PD-TOOLS-006`
revision 6's `todo_item`; REQ-CHAT-086, IN_PROGRESS drawn active and PENDING open. Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live runs:
finding P3 of the default autopsy at `a68f121` and its recurrence D7 in the duress autopsy, recorded in
[`a-parallel-delegations-todo-item-cannot-be-marked-in-progress.md`](../defects/fixed/a-parallel-delegations-todo-item-cannot-be-marked-in-progress.md);
the consortium's question P3. The round assigned it OQ-227, which fin30 took on main for `single_file_change` (PD-ORCH-011
revision 2) before this landed; raised as OQ-240 and renumbered OQ-249 before the landing, since origin/main moved to OQ-248
past a block (OQ-240 to OQ-244) another plan may still hold, so it takes the next free number after main's highest.
**Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

A coordinator running two delegated children at once cannot record both items as in progress. In the default live run at
`a68f121` (session `52aea43a`, the `edit` scenario) its plan `#5` marked both parallel children's items `IN_PROGRESS` and was
refused in `PD-TOOLS-008`'s sentence, which left `#7`, the same step's second `delegate`, refused by OQ-213; after the retry
`#14` tried to mark the running tests child's item `IN_PROGRESS` and was refused in REQ-TOOLS-145's sentence, which advised
marking the running implementer's item COMPLETED or ABANDONED. While both children ran the plan recorded the tests item
`PENDING`: 2 refused `todo` calls, 1 refused `delegate`, 2 extra coordinator steps, about 19.5 s on the critical path. The
duress run at `a68f121` (session `e6747bd0`) repeated it for the whole run: `#19` refused a plan marking three items, `#20` and
`#42` kept wave 1's items `PENDING` while their children ran, and `#113`, `#246` and `#404` moved wave 2's and wave 3's items
from `PENDING` straight to `COMPLETED`; the strip drew running work as open for about 67 of 69 minutes. The duress run at
`c2fdd6a` showed the same (`#305`, e's item never marked active while e ran). OQ-163, which kept the single-active rule
(`PD-TOOLS-008`), was a direct-work plan with no delegation.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** REQ-TOOLS-145's single-active rule
bounds the tasks an agent works on itself. A task held as `todo_item` (`PD-TOOLS-006` revision 6) by a non-terminal child of the
list's owner is outside the count, and the bound is checked only on a write that marks a task IN_PROGRESS. An admitted delegation
whose item is PENDING in the caller's plan marks it IN_PROGRESS. The product's texts tell a delegating agent to plan work items,
keep its own item IN_PROGRESS, leave the items it will delegate PENDING and name each in `todo_item`. Recorded as
[`PD-TOOLS-008`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-008) **revision 2** (it narrows REQ-TOOLS-145 and now REQ-TOOLS-146) and
[`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) **revision 7** (the marking, within its existing dispositions). No
directive touches REQ-ORCH-029, REQ-CHAT-086 or REQ-CHAT-088: IN_PROGRESS still maps to active.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **A**, with corrections from B:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended exempting from the count the items the agent's own live children serve through
  `todo_item`, marking a named PENDING item IN_PROGRESS when its delegation is admitted, and teaching the coordinator to leave
  the items it will delegate PENDING; recorded as `PD-TOOLS-008` revision 2 with one clause in `PD-TOOLS-006`. The ruling
  followed A's mechanism and its record. Under it the run marks the item at admission, so no extra `update` call is made, and
  the Agent plan shows active work on a coordinating run, the serial case included.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended keeping REQ-TOOLS-145 as `PD-TOOLS-008` left it, with no directive: the
  coordinator's IN_PROGRESS marks only its own item, a delegated item's progress is its holder's record, and the texts teach
  leaving an item a child works on PENDING until the child reports. The ruling did not follow B's texts: they would leave the
  primary progress display never showing active work on a coordinating run, and they rest on reading the child ledger as the
  plan's state, a reading B itself expected to be challenged. From B it took three things: the count is checked against the
  write that marks a task, so an item whose child has ended never fails a write that marks nothing; a plan written with two
  IN_PROGRESS items before any delegation is still refused, and the text handles it; and a harness finding for an item closed
  while its holder runs.

Both advocates, and OQ-220, rejected planning delegation steps instead of work items: it records a "Delegate X" item COMPLETED
while its child still runs, and turns REQ-ORCH-028's per-item ownership and REQ-ORCH-030's per-item attempt count into counts of
coordinator calls.

**What a live run then shows.** In the edit scenario the coordinator writes its plan, then delegates both children in the next
step naming their items; each `delegate` observation reads "Todo item … is now IN_PROGRESS" and carries the Todo state; while
both children run the Agent plan strip shows both rows active, each turning done when the coordinator closes it; after the plan
write there is no REQ-TOOLS-145 or `PD-TOOLS-008` refusal and no refused `update` like `#14`. In duress a parallel child's
item, such as e's, reads active while that child runs, so `#305` does not recur. The harness counts items recorded PENDING
while held (target 0), items marked COMPLETED while held (target 0) and single-active refusals in coordinating sessions (target
0, each counted as a NOTE). A plan written with two IN_PROGRESS items before any delegation is still refused once, in
`PD-TOOLS-008`'s sentence with its new hint; a model that re-marks an item the run already marked meets REQ-TOOLS-147's no-op
error, one cheap row.

<a id="oq-228"></a>

**OQ-228 — Which personas may a delegation name?** *(REQ-MCP-014, `intent-classifier` and `project-initializer` "are personas
that are not delegation targets"; REQ-ORCH-126, `gatekeeper` "never as an ordinary delegation target"; REQ-ORCH-028, the
delegation vocabulary; REQ-ORCH-034, the unknown-role rejection "listing the known role names and the supported aliases rendered
as `<alias>-><target>`"; REQ-ORCH-038, an unknown role rejected with no spawn; `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 4, "every persona that
agent can delegate to". Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live runs: finding P5 of the default autopsy at `a68f121` (pack
`2026-10-07T06-48-50-123Z`, all ten sessions; 71 of 71 coordinator requests), recorded in
[`delegate-offers-and-admits-personas-that-are-not-delegation-targets.md`](../defects/fixed/delegate-offers-and-admits-personas-that-are-not-delegation-targets.md);
the consortium's question P5, numbered OQ-228 as the round assigned. **Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

`delegate`'s catalogue lists every persona the configuration holds: in the default live run at `a68f121` every coordinator
request offered "intent-classifier (none of these: it neither reads nor writes workspace files nor runs commands)", and the
built-in table's `gatekeeper` among the research and decision roles. The ledger resolves through the same resolver, so a
delegation to either would be admitted, and a child of `intent-classifier` would run with an empty prompt and no tools. No
coordinator tried. The specification keeps three personas out of delegation; the build read `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 4's "every
persona that agent can delegate to" as every `personas:` key.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** `intent-classifier` is not
delegable, and neither are the other two personas the specification reserves, `project-initializer` (REQ-MCP-014) and
`gatekeeper` (REQ-ORCH-126), whether built in or configured under those names. One predicate, the **delegation targets**, decides
what `delegate`'s catalogue lists, what admission and the ledger accept, and which personas the unknown-role rejection and the
write-scope refusal name; a delegation to a reserved persona is refused `rejected` before any other admission check, with no
record and no task id, by REQ-ORCH-034's unknown-role message carrying the targets, the aliases as `<alias>-><target>` and what
the product runs that persona for. Every other persona the configuration holds, a user-defined one included, stays delegable,
listed with its facets and accepted, as built. This is **covered work** under REQ-MCP-014, REQ-ORCH-126, REQ-ORCH-034 and
REQ-ORCH-038; no directive. It records one reading: REQ-ORCH-034's "known role names" are the delegation targets. It corrects the
reading revision 4's first execution built (every `knownRoles()` entry, with `gatekeeper` among the research and decision
roles), which stays beside its replacement in `PD-TOOLS-006`'s revision 4 report; OQ-216's ruling text stands.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended that the three reserved personas be left out of the catalogue and refused with
  REQ-ORCH-038's unknown-role rejection and a reason that says why, through one shared predicate, user-defined personas staying
  delegable. The ruling took A's reason that names what the product runs the persona for.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same predicate read by every reader — the catalogue, the ledger's
  admission, the rejection text and the write-scope writers list. The ruling took B's rename of `knownRoles` to
  `delegationTargets()`, so no reader can reach the unfiltered list, and the aliases REQ-ORCH-034 requires in the rejection,
  which the resolver path dropped.

Both showed that a catalogue-only fix would leave the ledger's rejection advertising the names and `fileWriters` able to list one,
so the description could disagree with admission, the rule OQ-216 and OQ-220 secured. The ruling adds an order neither stated:
this refusal comes first in `delegate()`'s admission, so OQ-220's todo-item refusals never answer a delegation that cannot happen.
Whether `delegates_to` narrows which personas a caller may name is set aside as its own question, OQ-229: read as an
allow-list, its empty default would forbid every delegation.

**What a live run then shows.** Every coordinator request's `delegate` description lists twelve personas under the default
configuration, `orchestrator` and the eleven specialists, each with its facets, and the two aliases; `intent-classifier` and
`gatekeeper` appear in none (about 20 to 40 tokens saved per delegating request). No child of either is recorded. A coordinator
that names one sees one `rejected` observation saying the product runs that persona itself and listing the targets and aliases,
with no child row.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin33, `fin33-delegation-targets-and-plan`); reported in `PD-TOOLS-006`'s revision 4 first execution.*
`NOT_DELEGATION_TARGETS` and `isDelegationTarget` (`packages/contracts/src/roles.ts`); `PersonaResolver.delegationTargets`
(renamed from `knownRoles`), `delegationTargetsFor`, `aliasesAmong` and `resolveDelegationTarget`
(`packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`), read by `ChildLedger.spawn`, `IterationChildren.delegate` (first, before every other
admission check), `fileWriters` and the run host's `delegateCatalogue`; `personaResolverFor`'s targets
(`apps/desktop/src/run-host/configuration.ts`). Pinned by `contracts.test.ts`, `children/children.test.ts` ("OQ-228 / OQ-229",
each "(red)" case red on the code before), `run-host/tools.test.ts` (the catalogue under the default configuration and under one
overriding `intent-classifier`) and `tools/delegation.test.ts` (`gatekeeper` no longer among the research and decision roles). The
note is repaired.

<a id="oq-229"></a>

**OQ-229 — Does a persona's `delegates_to` narrow which roles it may delegate to?** *(REQ-CONFIG-101, `delegates_to` "roles this
one may spawn", "defaulting to empty"; REQ-CONFIG-045, a user's personas; REQ-CONFIG-062, the role vocabulary a file is
canonicalised by; REQ-CONFIG-231 and REQ-CONFIG-232, the referential and cycle checks over the lists; REQ-CONFIG-246, a
referential error with no one present refuses the run; REQ-CONFIG-464; REQ-ORCH-002, REQ-ORCH-028, REQ-ORCH-029, REQ-ORCH-030,
REQ-ORCH-034, REQ-ORCH-038; REQ-TOOLS-005 and REQ-TOOLS-006, an absent narrowing narrowing nothing; `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 4.
Raised 2026-10-07 by OQ-228's ruling, which set it aside, from the final live runs' finding P5 (the default autopsy at `a68f121`);
recorded in
[`a-personas-delegates-to-never-narrows-its-delegations.md`](../defects/fixed/a-personas-delegates-to-never-narrows-its-delegations.md);
the consortium's question DT1, numbered OQ-229 as the round assigned. **Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

The loader parses, canonicalises and validates `delegates_to`, reports an entry that names no role and any cycle through the
lists, Settings shows those messages, and an unattended run refuses to start over them. Admission and the catalogue never read
the list: a delegation is admitted to any target whatever the caller's list holds. Read as an allow-list, the empty default would
forbid every delegation, and no shipped persona sets the key.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** when a persona's `delegates_to` names
any persona, that agent may delegate only to the delegation targets the list names. Targets are matched after alias resolution,
and OQ-228's three reserved personas stay refused whatever the list holds. That agent's `delegate` catalogue lists only those
personas, plus the aliases whose target is among them. Admission refuses any other persona as `rejected`, before any record
exists and with no task id, with a reason that names the caller's `delegates_to` and lists its targets. An empty list is the
default and what every shipped persona carries, and it narrows nothing: the shipped orchestrator, and every configuration that
never sets the key, keep OQ-228's delegation targets. A persona stops delegating only when `delegate` is left out of its `tools`.
This is **covered work** under REQ-CONFIG-101 ("roles this one may spawn"), read together with REQ-CONFIG-045, -062, -231, -232
and -464, REQ-ORCH-002, -028, -029, -030, -034 and -038, and REQ-TOOLS-005 and -006; no directive and no back-pointer.

**The reading recorded.** An empty list narrows nothing at any layer, so a workspace that writes `[]` lifts a global list;
entries are role names, matched against the persona a delegation resolves to after alias resolution; OQ-228's reserved personas
stay refused; the list removes no tool; REQ-ORCH-034's "known role names" for a narrowed caller are its permitted targets. **The
reading rejected, kept beside its reason:** "an empty list means spawn none" — no shipped persona carries the key, `orchestrator`
alone declares `delegate`, and REQ-ORCH-002, -028 and -029 require it to delegate, so it would stop every shipped run; a
populated default would instead hide each persona a user adds (REQ-CONFIG-045) and reverse OQ-228. REQ-CONFIG-102, -103 and
REQ-TOOLS-006's run allow-list each read an absent narrowing as no narrowing. If a later round reads the empty case as departing
from REQ-CONFIG-101, it lands as `PD-CONFIG-004`, narrowing REQ-CONFIG-101 for the empty case alone, and the build stays as ruled.

**What it costs.** REQ-ORCH-028's routing table still names roles a narrowed coordinator may not reach (each such delegation is
refused once, 17.7 to 19.6 s a refused step); REQ-ORCH-030's diagnosis route is refused when the list leaves out
`codebase-analyst` and `librarian`; during a plan cycle a list naming only implementers leaves no admissible delegation; a list
naming its own persona, for example to keep a child orchestrator, is reported as a delegation cycle at every load (REQ-CONFIG-232),
which refuses an unattended run (REQ-CONFIG-246), so such a coordinator runs attended; and lists already in users' files start to
bind after the upgrade.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**; they take the same position:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended that a non-empty list narrow the catalogue and admission to the targets it names,
  aliases resolved first, the reserved personas still refused, a delegation outside it refused `rejected` with a reason naming the
  caller's `delegates_to`, and an empty list narrowing nothing. The ruling took A's sentence telling a narrowed caller its
  catalogue is narrowed, and the layering test (a workspace `[]` lifting a global list).
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same, with the refusal as REQ-ORCH-034's unknown-role message listing the
  caller's permitted personas and aliases, as covered work. The ruling took B's placement of this ruling in the OQ OQ-228's record
  raised, and the run's log lines.

The ruling adds three things neither stated: a log line for an explicitly empty list on a persona that holds `delegate`, the
order of the checks (unknown name, then a reserved persona, then a persona outside a non-empty list, all ahead of the plan gate,
the write scope, the continuation check and OQ-220's todo-item checks), and REQ-CONFIG-246's cost for a list naming its own
persona.

**What a live run then shows.** Nothing changes in the default or duress live runs, which set no `delegates_to`: every
coordinator request's description stays as OQ-228 leaves it and admission is unchanged. A run whose configuration gives the
coordinator a list shows only the listed delegation targets with the sentence saying the catalogue is narrowed, each delegation
outside the list as one `rejected` observation naming the list with no child row, and one log line at setup for an entry that
permits nothing. The evidence is scripted only.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin33, `fin33-delegation-targets-and-plan`); reported in `PD-TOOLS-006`'s revision 4 first execution.*
`Persona.delegatesTo`, set by `personaResolverFor` from a non-empty `delegates_to`, with its four log lines; `delegationTargetsFor`
and `resolveDelegationTarget`'s third refusal (`packages/engine/src/children/personas.ts`); the caller's persona into
`ChildLedger.spawn` (`SpawnInput.callerPersona`); `DelegateCatalogue.narrowedBy` and its two sentences
(`renderDelegateCatalogue`). Pinned by `children/children.test.ts` (a narrowed root, an alias of a listed persona, a list naming
only `gatekeeper`, the check ahead of a continuation, the writers among the targets, a child persona checked against its own list,
a follow-up not checked, the key unset), `run-host/tools.test.ts` (the catalogue equal to what admission accepts in both
directions; a global list narrowing and a workspace `[]` lifting it), `run-host/configuration.test.ts` (the carried list and the
four log lines) and `tools/delegation.test.ts`. The note is repaired.

REQ-TOOLS-001, the three facets; REQ-CONFIG-100, a configured `system_prompt` replacing the built-in one; REQ-CONFIG-101;

at `a68f121` missed; OQ-228 and OQ-229, the delegation targets. Raised 2026-10-07 from the final live runs: finding D3 of the duress
autopsy at `a68f121` (pack `2026-10-07T07-09-30-708Z`, session `e6747bd0`, `#114`, `#115`, `#164`), recorded in
[`the-routing-table-leads-the-coordinator-past-delegates-catalogue.md`](../defects/fixed/the-routing-table-leads-the-coordinator-past-delegates-catalogue.md);
the consortium's question D3. The round assigned it OQ-233, which fin32 took on main for `write_file`'s level-3 shift; raised
as OQ-241 and renumbered OQ-250 before the landing, after OQ-249, for the reason OQ-249's entry gives. **Ruled 2026-10-07.**)*

Revision 4's catalogue reached every coordinator request, and the coordinator still gave the work a route implies to the route's
persona: `docs/decisions.md` to `architect` with a `write_scope` (`#115`, refused in 170 ms, re-briefed in 19.4 s), and a brief
offering `node --test` to a docs-writer (`#114`), which then called a tool that does not exist (`#164`). At `c2fdd6a` the same task
had gone to `codebase-analyst` (`#107`): the misroute follows whichever route matches the subject.

**Ruled 2026-10-07 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)), as
[`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) revision 8:** the built-in coordinator's routing table keeps every route
and REQ-ORCH-028's two clauses word for word. It closes with one fixed sentence that names no persona's tools and sends the work a
route implies to a persona whose entry in `delegate`'s list allows it: a file to write goes to a persona that writes workspace
files, and a test or other command goes to one that runs commands. Where the route's own persona lacks the tools, it is asked for
its answer, which is handed on. `delegate`'s catalogue also tells the caller never to offer a persona, in its brief, a command or
tool its entry does not show. Revision 3's write-scope refusal and revision 4's catalogue stay as built. OQ-216's target of zero
stands, and its falsified first reading is recorded beside the `a68f121` measurement in OQ-216's entry.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended a per-route clause beside each target saying what that target's grant lacks
  ("writes no workspace files", "runs no commands"), rendered for the calling coordinator from the resolution that builds
  revision 4's catalogue, recorded as revision 8 and measured at the next duress run. The ruling took A's point that the
  coordinator decides at the routing table, so confirming the build leaves OQ-216's measure missed; it did not take the computed
  per-route clause, which would make the built-in prompt a per-configuration render (no longer the constant `entryInstructionsFor`
  recognises) for about 20 s a run.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended keeping the advice as built, with revision 3's refusal, recording the duress
  measurement in place, and replacing OQ-216's target with enforced bounds and a reopening condition. The ruling took B's points
  that enforcement now bounds the structured miss, that revision 3 already names the writers, and that facts about a persona's
  tools belong in one computed place — so the new sentence names no persona's tools and points to the catalogue.

One fixed routing sentence and one brief clause stay true under every `tools:` override, every `tool_restrictions` entry,
OQ-228's targets and OQ-229's narrowing. **Reopening condition:** if a later duress run shows any `write_scope` refused for a
non-writer, or any brief offering a command or tool its target lacks, A's computed per-route clause is weighed as the next
`PD-TOOLS-006` revision; if any enforced bound breaks (a scoped misroute not refused before a record, an invented tool not stopped
at the gate, a stray workaround file, an impossible brief on a failed child's path, an answer claiming a command a persona could
not run), the question reopens at once.

**What a live run then shows.** Every coordinating request carries the routing table with its closing sentence (about 80 more
tokens) and `delegate`'s closing instruction with the brief clause; direct-work runs and runs with a configured `system_prompt` show
no routing sentence. In the duress run: 0 `write_scope` refusals for a non-writer and 0 briefs offering a command or tool the
target's entry lacks; a design or decision document such as `docs/decisions.md` goes to a docs-writer directly or with
`architect`'s answer handed on through `depends_on` or `inherited_context`. The harness's duress NOTE prints both counts;
missing-shell asides are counted only. The default run is unchanged apart from the tokens.
