1, a plain substring search, and its "Found <n> occurrences" refusal; REQ-TOOLS-189. Raised 2026-10-13 from `PD-TOOLS-014`'s
block and the near-miss code (`nearMissMessage`, `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`), after fin32's review named the gap
and fin35 deferred it, and ruled the same day; the number is the round's assigned one.)*

The near-miss window is whole lines, but level 1 is a substring search, so the window's text can occur again inside a longer line
or across a line boundary. A file `x = 1\nmax = 1\n` with `old_string` `x = 1 ` matches one window at level 2 and is quoted as
`"x = 1"` with "Sent back as old_string with the same content_hash, the file's text over line 1 matches exactly"; the retry is
refused "Found 2 occurrences of old_str at lines 1, 2" and writes nothing. The several-windows reply ("send its exact text as
old_string") fails the same way whenever the windows' text is identical (two lines `x = 1`, `old_string` `x = 1 `). Clause 5's
promise of a level-1 match holds; it is silent on whether that match is unique. Recorded as
[`a-near-miss-quote-that-occurs-more-than-once-is-promised-to-match-exactly`](../defects/fixed/a-near-miss-quote-that-occurs-more-than-once-is-promised-to-match-exactly.md).

**What the build proceeds under.** The quote and its promise as built, whatever the text's occurrences.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a reply whose quote is not unique says so, widens the quote until it is, or stands as built.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** `PD-TOOLS-014` goes to revision 2.
When a near-miss reply's quoted text occurs more than once in the file at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 1, the reply still gives the quote.
Before the quote it states the count and the lines where the occurrences start (at most 10, then "and N more"), drops the promise
that the quote "matches exactly" when sent back alone, and asks that one neighbouring line, unchanged, be added to both
`old_string` and `new_string`, naming the reader's offset and limit for the window and one line on each side, clamped to the
file. The over-30,000-character direction carries the same sentence, and the several-windows reply carries it when a window's
text is not unique. The quote is never widened. `PD-TOOLS-015` inherits all of this through its clause 4, in `write_file`'s
voice (`read_file`, no hash). Every reply whose quoted text is unique stays word for word; REQ-TOOLS-136's levels and its "Found
<n> occurrences" refusal are unchanged.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: flag the repeat before the quote, naming the count and the
lines, withdraw "matches exactly", ask for a neighbouring line in both strings with the reader's offset and limit, and flag the
over-30,000-character branch too; revision 2 of `PD-TOOLS-014`. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: the same flag among the facts,
the listed lines capped at 10 then "and N more", revision 2 of `PD-TOOLS-014` reaching `PD-TOOLS-015` through its clause 4, and a
live-run count of retries answered "Found N occurrences". **The ruling followed both**: they agree on the remedy, flag and never
widen, on `PD-TOOLS-015`'s principle that "a refusal costs one call where a wrong success costs a corrupted file" — a widened quote
no longer lines up with the `new_string` the caller already wrote, so a resend would delete the added context lines beside a
success. From B the cap of 10 and B's example, which the code confirms (A's example, `  return x` against `    return x`, is a
plain substring and matches at level 1, never reaching the near miss; A's conclusion stands on B's mechanism); from A the
concrete read window and the over-30,000-character flag. Added by the ruling: the several-windows reply fails the same way when
the windows' text is identical, likely its common case, so the same count covers it. **Rejected:** widening the quote (a wrong
success that deletes context lines); confirming as built (a reply the next call contradicts); deferring (the model doing the
user's task receives the reply). **Costs kept on record:** in the non-unique case one read and one retry where widening would
have taken one retry; a caller that adds the neighbouring line to `old_string` only would delete it with a success, which the
wording's "to both" is the only guard against; a second implementation built from the specification alone keeps the unflagged
quote.
**Built 2026-10-13 (fin36):** `nearMissMessage` and `levelOneLines` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`); pinned by four
cases under "PD-TOOLS-014" and one under "PD-TOOLS-015" in `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts`, each red on the code
before; `lib/near-miss-edits.mjs` counts retries refused "Found N occurrences". The first execution is in place under the
directive.

<a id="oq-253"></a>

**OQ-253 — Does a one-second per-agent limit read "1 second" or "1 seconds"?** *(`PD-CONFIG-003` revision 3, "Where a cut-off
agent shows", the `<limit>` bullet: "written '1 minute' or '<m> minutes' when N is a whole number of minutes, and '<N> seconds'
otherwise", and revision 3's first execution, "except that one second reads '1 second'"; REQ-MONITOR-052, REQ-MONITOR-069;
REQ-CONFIG-113, `runtime.child_timeout` in whole seconds; REQ-ORCH-088's "Child timed out after <N>s". Raised 2026-10-13 from
that first execution's evidence and ruled the same day; the number is the round's assigned one.)*

The directive's template writes every limit that is not a whole number of minutes as "<N> seconds", so a one-second limit reads
"1 seconds"; the build writes "1 second" (`timeoutLimitText`, `packages/ui/src/agents.ts`, through `countNoun`), and revision 3's
first execution recorded that without the directive following. The case is reachable: the workspace file takes any integer of
at least 1 second (`child_timeout: z.number().int().min(1)`, `packages/contracts/src/config.ts`; no maximum in
`packages/config/src/sections/runtime.ts`), though the widget offers 60 to 14,400. Recorded as
[`pd-config-003-writes-a-one-second-limit-as-1-seconds`](../defects/fixed/pd-config-003-writes-a-one-second-limit-as-1-seconds.md).

**What the build proceeds under.** "1 second", as built at revision 3.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether the directive's template follows English number agreement ("1 second"), the code follows
the template's letter ("1 seconds"), or the case is ruled out of reach.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the built "1 second" stands.
`PD-CONFIG-003` gains **revision 4**, which changes only revision 3's `<limit>` bullet so it reads: N, the limit the agent ran
under, written "1 minute" or "<m> minutes" when N is a whole number of minutes, and "1 second" or "<N> seconds" otherwise.
Revision 3's text is quoted beside it as no longer governing. REQ-ORCH-088's error form "Child timed out after <N>s", which the
parser reads, REQ-CONFIG-113's range, REQ-MONITOR-286 and every other clause of revisions 1 to 3 are unchanged. No code, test
or proof changes.

**The two recommendations weighed.** *Advocate A (the user's lens)*: keep the built "1 second" and correct revision 3's bullet
with a dated note in the style of OQ-237's correction, keeping the original wording quoted; the case is reachable through the
workspace file, so it is not to be ruled unreachable. *Advocate B (the system's lens)*: the same, with an explicit statement that
REQ-ORCH-088's machine-read error form is unchanged, and R-071's reading of REQ-GIT-122's form as a template of singular and
plural as the precedent. **The ruling followed both** on substance — the case is reachable (the file's integer of at least 1
second), the minutes clause already spells "1 minute", so the template was meant to agree in number, and showing "1 seconds"
would put a grammar defect on screen to match an omission; B's carve-out for REQ-ORCH-088 is taken — and **departed from both**
on the form: a dated "Corrected" note is the record's form for reasons and directive verbs, while `docs/product/README.md`
makes a change to a directive's own normative text a new revision, its replaced text quoted beside it. The `<limit>` bullet is
normative, so the change is revision 4. **Rejected:** changing the code to "1 seconds"; ruling the case unreachable (false).
**Costs kept on record:** none in code; one more revision on a directive already at three.
**Recorded 2026-10-13 (fin36):** revision 4 written in place in `PD-CONFIG-003` with its first execution (held as already
built; `agent-timeout.test.ts` green), the two back-pointers amended in place.

<a id="oq-254"></a>

**OQ-254 — Does an exact (level-1) edit of a CRLF file keep the file's line endings in `new_string`'s added lines?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-136, level 1 "exact" and replace-all "replaces every exact occurrence as plain text"; REQ-TOOLS-189, `haet_edit`'s
level-1 match; REQ-TOOLS-135, the success; `PD-TOOLS-016`, which keeps the file's line endings for a window match at levels 2
to 4 and says it does not decide level 1; `PD-STARTUP-001`, Windows the only platform shipped. Raised 2026-10-13 by fin36's
review from the probe OQ-246's ruling asked for, recorded by fin36's builder without a number; the number is the next free one
on `origin/main` when raised; if another plan lands it first, this one takes the next free number. **Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

An edit whose `old_string` matches at level 1 replaces the exact span with `new_string` verbatim. When `new_string` has several
lines written with `\n` alone and the file is CRLF, the result has LF-only lines among CRLF ones: `write_file` on
`one\r\ntwo\r\n` with `old_string` `one` and `new_string` `ONE\nX` leaves `ONE\nX\r\ntwo\r\n`; `haet_edit` does the same, and so
does a `replace_all`. Recorded as
[`a-level-1-edit-writes-new-strings-lf-lines-into-a-crlf-file`](../defects/fixed/a-level-1-edit-writes-new-strings-lf-lines-into-a-crlf-file.md),
and pinned as built by "PD-TOOLS-016 … level 1, replace_all and haet_edit are unchanged on a CRLF file" in
`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/tools.test.ts`. No requirement's text is contradicted: "exact" writes `new_string` as given.

**What the build proceeds under.** `new_string` written as given at level 1 and by `replace_all`, through both tools.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an exact match carries the file's line endings into `new_string`'s added lines (narrowing
REQ-TOOLS-136 and REQ-TOOLS-189 for both tools, `PD-TOOLS-016`'s rule extended to level 1 and `replace_all`), or stands as built
(the caller's bytes written exactly, `PD-TOOLS-016`'s cost "an exact level-1 `old_string` still does either" kept).

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** an exact edit keeps a CRLF file's
line endings. When `write_file`'s `edit` matches at level 1 or uses `replace_all`, and when `haet_edit` or `haet` matches at
level 1 or uses `replace_all`, each occurrence is tested by `PD-TOOLS-016` clause 2's test read on the lines its span touches;
on a CRLF occurrence every line break inside the replacement, or directly after it in the result, gains a `\r` when it lacks
one, and a `\r` is never doubled. An edit whose carried result leaves the file's bytes unchanged is refused with nothing
written. The success says when a `\r` was added. Recorded as [`PD-TOOLS-017`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-017) (it
narrows REQ-TOOLS-136 and REQ-TOOLS-189 and extends REQ-TOOLS-135), with [`PD-TOOLS-016`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-016)
**revision 2**, whose cost sentence "an exact level-1 `old_string` still does either" became false and is kept quoted beneath.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended a new directive under which a level-1 edit and a `replace_all`, through both
  tools, give a `\r` to every line break inside the replacement or directly after it, tested on each occurrence, with
  `PD-TOOLS-016`'s sentence on the success. The ruling followed A on the break after the span: `PD-TOOLS-014`'s quote ends in
  the file's `\r` (`one\r\ntwo\r`), so a retry with `ONE\ntwo` takes the file's own `\r` with it, and only a rule that reads the
  result gives it back. It followed A on testing each occurrence by its own lines, as `PD-TOOLS-016` reads only its window.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same directive with the `\n`s of `new_string` carried, one test over all
  of a `replace_all`'s occurrences, an explicit refusal when the carried edit changes nothing, a revision of `PD-TOOLS-016`'s
  cost sentence, and the sibling `insert` path recorded as its own note and question. The ruling followed B on the refusal (an
  edit `a\r\nb` → `a\nb` would otherwise rewrite identical bytes beside a success, the no-op already repaired for `haet_edit`),
  on revising `PD-TOOLS-016` rather than extending it (each identifier's case stays exhaustive), and on `insert`, which the code
  confirms writes LF lines into a CRLF file the same way.

**Rejected:** confirming the build (a silent format corruption on the only shipped platform, in the commonest edit shape, and
level-1 drift that later defeats `PD-TOOLS-016`'s own test); a tool-description sentence asking callers to send CRLF (a model
does not see an invisible `\r`, as `PD-TOOLS-014`'s first execution measured); deferring. **Costs kept on record:** an edit can
no longer write LF lines into a CRLF file (`overwrite` still can, and `haet_edit` has none); a mixed file keeps the old
behaviour; a model predicting its own bytes may meet one near miss; an implementation built from the specification alone writes
`new_string` as given; nothing measures it live, since the live-run fixtures are LF files on Linux.

**What a live run then shows.** Nothing new on Linux. On Windows, a CRLF file edited by an exact or replace-all edit keeps
uniform CRLF endings, and its success carries `new_string was written with the file's CRLF line endings.`

<a id="oq-255"></a>

**OQ-255 — May a `replace` close a delegated item once its child has ended, and does its success say what it kept?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-146, `replace`'s protection of finished and active work, "a replace can neither silently retire the task the agent is
working on nor introduce a second IN_PROGRESS task"; REQ-TOOLS-145 as `PD-TOOLS-008` revision 2 bounds it, "REQ-TOOLS-146's
protection is otherwise unchanged"; `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 7, an admitted delegation marks its PENDING item IN_PROGRESS;
REQ-TOOLS-147; REQ-ORCH-029, REQ-ORCH-075 and PD-ORCH-015, the correction and re-queue an open plan meets; OQ-249 and OQ-163.
Raised 2026-10-13 from revision 7's first execution in [`directives.md`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) ("`replace`
cannot complete an active item") and the `todo` tool's `replace` branch (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/todo.ts`), recorded in
[`a-todo-replace-cannot-close-a-delegated-item-and-hides-the-restore.md`](../defects/fixed/a-todo-replace-cannot-close-a-delegated-item-and-hides-the-restore.md);
the consortium's question RC1. Raised as OQ-254 and renumbered OQ-255 before the landing, since origin/main took OQ-254 for the
level-1 CRLF edit meanwhile. **Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

Since revision 7 the run sets a delegated item IN_PROGRESS at admission (`markDelegatedItem`,
`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`) without the coordinator writing it. Once the child has ended, the item is held by no one,
and REQ-TOOLS-146 still restores it over whatever a `replace` sends: a coordinator that closes its plan with one `replace`
setting every item COMPLETED leaves the delegated items IN_PROGRESS, and the tool answers `Replaced the todo list: 1 phase, N
tasks.` with no word of the restore. The coordinator then answers with its plan open; PD-ORCH-015's correction asks only for
"each item's true state with the todo tool", so the same `replace` meets the same restore, and REQ-ORCH-075 re-queues a met
request to a fresh root under a `system` row saying the coordinator "answered with items of its plan not done". Revision 7's own
first execution met this on the scripted coordinator and changed the coordinator, which hides the case from the proofs while a
live model still meets it. No live run since revision 7 has measured how a model closes a delegated plan.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a `replace` stores COMPLETED or
ABANDONED for an IN_PROGRESS task that a child of the list's owner records as its `todo_item` once no non-terminal child holds
it, and a task closed this way does not count as the active task against a mark in the same list. Every other protection stays:
finished work, held tasks and the agent's own active task are still restored. Every task a `replace` restores over a different
incoming state is named in its success observation, with the state kept, the reason, and `update` as the way to change it.
Recorded as [`PD-TOOLS-008`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-008) **revision 3** (it narrows REQ-TOOLS-146 again and, for the
count, REQ-TOOLS-145 as revision 2 bounds it). Revision 7's first-execution reason "`replace` cannot complete an active item" is
kept beside this ruling as falsified for a served-and-ended item.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended `PD-TOOLS-008` revision 3 letting a `replace` close any IN_PROGRESS task no
  non-terminal child holds, the agent's own included, with every task a `replace` keeps over a different state named in the
  success observation and why. The ruling took A's named-restore observation, since a success that hides an override is a false
  observation, and A's reading that the bound is checked on the resulting list, so a list that closes one task and starts
  another is a valid handoff. It did not take A's wider scope: releasing the agent's own unserved active task reopens ground
  OQ-163 and revision 1 settled, and no live evidence asks for it.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same revision scoped to a task some child of the owner serves as its
  `todo_item` once no non-terminal child holds it (a second read through the run, the items served by terminal children
  included), with every restore named, its state, its reason and `update` as the remedy. The ruling followed B's scope: such a
  task fails every part of REQ-TOOLS-146's stated reason, and exists only because revision 7 added a state the agent never sets.
  It added what B left implicit: as built, an unheld served item is the protected active task, which would reject a list that
  closes it and marks another, so that same list is allowed to close it. Omitted tasks are named only when their state changed,
  which a kept omitted task never does.

**What a live run then shows.** When a coordinator closes its plan with one `replace` after its delegated children ended, the
delegated items are stored COMPLETED, the root reaches `succeeded` with no PD-ORCH-015 correction, and no "items not done"
`system` row appears. A `replace` that sends COMPLETED for an item a running child holds, or for the coordinator's own active
item, has its observation name that item, the state kept and the reason, and tell it to use `update`; the next `todo` call is
then an `update` for that item. The harness reads 0 served-and-ended items restored over a close.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin37, `fin37-replace-closes-delegated`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-008` revision 3.*
`TodoToolOptions.served`, `closes` and `keptReason` in `todoTool`'s `replace` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/todo.ts`);
`IterationChildren.servedTodoItems`, `Run.servedTodoItems` and `ToolPortContext.servedTodoItems` (`packages/engine`), passed by
`createToolPort` (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/tools.ts`); the scripted `donereplace` step
(`apps/desktop/src/run-host/scripted-client.ts`), shown in the built app by `pnpm mission-proof` item 1e; the live run's
`restoredOverClose` and `namedRestores` (`apps/desktop/scripts/lib/coordinator-todo.mjs`). Pinned by `tools/tools.test.ts`,
`run-host/tools.test.ts` and `children/children.test.ts`, each red on the code before. The note is repaired.

<a id="oq-256"></a>

**OQ-256 — Does a sibling's answer handed on through `inherited_context` or `depends_on` reach the next child whole?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-152, `depends_on` "summary and key findings" and `inherited_context` "reports", with no cap; REQ-TOOLS-154 item (5),
the inherited-context block; REQ-ORCH-047, the prior-agent-context block; REQ-ORCH-060, the 4,000-character cap of a resume
message's report block; REQ-TOOLS-153, the observation's warnings; `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 8, whose routing sentence sends an
answer through either channel, and revision 5, the 100,000-character attachment budget. Raised 2026-10-13 from finding V1 of the
duress live-run autopsy at `552d346` (session `18a9d22d`), recorded in
[`an-answer-handed-on-through-inherited-context-reaches-the-writer-cut-to-4000-characters`](../defects/fixed/an-answer-handed-on-through-inherited-context-reaches-the-writer-cut-to-4000-characters.md);
the consortium's question V1. **Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

The inherited-context block rendered each sibling with REQ-ORCH-060's report block, so a long answer reached the child as 4,000
characters and a marker, while REQ-ORCH-047's block carried a dependency's answer unbounded. In the duress run the architect's
28,330-character analysis reached the writer as 14 % of itself and the verifier's 20,195-character report as 20 %; the writer
hunted for the rest with 7 calls, then wrote 7 of `docs/decisions.md`'s 8 file sections from its own reading, and the user's
answer credited them to the architect. No channel a child holds carries the rest.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** both hand-off channels revision 8 names,
the inherited-context block and REQ-ORCH-047's prior-agent-context block, carry each named sibling's or dependency's result text
whole (final response, else last response, else key findings, else summary), each block under a 100,000-character budget. An
answer that does not fit is given the larger of the remaining budget and 4,000 characters, and ends in a marker telling the child
what was omitted, that the rest is in neither the workspace nor the artifact store, and that its report must say what it did not
receive. The caller is warned at acceptance (for a `depends_on` answer already complete, a forecast), `delegate`'s description
says what each channel carries, and REQ-ORCH-060's cap stays on the resume message and the wait results. Recorded as
[`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) **revision 9**, "What an answer handed on carries" (it narrows
REQ-TOOLS-152, REQ-TOOLS-154 and, newly, REQ-ORCH-047). The falsified reason the block was built on, "a child inherits exactly
what its parent was told", is kept beside its replacement in `notify.ts`.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended revision 9 with both channels under one 100,000-character budget, a cut answer
  given the larger of the remainder and 4,000 characters so no child ever receives less than before, a marker telling the child
  what it lacks and that its report must say so, a warning to the caller, and a description sentence saying what each channel
  carries. The ruling followed A on the floor, since B's prefix rule would leave every later sibling a heading and a marker,
  less than a child gets today, and on making the description sentence required, since the coordinator's req 98 believed the
  architect had published no artifact.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same budget and marker with a prefix rule, the cut warned to the caller as
  a forecast for `depends_on`, REQ-ORCH-060's cap kept on the resume message and wait results, the test cases, and the falsified
  `reportBlock` reason kept beside its replacement. The ruling took B's test cases and the kept reason.

Both rejected the artifact route (a child report's artifact holding its final response): it duplicates the stored report,
depends on an id the wait results do not carry, and drops an over-budget body whole. **Costs kept on record:** a child's payload
grows on every turn that carries it, up to about 300,000 characters across three blocks in the worst case; a `depends_on` answer
over 100,000 characters, unbounded until now, is cut; an implementation built from the specification alone caps the inherited
block at 4,000 characters.

**What a live run then shows.** In the next duress pack a writer handed the architect's or the verifier's answer through
`inherited_context` or `depends_on` sees it whole in its first request: 0 hand-off markers for answers under 100,000 characters
(the harness NOTE `hand-off answers a child received cut`), no hunting calls (`artifact_read`, `glob` or `read_file` of
`.rotaris`) for the missing answer, and no `background_output` verbatim retrieval or re-typed brief by the coordinator to hand a
report on. A `delegate` observation names a cut only when an answer exceeds the budget; the coordinator's resume and wait blocks
still show 4,000 characters per child.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin38, `fin38-edits-handoff-classifier`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 9.*
`inheritedContext`, `priorAgentContextParts` and `handOffMarker` (`packages/engine/src/children/notify.ts`) under `HAND_OFF_BUDGET`
(`packages/kernel/src/hand-off.ts`); `Spawned.inheritedCuts` and `DelegateOutcome.handOff`, rendered by `handOffWarnings` beside the
attachment warning, and `HAND_OFF_SENTENCE` in `delegate`'s description (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/delegation.ts`); the live
run's NOTE (`apps/desktop/scripts/lib/hand-off-cuts.mjs`). Pinned by `children/notify.test.ts`, `children/children.test.ts` and
`tools/delegation.test.ts`, red on the code before. The note is repaired.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** the hand-off was **NOT
REACHED** at `0bc3eee`: no delegation used `depends_on` or `inherited_context`, so the harness's 0 cut answers does not
discriminate. The duress pack named above is still owed; none has been made since `552d346`. Evidence: [`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in
[`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

<a id="oq-257"></a>

**OQ-257 — Does `delegate`'s write-scope sentence tie file work to a writer, and what bound replaces OQ-216's target of zero
`write_scope` refusals?** *(REQ-TOOLS-152's `write_scope` as `PD-TOOLS-006` narrows it; revision 3, the refusal of a scope for a
persona that writes no files; revision 4, the catalogue; revision 8, the routing sentence; REQ-ORCH-028, the routing table;
OQ-216's target of zero; [OQ-250](#oq-250)'s reopening condition, whose first limb is "any `write_scope` refused for a
non-writer". Raised 2026-10-13 from finding V2 and the D3 verdict of the duress live-run autopsy at `552d346` (session
`18a9d22d`, #92), recorded in
[`the-routing-sentence-did-not-stop-a-write-scope-for-architect`](../defects/fixed/the-routing-sentence-did-not-stop-a-write-scope-for-architect.md);
the consortium's question V2. **Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

With the routing sentence in 41 of 41 coordinator requests, req 59 still gave `architect` a `write_scope` for
`docs/decisions.md`, chosen by habit while reasoning about scope overlap, and revision 3 refused it in 5 ms before any record; the
next `delegate`, 30.0 s later, re-routed the work exactly as revision 8 prescribes. `delegate`'s sentence read "When the child will
write files, give write_scope: …", which makes the task the condition and never the persona, and the field had no description.
Every enforced bound held.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** `delegate`'s write-scope sentence, and
a description on the `write_scope` field, say that work writing files goes to a persona whose catalogue entry writes workspace
files and that a scope given to any other persona is refused before the child starts; both texts are fixed and name no persona.
Revision 3's refusal, the routing table's order and revision 8's sentence stay as built, and Advocate A's computed per-route clause
of OQ-250 is declined again, for OQ-250's reason. OQ-216's write-scope target of zero is replaced by a bound: at most one refusal
per duress run, each refused before any record exists and re-routed by the coordinator's next request; the falsified target is
kept beside the bound in OQ-216's entry, and the impossible-brief target of zero stands. Recorded as
[`PD-TOOLS-006`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-006) **revision 9**, in the same revision as [OQ-256](#oq-256), and revision 8's
first live execution is reported in place under it.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both**:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended rewriting `delegate`'s write-scope sentence and giving the field a schema
  description, so that the moment the coordinator fills in a scope it is told file work goes to a persona whose entry writes
  workspace files, keeping revision 3's refusal as the tripwire and the routing order as it is, and replacing the target with a
  bounded, recovered refusal. The ruling followed A on the wording: the text the coordinator followed was `delegate`'s own
  sentence, and A's wording names no persona and makes the persona the condition of the file work, so a habitual scope on a
  non-writer still trips revision 3 rather than teaching the model to drop the scope.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended confirming the tool, the refusal and the table as built and amending the record:
  the refusal counts as the enforced bound doing its job, OQ-216's target becomes a bound, the falsified target is kept, and the
  harness reports the seconds to re-route. The ruling took B's bound, the harness's seconds to re-route, revision 8's first
  execution recorded in place, and B's reopening limb for a non-writer briefed to write without a scope — the one risk A's change
  adds.

**Reopening condition:** more than one `write_scope` refusal for a non-writer in a duress run; a refusal whose work is not
re-routed by the coordinator's next `delegate`; a non-writer child briefed to write a file, with or without a scope (its report
says it cannot write); or at once if any enforced bound OQ-250 lists breaks. **Costs kept on record:** still advice; about 40
tokens more on every delegating request; a model that leaves out the scope but still briefs a non-writer to write is caught only
by the reopening limb.

**What a live run then shows.** Every delegating request's `delegate` description carries the new sentence and the offered schema
gives `write_scope` its description. In the duress run a design or decision document goes to a docs-writer, directly or with the
architect's answer handed on, and the scope is given to the writer; at most one write-scope refusal for a non-writer, refused
before any record and re-routed by the coordinator's next request, the harness NOTE printing the seconds to re-route; 0 briefs
offering a command or tool the target lacks, and no non-writer child reporting it was asked to write a file. The default run is
unchanged apart from the tokens.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin38, `fin38-edits-handoff-classifier`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-006` revision 9.*
`WRITE_SCOPE_SENTENCE` and `WRITE_SCOPE_FIELD_SENTENCE` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/delegation.ts`); the live run reads the bound
with the seconds to re-route (`routingMissReading`'s `rerouted`, `secondsToNext` and `flagged`, `apps/desktop/scripts/lib/routing-misses.mjs`).
Pinned by `tools/delegation.test.ts` and `lib/routing-misses.test.ts`, red on the code before. The note is repaired.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the live packs at `552d346` (default and duress) and `0bc3eee`:** at `0bc3eee` the new
sentence and the field's description were in 94 of 94 `delegate` offers, 8 write scopes went to writers only, and 0 were refused
for a non-writer. The default run is unchanged but for the tokens, as foreseen; the duress bound is still owed. Evidence:
[`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

<a id="oq-258"></a>

**OQ-258 — Does the intent classifier's strict rung name the classification object's fields?** *(REQ-ORCH-010, the three-rung
ladder, rung 2's keys and example fixed and rung 1's wording open; REQ-ORCH-007 and REQ-ORCH-008, the fallback and the 12 s
bound, kept by OQ-114's ruling under R-071; REQ-ORCH-011, the result's fields; ADR-0026's third execution, "the schema
was meant to be the instruction"; `PD-ORCH-011` revision 2. Raised 2026-10-13 from finding V3 of the duress live-run autopsy and
finding Q2 of the default autopsy at `552d346`, recorded in
[`the-intent-classifiers-strict-rung-never-names-the-objects-keys`](../defects/fixed/the-intent-classifiers-strict-rung-never-names-the-objects-keys.md);
the consortium's question V3. **Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

Every classifier request went out at `json_schema` with user text ending "Reply with the classification object only.", naming no
key, because the schema was to carry them; a reasoning model never sees `response_format` while it reasons. The duress
classification chose `whole_project` early, deliberated over the key from character 1,464 and was cut at 11,975 ms mid-way
through `{"classification":"whole_project"}`; the default pack was cut in 4 of 10 launches, three of them deliberating the same way
(the fourth received no bytes: the endpoint queueing), and faults-args lost its direct-work route.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** the intent classifier's `json_schema`
rung names the classification object's three fields in its user text, in the same sentence the `json_object` rung carries and
without that rung's example. The `json_object` rung keeps its example; the text rung, the system prompt and the 12 s bound
(REQ-ORCH-008, OQ-114 as ruled under R-071) are unchanged. It is covered work under REQ-ORCH-010, REQ-ORCH-007, REQ-ORCH-008 and
REQ-ORCH-011, which leaves rung 1's wording open: **no directive**, no specification text and no symbol changes. ADR-0026's
reading "the schema was meant to be the instruction" is kept beside its replacement as falsified.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both** — they recommended the same repair (one keys sentence on rung
1, no example there, the bound kept):
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended naming the fields on rung 1, leaving the bound alone, reporting `PD-ORCH-011`
  revision 2's first execution in place as a NOTE, and keeping the falsified reason beside its replacement. The ruling took A's
  dated paragraph on the earlier fixed note and the reopening limb "cut after naming its category".
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same change as covered work under REQ-ORCH-010, the same sentence without
  the example and nothing else, with the gap recorded as a defect against ADR-0026's correction and reported back to every record
  that decided it. The ruling took B's shared constant, the ADR-0026 report-back, the `codebase.md` line and the count limb.

**Rejected:** a longer bound (the owner kept it on 2026-10-06, and terminal's queueing would make a longer wait pure loss);
confirming as built. **Reopening condition (OQ-114's intent-bound limb):** a default pack after this change that shows a
classification cut after its reasoning has named its category, with no deliberation about field names; or 3 or more cuts in 10
launches where the endpoint was not queueing (bytes were received before the cut).

**What a live run then shows.** Every `json_schema` classifier request's user text ends with the keys sentence naming `intent`,
`confidence` and `reason`, and the reasoning no longer debates `category`, `classification` or `intent` as the key. Cuts at the
12 s bound fall toward `a68f121`'s 2 of 10 and come only from category deliberation or a queueing endpoint; duress classifies
`whole_project` in time; faults-args classifies `single_file_change` and runs direct (about 43 s, against 169 s); launch audits
read `fallback: true` less often.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin38, `fin38-edits-handoff-classifier`); its first execution is reported in ADR-0026's third execution, in
place, and in `PD-ORCH-011` revision 2's first live execution.* `KEYS_INSTRUCTION`, `SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION` and
`JSON_OBJECT_INSTRUCTION` (`packages/engine/src/intent/classifier.ts`); pinned by `intent.test.ts`'s OQ-258 case, red on the code
before. The note is repaired.

**Reported back 2026-10-13 (fin41), from the default pack at `0bc3eee`, "the next default pack":** the reopening
condition is **not met** on either limb. Every `json_schema` request (10 of 10) ended with the keys sentence naming `intent`,
`confidence` and `reason`; no reasoning debated `category`, `classification` or `intent` as the key; 9 of 10 launches
classified in 2.3 to 9.8 s, against 6 of 10 at `552d346`. The one cut, requirements at 11,973 ms, came after 91 kB of stream
while the reasoning was still weighing `small_feature`, `moderate_feature` and `single_file_change`: category deliberation, not
a category named and then lost, and 1 cut in 10, not 3. faults-args did run direct (46.1 s, against 169.1 s), but as
`explicit_trivial` 0.78 rather than the `single_file_change` foreseen above; terminal (`explicit_trivial` 0.92) ran its shapes
itself in 183.5 s against 338.8 s. Duress was not run at this head, so "duress classifies `whole_project` in time" is still
unmeasured. Evidence: [`live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md`](live-runs/live-0bc3eee-default-autopsy.md). The row is in [`first-executions.md`](first-executions.md).

<a id="oq-259"></a>

**OQ-259 — Does a `write_file` insert into a CRLF file carry the file's line endings into the inserted lines?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-135, `insert` and its success; `PD-TOOLS-016` and `PD-TOOLS-017`, which keep a CRLF file's line endings for every
`edit`; `PD-STARTUP-001`, Windows the only platform shipped. Raised 2026-10-13 by fin38 from the R-072 consortium's ruling of
[OQ-254](#oq-254), which confirmed the case in the code and asked that it be recorded as its own note and question.
**Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

`write_file`'s `insert` joins the file's lines and the content's lines with `\n`. The file's lines keep their `\r` and the
inserted ones have none unless the caller sent it: `a\r\nb\r\n` with `content` `X` at `insert_line` 1 leaves `a\r\nX\nb\r\n`,
beside "Inserted 1 line into … at line 1.". Recorded as
[`a-write-file-insert-writes-lf-lines-into-a-crlf-file`](../defects/fixed/a-write-file-insert-writes-lf-lines-into-a-crlf-file.md).
No requirement's text is contradicted: REQ-TOOLS-135 names `insert_line` and its bounds and says nothing of line endings.

**What the build proceeds under.** The inserted lines written as given.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether an insert into a CRLF file (by `PD-TOOLS-016` clause 2's test, read on the lines around the
insertion point or the file's other lines) gives each inserted line the file's `\r`, with `PD-TOOLS-017`'s success sentence
(extending REQ-TOOLS-135), or stands as built, `overwrite`'s and `insert`'s bytes being the caller's.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a `write_file` insert of non-empty
`content` into a CRLF file gives every line break it writes the file's `\r` — the break after each inserted line that a break
follows, and the break added after a previously unterminated last line — never doubling one and changing no byte of the file's
existing lines. The test is `PD-TOOLS-016` clause 2's, read on the file's line before the insertion point and the line at it
(the file's other lines when neither is followed by a line break; an empty file is not CRLF), and the success then adds
`content was written with the file's CRLF line endings.`. Minted as a new directive,
[`PD-TOOLS-018`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-018), extending REQ-TOOLS-135 and naming `PD-TOOLS-016` and `PD-TOOLS-017`;
`PD-TOOLS-017` is not revised, its case being `operation: edit` and its no-op and `content_hash:` clauses edit-only. An insert
with empty `content` writes nothing new and stays outside the case.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both** — they recommended the same change and differed only on the
vehicle:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended giving every line break an insert writes the file's `\r` with `PD-TOOLS-017`'s test,
  write rule and success sentence, recorded as revision 1 of `PD-TOOLS-017` with an insert clause, so that one directive holds "line
  endings belong to the file" for every incremental write. The ruling took A's edge cases, the unterminated end above all
  (`a\r\nb` + `X\n` at 2 → `a\r\nb\r\nX\r\n`), and its reading that no refusal is needed.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same behaviour as a new directive, `PD-TOOLS-018`, since `docs/product/README.md`
  keeps a revision for a change to a directive's own case and `PD-TOOLS-017`'s is `edit` alone; and added that LF lines an insert
  leaves behind later fail `PD-TOOLS-016`'s test, so the 016/017 guarantees decay wherever an insert has been. The ruling took B's
  vehicle and that reason; A's point that one directive is easier to find is met by `PD-TOOLS-018` naming both and by its
  back-pointer at REQ-TOOLS-135.

**Costs kept on record:** an insert can no longer write LF lines into a CRLF file (`overwrite` and `create` still write the
caller's bytes); the test is local, so a mixed neighbourhood is written as given and existing drift is not repaired; an
implementation built from the specification alone writes `content` as given.

**What a live run then shows.** Nothing in the current live-run fixtures, which are LF files on Linux; an LF insert is unchanged.
On Windows, an agent's insert into a CRLF file leaves the file uniformly CRLF, and the success adds "content was written with the
file's CRLF line endings.".

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin39, `fin39-insert-noop-optionals`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-018`, in place.*
`carryInsert` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`); pinned by the "PD-TOOLS-018" cases in `tools.test.ts`, red on the code
before. The note is repaired.

<a id="oq-260"></a>

**OQ-260 — Is a window edit whose carried replacement leaves the file unchanged refused, or applied as a success?**
*(REQ-TOOLS-135, `edit`'s "identical strings rejected"; `PD-TOOLS-016`, which carries a window match's line endings and, at
level 2, the bytes of every line `new_string` repeats; `PD-TOOLS-017` clause 3, which refuses an exact or replace-all edit left
with the file's own bytes. Raised 2026-10-13 by fin38 from the probe the R-072 consortium's ruling of [OQ-254](#oq-254) asked
for. **Ruled 2026-10-13.**)*

A window edit can land on the window's own bytes once `PD-TOOLS-016` has carried it: `one\r\ntwo\r\nthree\r\n` edited `one
\ntwo` → `one\ntwo` matches at level 2, pairs `two` with the file's `two\r` and gives `one` the window's `\r`, so the file is
rewritten unchanged beside `Edited n.txt: 2 lines replaced by 2 at line 1 (+0 -0). Match level: 2. new_string was written with
the file's CRLF line endings.`, with an undo entry that restores the same content. Recorded as
[`a-window-edit-that-lands-on-the-files-own-bytes-is-applied-as-a-success`](../defects/fixed/a-window-edit-that-lands-on-the-files-own-bytes-is-applied-as-a-success.md).
The strings differ, so REQ-TOOLS-135's rejection of identical strings does not reach it, and `PD-TOOLS-016` does not decide it.

**What the build proceeds under.** Applied as a success, as built.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a window edit whose result equals the file is refused before writing, with no undo entry and a
reply saying the file already holds that text (extending `PD-TOOLS-016` as `PD-TOOLS-017` clause 3 extends the exact edit), or
stands as built.

**Ruled 2026-10-13 under the owner's delegation ([R-072](../product/requests.md#r-072)):** a `write_file` edit that matches one
window at REQ-TOOLS-136 level 2, 3 or 4, and whose carried result equals the file's bytes, fails before writing: no undo entry is
pushed, the read record does not change, and the reply is `old_string matches <p> only at match level <N> (lines <a>-<b>), and
those lines already hold new_string as this edit would write it; nothing to change. Use write_file's 'overwrite' to write a file
exactly as given.` (`(line <a>)` for a one-line window). Published as [`PD-TOOLS-016`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-016)
revision 3, clause 4 "No-op, at levels 2, 3 and 4", which mirrors `PD-TOOLS-017` clause 3 for the window path; the PD-TOOLS-016
back-pointer under REQ-TOOLS-135 is amended in place. The reply differs from `PD-TOOLS-017`'s "differ only in line endings",
since at levels 2 to 4 the difference may be trailing whitespace, indentation or a fuzzy near miss. `haet_edit` is unchanged: its
levels 2 and 3 already refuse (`PD-TOOLS-014`), a level-4 match replies as a miss, and level 1 is `PD-TOOLS-017`'s.

The two recommendations weighed, and the ruling followed **both** — they agreed on the outcome, the vehicle and the cost:
- **Advocate A (the user's lens)** recommended refusing the no-op as revision 3 of `PD-TOOLS-016`, showing the success false three
  times over (nothing replaced, no CRLF written, the caller's intended fix never needed) and the live-run precedent in which a
  model said a no-op "should have errored but didn't", and an undo entry that pushes a real one out of REQ-TOOLS-132's ten. The
  ruling took A's argument from the user's view and its LF level-2 case.
- **Advocate B (the system's lens)** recommended the same refusal as a clause within `PD-TOOLS-016`'s own case, since every other
  edit path refuses its no-op and `docs/product/README.md` makes a change to a directive's own case a revision. The ruling took
  B's reply text ("already hold new_string as this edit would write it"), which stays true at levels 3 and 4, and B's level-4
  retry case; the overwrite hint is made general.

**Costs kept on record:** a refusal is one more failed tool call, so its text says plainly there is nothing to change; a caller
that relied on a no-op success to touch a file loses it (`overwrite` remains); an implementation built from the specification
alone applies the no-op.

**What a live run then shows.** Nothing: the live-run fixtures are LF files on Linux, and none of the six autopsies records a
window edit that lands on the file's own bytes. If one occurs, the transcript shows a refused `write_file` call naming the match
level and lines in place of a "+0 -0" write row.

*Built 2026-10-13 (fin39, `fin39-insert-noop-optionals`); its first execution is reported in `PD-TOOLS-016` revision 3, in
place.* `windowNoOpMessage` and the edit branch's comparison before `commit` (`packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`); pinned by
the "PD-TOOLS-016 revision 3" cases in `tools.test.ts`, red on the code before. The note is repaired.

<a id="oq-261"></a>

**OQ-261 — Which moments does REQ-STARTUP-160's setup statement name, when the build fetches at a tool's first start
rather than at machine setup or cache warm-up?** *(REQ-STARTUP-160 with REQ-STARTUP-058, REQ-STARTUP-064 and
REQ-STARTUP-084; `PD-STARTUP-005`; OQ-73, deferred, which records that machine setup is not built. Raised
2026-10-13 by fin41, building the disclosure the note
[`the-about-page-carries-no-network-activity-disclosure`](../defects/fixed/the-about-page-carries-no-network-activity-disclosure.md)
records. Open.)*

REQ-STARTUP-160 has About & Legal state "that first-launch machine setup and cache warm-up may contact the pinned
tool-archive hosts and the package registries the configured package runners use, and only for work the machine does not
already satisfy". It also requires the disclosure to name "no host, endpoint, or request this document does not require",
and calls a build "whose disclosure and behavior disagree" non-conformant on the disclosure. This build meets the clause
from the other side:

- **Neither moment exists in this build.** Machine setup (REQ-STARTUP-058's first list, REQ-STARTUP-060 onward, the tool
  archives of REQ-STARTUP-084) and the MCP cache warm-up of REQ-STARTUP-064 are not built (OQ-73, deferred by R-071). The
  build downloads no Git and no ripgrep archive, and it warms no cache.
- **The same kind of request happens at another moment.** The package runner fetches a pinned tool-server package
  (`@playwright/mcp` 0.0.80) from its registry the first time that tool server starts (`PD-STARTUP-005` says so of the
  notices file). The bundled code-intelligence runtime provisions a language server from the npm registry or PyPI at the
  first use of a language (REQ-STARTUP-058's second list, ESC-32). Both are requests this document requires, and both are
  made only for work the machine has not already done.

**What the build proceeds under.** The disclosure states the clause as the requirement words it, "may contact", and
names the third moment beside the two: "Setting up this machine's tools, on first launch, while warming caches, or the
first time a tool is needed, may contact …". It names no host. Without the third moment the disclosure would be silent
on the only requests of this kind the build makes; with the first two the text keeps the requirement's statement, which
a build that ships machine setup makes true without a change.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether "the first time a tool is needed" may stand beside the requirement's two moments
(extending REQ-STARTUP-160), whether a build that does not carry machine setup or warm-up must leave those two moments out
of its disclosure, or whether both stand as built.

<a id="oq-271"></a>

**OQ-271 — Is a retrospective's artifact part of a later run's analysis history?** *(REQ-LIBRARY-034, the analyst's prior
artifacts — `task_run` artifacts other than the session's own, the five newest; REQ-LIBRARY-025, `considered_session_ids`
records the source session of each; REQ-LIBRARY-017, "Data from another run, another session, or another workspace MUST NOT
inform it", beside "the bounded prior-artifact history of REQ-LIBRARY-034"; [`PD-LIBRARY-002`](../product/directives.md#pd-library-002)
revision 2 (a), a retrospective artifact stores `source_session_id` null and names the sessions it read. Raised 2026-10-13 by
fin42 from [`a-post-run-analysis-after-a-retrospective-is-never-captured.md`](../defects/fixed/a-post-run-analysis-after-a-retrospective-is-never-captured.md).)*

A retrospective's artifact carries `source_run_type` `task_run` and no source session, so REQ-LIBRARY-034's filter, read by its
letter, keeps it among a later run's five prior artifacts, and REQ-LIBRARY-025 has no session of it to record. Until fin42 the
null reached the job and its parse threw, so no run's analysis was captured while a retrospective artifact stood among the five
newest. The specification was written before the retrospective existed, and PD-LIBRARY-002 revision 2 names REQ-LIBRARY-011,
-020, -109, -124, -125 and -130 and REQ-NOTIFY-250, not REQ-LIBRARY-025 or -034.

**What the build proceeds under.** The letter of REQ-LIBRARY-034: a retrospective's artifact stays in a later run's history,
bounded like any prior artifact, and contributes no session to `considered_session_ids`, since it has none
(`captureImprovementJob`, `packages/engine/src/improvements/capture.ts`). Its proposals then reach the per-run analyst as history,
and REQ-LIBRARY-046's duplicate suppression already reads them.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a retrospective's artifact belongs to the per-run analyst's history — as built, by the letter of
REQ-LIBRARY-034, or excluded, since its content is drawn from other sessions and REQ-LIBRARY-017 keeps another session's data
from informing a run's analysis — and, if it stays, whether `considered_session_ids` should carry the sessions the retrospective
itself read. **The costs either way:** kept, a run's analyst reads proposals written over sessions it was never shown, and only
their summaries; excluded, a run's analyst may propose again what a retrospective already proposed, which REQ-LIBRARY-046's
suppression at store time still catches.

<a id="oq-262"></a>

**OQ-262 — Which notice offers REQ-NOTIFY-044's project-initialization action, and what does the action open for a
workspace this window does not hold?** *(REQ-NOTIFY-044, the action vocabulary; REQ-NOTIFY-047, actions write nothing into
the project; REQ-SHELL-115, "start project initialization; resolve project initialization"; REQ-CONFIG-404; ADR-0064, the
initialization registry and its surface. Raised 2026-10-13 by fin41 while correcting the stale comment on the renderer's
notice-action switch, recorded in
[`code-comments-call-built-mechanisms-unbuilt-or-owed`](../defects/fixed/code-comments-call-built-mechanisms-unbuilt-or-owed.md).
Open.)*

REQ-NOTIFY-044 lists "open the project-initialization surface for a named workspace" among the actions a notice may carry,
and the contract carries it (`open-project-init`, with a `workspace`, `packages/contracts/src/notices.ts`). The renderer's
arm (`apps/desktop/src/renderer/main.tsx`, `dispatchNoticeAction`) dispatches nothing and logs that the action "has no target in
this build". Its comment gave the reason as "no project-initialization surface". That reason is false since ADR-0064:
Settings › Project draws the initialization tasks and their outcomes (`packages/ui/src/settings/ProjectSettings.tsx`,
`project-init.ts`). Nothing in the build raises the action either: no notice offers it, so the arm cannot be reached.

The specification leaves two things open:

- **Which notice carries it.** REQ-NOTIFY-044 fixes the vocabulary, not which notice offers which member. The
  initialization banners (PD-WORKSPACE-005) offer no action today. REQ-WORKSPACE-103 puts the recorded outcome in
  Settings › Project, which a banner could lead to with this action or with the existing "open settings at a named
  category". Nothing says whether a banner should offer it at all.
- **What it opens for another workspace.** The action names a workspace. Settings › Project shows the window's own
  workspace. A notice is an application notice shown in every open window (ADR-0049, PD-WORKSPACE-005), so another window
  may hold a different workspace. The specification does not say whether the action focuses the window that holds the
  named workspace, opens Settings › Project in the window it was activated in only when the workspace matches, or is not
  dispatched otherwise (REQ-NOTIFY-044's "an action naming a value outside the owning domain's vocabulary is not
  dispatched" covers vocabularies, not windows).

**What the build proceeds under.** Unchanged: the arm logs and dispatches nothing, and no notice raises the action. Only
the comment changed, to say that the surface exists and that nothing raises the action.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether any notice offers the action, and, if one does, which surface it opens in which
window.

**What a live run then shows.** Nothing until a ruling adds a notice that carries the action: no live scenario raises one.

<a id="oq-263"></a>

**OQ-263 — Is a `worktree_storage_subpath` that contains the requirement checkout directory rejected at load?**
*(REQ-GIT-138, whose first sentence keeps the worktree directories of the three namespaces disjoint, "no worktree directory of one
namespace SHALL lie inside the directory of another", and whose directory-side rejection names only a value that "resolves to the
fixed requirement checkout directory of REQ-GIT-137 or to any directory inside it"; REQ-GIT-005, REQ-GIT-073, REQ-CONFIG-068.
Raised 2026-10-13 by fin41 while building the load-time half of REQ-GIT-138, task N72, as OQ-261; renumbered OQ-263 at
landing, because origin/main had given OQ-261 to REQ-STARTUP-160's question and OQ-262 to REQ-NOTIFY-044's first.)*

**What is open.** A session worktree lies at `<workspace>/.rotaris/<subpath>/<session-id>`. A `worktree_storage_subpath` of
`requirements` or `.` names a session directory (`.rotaris/requirements/`, `.rotaris/`) that CONTAINS the requirement checkout
directory `.rotaris/requirements/worktrees/`. No session tree ever lands in that directory, since a session id is never
`worktrees`, but the requirement directory then lies inside the session one, which the first sentence of REQ-GIT-138 forbids. The
rejection the requirement states names only the two cases the other way round: the fixed directory itself, and a directory inside
it. The two sentences read differently over `requirements` and `.`, and the specification does not say which governs.

**What the build proceeds under.** The rejection as stated: only a value that resolves to `.rotaris/requirements/worktrees` or
inside it fails the load (`worktreeStorageCollision`, `packages/config/src/sections/requirements.ts`); `requirements` and `.`
load, and a session tree is placed at `.rotaris/requirements/<sid>` or `.rotaris/<sid>`. The cases are pinned as loading in
`load.test.ts` and `requirements-section.test.ts`, so a ruling the other way turns them red.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether a value whose session directory contains the requirement checkout directory is rejected at load
too, on REQ-GIT-071's terms, with the same report (key, value, the namespace it collided with), or loads as built.

**What a live run then shows.** Nothing: the live-run workspaces keep the default `worktrees`.

<a id="oq-264"></a>
**OQ-264 — Where in Settings does REQ-CHAT-167's reasoning-visibility switch live, when REQ-CONFIG-403 says the
Display category "holds two transcript toggles"?** *(REQ-CHAT-167 with REQ-CONFIG-403 and REQ-CONFIG-472. Raised
2026-10-13 by fin41, building the repair the note
[`search-transcript-and-the-reasoning-toggle-are-withheld-for-reasons-no-longer-true`](../defects/fixed/search-transcript-and-the-reasoning-toggle-are-withheld-for-reasons-no-longer-true.md)
records, as OQ-263; renumbered OQ-264 at landing, because origin/main had given OQ-263 to
REQ-GIT-138's question. Open.)*

REQ-CHAT-167 requires `display/showReasoning` to be "reachable both from the settings surface and from the command
palette". It names no category. REQ-CONFIG-403 says "The Display category holds two transcript toggles", names them —
auto-collapse older tool outputs and group consecutive tool calls — and fixes their order; REQ-CONFIG-472 says the
category "additionally holds" REQ-CHAT-166's four tool-row controls. No settings requirement names the reasoning switch,
so read together the two documents either count the Display category short by one or leave the switch with no
category at all.

**What the build proceeds under.** The switch, "Show reasoning bodies", is the third control under Display's
Transcript heading, after REQ-CONFIG-403's two in their order, with the same commit policy (a desktop preference written
the moment it moves, not undone by Discard). The heading's sentence now says "These three". That is where a reader
looking for a transcript display preference looks, and it keeps REQ-CONFIG-403's two in their stated order.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether REQ-CONFIG-403's "two" is an enumeration a third preference may join (extending it
by a directive), or whether the switch belongs in another category (Interface holds the other desktop-preference
toggles), or whether it stands as built.

<a id="oq-272"></a>

**OQ-272 — Is a person's edit inside an artifact document's frontmatter kept, or rewritten away at the next re-render?**
*(PD-LIBRARY-003 (d) and (f), REQ-LIBRARY-133, REQ-LIBRARY-095, REQ-LIBRARY-092; REQ-SESSION-115. Raised 2026-10-13 by fin42
(`fin42-live-gaps`), found by building `artifacts-proof` launches 8 and 9 (item N57). Minted on its branch as OQ-271 and
renumbered OQ-272 at its landing, `origin/main` having taken OQ-271 meanwhile.)*

The inspector's Markdown tab shows and edits the whole document, its leading frontmatter included (PD-LIBRARY-003 (f)), and a
re-render of an edited document rewrites that block from the record and keeps what follows it (clause (d)). So a person's edit
typed inside the frontmatter is saved, `edited_at` is stamped and the table shows ` · edited`, and the next supersession or
re-materialisation removes it without a word. Measured on the built app: launch 8's first build clicked the editor at its centre,
which lies inside the frontmatter, and typed there; the save read "Saved.", the document held the text, and after launch 9's
superseding publish the document's frontmatter was rewritten and the text was gone, while the continued run's handoff still
named the artifact `(… , edited)` and carried no edit. The directive's costs name a deleted frontmatter coming back; an edit
inside it, and a record that keeps saying `edited` once nothing edited remains, are not named.

**What the build proceeds under.** As built: the frontmatter is the record's, and an edit inside it lasts until the next
re-render. The proofs now move the caret below the frontmatter before typing (`Ctrl+End`), and the live run's `delegation-edit`
launch does the same.

**What a ruling decides.** One of: the Markdown tab keeps the frontmatter out of the person's reach (shown read-only, or not
shown), as the Preview already does (clause (f)); the tab says, when a save changes the block, that frontmatter edits are not
kept; a re-render keeps a person's changed values; or the cost stands as built and is added to PD-LIBRARY-003's list.

<a id="oq-280"></a>

**OQ-280 — Does match level 3 compare a line without its carriage return?** *(REQ-TOOLS-136, the four match levels — level 2
"each line equal once trailing whitespace is ignored", level 3 "each line equal once one uniform leading prefix is added or
removed"; REQ-TOOLS-189, `haet_edit`'s exact match; [`PD-TOOLS-014`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-014)'s near miss at
levels 2 and 3, [`PD-TOOLS-015`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-015)'s level-3 shift, and
[`PD-TOOLS-016`](../product/directives.md#pd-tools-016), each stating that REQ-TOOLS-136's levels are unchanged. Raised
2026-10-13 by fin42 (N52) from
[`on-a-crlf-file-an-lf-old-string-one-indent-off-skips-match-level-3.md`](../defects/on-a-crlf-file-an-lf-old-string-one-indent-off-skips-match-level-3.md);
numbered from the top of the plan's range, OQ-271 to OQ-280, to keep clear of its sibling bundles.)*

On a CRLF file every line ends in `\r`, and an `old_string` a model writes as a JSON string almost never carries one. Level 2
strips trailing whitespace, the `\r` with it, so an LF `old_string` matches a CRLF file there (`PD-TOOLS-016` was ruled for
exactly that). Level 3 as built (`matchEdit`, `packages/agent-tools/src/tools/files.ts`) compares each window line with the
shifted `old_string` line exactly, so the `\r` keeps an LF `old_string` one indent off from level 3 on a CRLF file. Measured
in the built app (`pnpm edits-proof`, `shift-lf`) and with the tools directly, the same three-line block one tab shallow:
on an LF file, `write_file` applies at level 3 with `PD-TOOLS-015`'s shift and `haet_edit` gives `PD-TOOLS-014`'s near miss with
the quote; on a CRLF file, `write_file` applies at "Match level: 4 (similarity: 0.91). Verify the result." and writes the block
**one tab too shallow beside a success**, and `haet_edit` gives the plain "not found exactly" with no quote. A shorter window
scores under 0.85 and reads "not found at any of the four match levels". Windows is the only platform shipped
(`PD-STARTUP-001`), where CRLF files are ordinary; the guarantee `PD-TOOLS-015` was ruled for (OQ-233: a mis-indented block
never lands beside a success) holds there only for an `old_string` that carries the file's `\r`s.

**What the build proceeds under.** The letter of REQ-TOOLS-136 as built: level 3 compares lines exactly, `\r` included; on a
CRLF file an LF `old_string` one indent off reaches level 4 or no match. Nothing was changed; `edits-proof` records the reading
and asserts neither way.

**What a ruling decides.** Whether level 3's "each line equal" reads a line without its line ending (the `\r` of a CRLF line
being part of its ending, not its text) — so that an LF `old_string` one indent off matches a CRLF file at level 3 and
`PD-TOOLS-015` (shift, as given, or refusal) and `PD-TOOLS-014` (the near miss and quote) answer it, with `PD-TOOLS-016` clause 2
carrying the endings as it already does at level 3 — or whether the build's exact reading stands. **The costs either way:**
read without the `\r`, level 3 takes cases level 4 took, so an edit that applied at level 4 is shifted or refused instead, and
the near-miss quote of such a window carries `\r`s the caller must send back; kept exact, on Windows a model's commonest
mis-indented edit lands unshifted beside a success at level 4 — the case `PD-TOOLS-015` was ruled to prevent — and `haet_edit`
gives no near miss for it.

<a id="oq-272"></a>

**OQ-272 — When the pinned runtime's symbol rename answers before its language server has loaded the project, does the product
warm it, change the runtime, or tell the model?** *(REQ-MCP-015, the EDIT tier's symbol rename; REQ-MCP-011 and ADR-0035, the
pinned runtime the product bundles and drives as it is; REQ-MCP-116, the binding manifest, the one place the runtime's
identifiers are written; [OQ-245](#oq-245), the reach observation that records what the call changed. Raised 2026-10-13 by
fin42 (N59) from
[`a-symbol-rename-that-is-the-servers-first-cross-file-request-renames-the-declaring-file-alone`](../defects/a-symbol-rename-that-is-the-servers-first-cross-file-request-renames-the-declaring-file-alone.md).
Open. fin42 held OQ-271 to OQ-280; OQ-271 was taken on main by another of the plan's bundles, so this is the next free number.)*

The first rename of a server session that needs the language server's cross-file view renames the declaring file alone and says
it succeeded: `code-intel-proof`'s eleventh launch (`child-rename-cold`) and four arrangements over the runtime's stdio branch,
a copy of the live run's `todo-app` fixture among them, all changed one file. The same rename after one referencing-symbol search
of the symbol reaches every file (launch 10, `child-rename`). The pinned runtime (`serena-agent` 1.7.0) waits for the TypeScript
server's project loading before a references request and not before a rename, so the server answers the rename before it has
loaded the other files. The run host's record of the call is true; the tool's success is not, and the model is not told.

**What the build proceeds under.** As built: the call is forwarded as the model made it, the result is the runtime's, and the
reach observation lists the one file it changed. A model that searched for references first, as many do, renames correctly.

**What a ruling decides.** Which of these, or none:

- **(a) A product-side warm-up.** The MCP executor (`apps/desktop/src/run-host/mcp.ts`) sends the runtime's referencing-symbol
  search for the same `name_path` and `relative_path` before the first rename of each server session, discards its answer and
  then forwards the rename. Costs: one extra server request the model did not make, the search's name written into the manifest
  as a new capability of the binding (REQ-MCP-116), and a dependency on the runtime's internals that a later pin may change.
- **(b) A runtime-side repair.** The bundle recipe patches the pinned distribution's rename to take the references path's wait,
  or the pin moves to a version that does. Costs: a patched third-party tree the recipe must carry and the drift check must know
  of (ADR-0035, ADR-0054), or an upgrade measured like any pin change.
- **(c) Tell the model.** The rename's description in the manifest (as `PD-MCP-001` describes the usage-instruction tool) says to
  search for references first, or the run host appends to a rename result whose reach observation lists one file that the files
  referencing the symbol may not have been renamed. Costs: advice a model may ignore; the second needs a reading of "one file"
  that a single-file symbol would trip.
- **(d) Nothing.** A rename made first in a session is the runtime's behaviour, and the record already lists what changed.

**What a live run then shows.** The opt-in `rename` scenario (`live-run.mjs --only=rename`) delegates a coding-agent to rename
`remaining` to `countRemaining` with `rename_symbol` and reads whether the agent searched for references before its first rename,
which of the three files still name `remaining` and which were written by another tool after the rename, and whether
`node --test` passes; a cold rename whose importing files were left behind, or were mended by hand afterwards, is a NOTE naming
this question.
